source.title: On Stevenhagen's conjecture
source.venue: Acta Mathematica, to appear (accepted; not yet assigned to a volume or issue as of 23 September 2026)
readSections: arXiv 2201.13424v1 (31 January 2022), the only public version, read in full: 110 pages, PDF SHA-256 c7a93ffea06491d824d900fe067f6768246e84555fa8da8282833caac7850cbd, TeX source SHA-256 d6c9d917f61876b9b3ff9f06e66a002132f90c2a518cf714f7c054141b3f8e12, fetched 23 September 2026. Item locators are v1 pages.

Venue, as the maintainer asked: the Acta volume and year are not yet established. Peter Koymans's publication page (https://webspace.science.uu.nl/~koyma001/publications.html, 23 September 2026) lists the paper as 'To Appear in Acta Mathematica'. Crossref records Acta Mathematica (ISSN 0001-5962, International Press, DOI prefix 10.4310/ACTA) through volume 236, no. 2 (2026) without it, and no Crossref record matches the title. zbMATH Open lists only the arXiv preprint. The International Press pages for Acta refused automated access (HTTP 403). So the published version, which may differ from v1, could not be read or compared.

Read: §1 (Theorem 1.1, the history and the outline), §2 (raw cocycles, expansion maps, Artin pairings), §3 (higher Rédei reciprocity, Theorem 3.2 and its proof), §4 (profitable triples), §5 (reflection principles for ∞, for the self-pairing, and the standard ones), §6 (additive systems, Ramsey theory, Galois groups), §7 (prime divisors, preboxes and Legendre symbols, boxes: equidistribution of the first Artin pairing), §8 (boxes, genericity, a second-moment computation, the end of the proof of Theorem 1.1) and the references. Three readers covered the paper with coverage tables mapping every numbered statement to an item; every recorded mistake was checked on the page images.

Cited inputs were not read; items resting on Smith [Smith] (arXiv 1702.02325) and [Smith8] (arXiv 1607.07860), Koymans–Pagano [KP1]–[KP4], Fouvry–Klüners [FK1]–[FK4], Friedlander–Iwaniec–Mazur–Rubin [FIMR], Koymans–Milovic [KM], Chan–Koymans–Milovic–Pagano [CKMP], Heath-Brown [HB], Rédei [Redei], [Redei8], Rédei–Reichardt [RR], Stevenhagen [Stevenhagen], [StevenhagenRedei], Gerth [Gerth], Heilbronn [Heilbronn], Iwaniec–Kowalski [IK], Montgomery–Vaughan [MoVa], MacWilliams [Williams] and Cohen–Lenstra [CL] state them as the paper uses them.

summary: Koymans and Pagano prove Stevenhagen's conjecture (Theorem 1.1): among squarefree d with 0 < d < X all of whose odd prime factors are ≡ 1 mod 4 (the family 𝒟 in which x² − dy² = −1 is locally soluble), the proportion for which the negative Pell equation is soluble tends to 1 − α, α = ∏_{j odd}(1 − 2^{−j}) ≈ 0.41942. Solubility means that (√d) is trivial in the narrow class group, which is decided by the Artin pairings on the 2-power torsion of the narrow class group of ℚ(√d). The proof adapts Smith's method for 2^∞-class groups. It sets up raw cocycles, expansion maps and higher Artin pairings (§2), and proves a higher Rédei reciprocity law generalizing quadratic and Rédei reciprocity (§3). Because the first Artin pairing is symmetric on 𝒟 and the relevant cubes are one dimension short, it builds new reflection principles through 'profitable triples', including one for the self-pairing whose right-hand side is a trivial spin symbol (§§4–5). With Smith's additive-system and Ramsey combinatorics (§6), effective Chebotarev with exceptional-zero control, and Heath-Brown's large sieve for Legendre symbols in boxes (§7), this yields the equidistribution of every higher pairing, and a Markov-chain and second-moment argument (§8) gives the limit. Nothing in the atlas plans Smith's method, so most of the paper is a proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics; the analytic, classical and statistical inputs are sources of existing layers. The Acta volume and year are not yet established.

items.name: The family 𝒟 and its truncation 𝒟(X)
items.statement: 𝒟 is the set of squarefree integers d > 0 such that every prime p ∣ d satisfies p ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4) (equivalently p = 2 or p ≡ 1 mod 4). For real X, 𝒟(X) := {d ∈ 𝒟 : d < X}.
items.locator: §1, running text before Theorem 1.1, p. 2 (arXiv v1)
items.note: The family is ordered by the radicand d. Footnote 1 says Stevenhagen orders real quadratic fields by discriminant, and that both the heuristic and the proofs work for both orderings; no comparison is written out. d = 1 ∈ 𝒟 vacuously. ST.0's acceptance, 'changing height changes the theorem until a comparison is proved', applies to that footnote. Route: a source of ArithmeticStatistics (ST.0 families, ST.3 class groups, ST.5 random-matrix distributions).

items.name: The negative-Pell set 𝒟⁻ and its truncation 𝒟⁻(X)
items.statement: 𝒟⁻ is the set of squarefree integers d for which the negative Pell equation x² − dy² = −1 (1.1) has a solution x, y ∈ ℤ. For real X, 𝒟⁻(X) := {d ∈ 𝒟⁻ : d < X}.
items.note: No sign condition is imposed, but d < 0 is impossible because x² + |d|y² ≥ 0. d = 1 ∈ 𝒟⁻ via (x, y) = (0, 1). By item 3, 𝒟⁻ ⊆ 𝒟. Mathlib's Pell.Solution₁ covers only x² − dy² = 1. Tau Ceti has NumberField.exists_norm_eq_neg_one_of_sq_sub_mul_sq_eq_neg_one (a solution gives a unit of norm −1). Route: a source of ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.4 (Pell equations).

items.name: Rational solubility of the negative Pell equation (Hasse–Minkowski)
items.statement: Let d > 0 be squarefree. Then x² − dy² = −1 has a solution x, y ∈ ℚ if and only if every prime p ∣ d satisfies p ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4). Consequently 𝒟⁻ ⊆ 𝒟.
items.note: Cited as a consequence of Hasse–Minkowski. Equivalently −1 is a norm from ℚ(√d), i.e. (−1, d)_v = 1 at every place, i.e. d is a sum of two rational squares. Mathlib's Nat.eq_sq_add_sq_iff (Mathlib/NumberTheory/SumTwoSquares.lean:211 at 082e2d3) gives the integral sum-of-two-squares criterion. The Hasse–Minkowski input is planned in GlobalQuadraticForms Layer 5; this corollary is not. Route: a source of ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.4 (Pell equations).

items.name: Dirichlet: primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 lie in 𝒟⁻
items.statement: Every prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) lies in 𝒟⁻, i.e. x² − py² = −1 has a solution in integers. In particular 𝒟⁻ is infinite.
items.note: Classical. The usual proof: the fundamental unit ε of ℤ[√p] has norm −1, because otherwise ε = u² or ε = pu² up to 2-power factors, which is impossible modulo p and 4. Not used later in the paper. Route: a source of ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.4 (Pell equations).

items.name: Negative Pell and the 2-parts of the narrow and ordinary class groups ([FK1, Lemma 1])
items.statement: Let d > 1 be squarefree. Then d ∈ 𝒟⁻ if and only if the 2-Sylow subgroup of the ordinary class group of ℚ(√d) coincides with the 2-Sylow subgroup of the narrow class group, i.e. the natural surjection Cl⁺(ℚ(√d))[2^∞] → Cl(ℚ(√d))[2^∞] is an isomorphism.
items.locator: §1, running text, p. 2, citing [18, Lemma 1] (arXiv v1)
items.note: Tau Ceti at f790474 has NumberField.NarrowClassGroup.toClassGroup_injective_iff_exists_norm_eq_neg_one (for 0 < d, Cl⁺(K) → Cl(K) is injective iff some unit of 𝒪_K has norm −1). The missing steps are two. First, a unit of 𝒪_K of norm −1 gives an integral solution; for d ≡ 5 mod 8 use ε³ ∈ ℤ[√d]. Second, the 2-Sylow form follows because the kernel of Cl⁺ → Cl has order at most 2. Route: a source of ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.4 (Pell equations).

items.name: Prior bounds towards Stevenhagen's conjecture (cited)
items.statement: Fouvry–Klüners [FK1]: α ≤ liminf_{X→∞} |𝒟⁻(X)|/|𝒟(X)| ≤ limsup_{X→∞} |𝒟⁻(X)|/|𝒟(X)| ≤ 2/3, with α as in item 7. Blomer: |𝒟⁻(X)| ≫ X/(log X)^{0.62}. Cremona–Odoni: when the number t ≥ 1 of prime divisors of d is fixed, the liminf of the proportion is at least some λ_t ≥ α.
items.note: Background only; none is used in the proof. The lower bound was improved in [FK2] and [CKMP], the upper bound in [KP3]. The printed '𝒟⁻(X) ≫' means |𝒟⁻(X)| ≫. The paper says Blomer's exponent is 0.12 away from the truth, consistent with |𝒟(X)| ≍ X/√(log X). Route: a source of ArithmeticStatistics (ST.0 families, ST.3 class groups, ST.5 random-matrix distributions).

items.name: Stevenhagen's density constant α
items.locator: §1, running text before Theorem 1.1, p. 2 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Checked here: numerically: α = 0.4194224…, 1 − α = 0.5805776…. Nagell conjectured that lim |𝒟⁻(X)|/|𝒟(X)| exists and lies in (0, 1). Stevenhagen, from a heuristic model, conjectured that it equals 1 − α (Stevenhagen's conjecture). Theorem 1.1 is that conjecture, and Nagell's follows since 0 < 1 − α < 1. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (Stevenhagen's conjecture)
items.statement: With 𝒟, 𝒟⁻, 𝒟(X), 𝒟⁻(X) as in items 1–2 and α = ∏_{j ≥ 1, j odd}(1 − 2^{−j}): lim_{X→∞} |𝒟⁻(X)|/|𝒟(X)| = 1 − α. That is, among squarefree d with 0 < d < X all of whose prime factors are 2 or ≡ 1 mod 4, the proportion for which x² − dy² = −1 is soluble in integers tends to 1 − α ≈ 0.58058.
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.1, p. 2; proved in §8 from Theorem 8.1 (arXiv v1)
items.note: This is the main theorem; §1 has no other numbered theorem. Proved in §8 ('Proof that Theorem 8.1 implies Theorem 1.1'). p. 3 adds that, as in [Smith, Corollary 7.2], Theorem 8.1 gives an explicit, effectively computable error term; the error term is not stated. Per footnote 1, the result also holds when fields are ordered by discriminant. Nothing in the atlas plans it: no stage mentions negative Pell densities, Stevenhagen or Smith's method. ST.3 plans only 'selected counting and class-group moment/distribution theorems' from BHARGAVA-SHANKAR and COHEN-LENSTRA. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Unit-group Galois-module reformulation
items.statement: For squarefree d > 1 with K = ℚ(√d) and Gal(K/ℚ) = ⟨σ⟩: d ∈ 𝒟⁻ if and only if the ℤ[Gal(K/ℚ)]-module 𝒪_K^× is isomorphic to ℤ ⊕ ℤ/2ℤ with σ(1, 0) = (−1, 1) and σ(0, 1) = (0, 1). Here (1, 0) is a fundamental unit ε, (0, 1) is −1, and σ(ε) = N(ε)ε^{−1}.
items.locator: §1, running text after Theorem 1.1, p. 3 (arXiv v1)
items.note: A remark, not used later. The alternative module has σ(1, 0) = (−1, 0), the case N(ε) = +1. It needs the same passage from 𝒪_K to ℤ[√d] as item 5. Route: a source of ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.4 (Pell equations).

items.name: Asymptotic for |𝒟(X)| (classical, cited)
items.statement: Classical analytic number theory gives an asymptotic formula for |𝒟(X)| as X → ∞ (of order X/√(log X)); hence Theorem 1.1 gives an asymptotic formula for |𝒟⁻(X)|.
items.note: The paper gives neither the constant nor a proof. The order X/√(log X) is implicit in the remark on Blomer's exponent. A Landau/Selberg–Delange mean-value theorem for the multiplicative indicator of 𝒟. Route: a source of AnalyticNumberTheory (AN.2 exceptional zeros and uniform prime number theorems, AN.4 effective Chebotarev and Dedekind zeta functions, AN.5 mean values of multiplicative functions).

items.name: Smith's theorem: Gerth's extension of Cohen–Lenstra ((1.2), cited)
items.statement: For every finite abelian 2-group A: lim_{X→∞} |{K imaginary quadratic : |D_K| ≤ X, 2Cl(K)[2^∞] ≅ A}| / |{K imaginary quadratic : |D_K| ≤ X}| = ∏_{i≥1}(1 − 2^{−i}) / |Aut(A)|, where D_K is the discriminant of K.
items.note: Printed (1.2) omits lim_{X→∞} (issues file); restored here. Cited background. [FK3, FK4] earlier found the distribution of 2Cl(K)[4], and the authors' [KP1] treats cyclic fields of odd prime degree under GRH. ST.3 plans unspecified 'selected ... class-group moment/distribution theorems'; Smith's theorem is not among them. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Negative Pell as narrow triviality of (√d)
items.statement: For squarefree d > 1 (in the paper d ∈ 𝒟): d ∈ 𝒟⁻ if and only if the ideal (√d) = Up_{ℚ(√d)/ℚ}(d) is trivial in the narrow class group Cl(ℚ(√d)).
items.note: This is why the Artin pairing against the class of (√d) must be computed, which (1.3) does not cover. Tau Ceti f790474 proves the 𝒪_K-unit form inside toClassGroup_injective_iff_exists_norm_eq_neg_one: the narrow class of (θ) is trivial iff a unit has norm −1. The ℤ[√d] passage is the same as item 5. Route: a source of ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.4 (Pell equations).

items.name: Smith's reflection principle, as sketched in (1.3) (informal, cited)
items.statement: Let C = {d_0} × {p_{1,1}, p_{1,2}} × ⋯ × {p_{k,1}, p_{k,2}}, with points read as squarefree integers by multiplying coordinates, and write ⟨b, χ_a⟩_{k,ℚ(√d)} for the k-th Artin pairing (§2.3) between χ_a (the character of ℚ(√a)) and the ideal of ℚ(√d) of norm b. For suitable divisors a, b of d_0: ∑_{d∈C} ⟨bπ_k(d), χ_a + χ_{π_1(d)}⟩_{k−1,ℚ(√d)} = Frob_{K/ℚ}(p_{k,1}) + Frob_{K/ℚ}(p_{k,2}), where K = K_{p_{1,1},p_{1,2},…,p_{k−1,1},p_{k−1,2}} is an explicit field and the Frobenius elements lie in Z(Gal(K/ℚ)) ≅ 𝔽₂.
items.note: An informal overview. The precise reflection principles are Theorems 4.6 and 5.x, outside this range. The indexing is off by one: with d_0 as the first factor, the paper's convention makes π_1(d) = d_0 (issues file). The intended reading is π_i(d) ∈ {p_{i,1}, p_{i,2}}. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Negative-Pell reflection principle at ∞ (informal)
items.statement: With C = {d_0} × {p_{1,1}, p_{1,2}} × ⋯ × {p_{k,1}, p_{k,2}} and the pairing ⟨−, −⟩_{k,ℚ(√d)} as in item 13, and a ∣ d_0: ∑_{d∈C} ⟨d, χ_a + χ_{π_1(d)}⟩_{k,ℚ(√d)} = Frob_{K_{p_{1,1},p_{1,2},…,p_{k,1},p_{k,2}}/ℚ}(∞). Equidistribution of the right side follows from the extended reciprocity law (Theorem 3.2) and Chebotarev.
items.note: Informal. The precise statements are the reflection principles for ∞ in §5.1, outside this range. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Symmetry of the first Artin pairing on 𝒟 (informal)
items.statement: For d ∈ 𝒟 the first Artin pairing ⟨−, −⟩_{Art_1(d)} of ℚ(√d) is symmetric. This uses the identification of Cl(ℚ(√d))[2] with the classes of Up(b), b ∣ d, and of Cl(ℚ(√d))^∨[2] with the genus characters χ_b, b ∣ d.
items.note: Stated as motivation: symmetry blocks Smith's method, which is why the self-pairing ⟨a, χ_a⟩_{k+1} and the spin-like symbol of Theorems 5.3 and 5.5 are needed. Classically this is the symmetry of the Rédei matrix, by quadratic reciprocity, since all odd p ∣ d are ≡ 1 mod 4. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: [n] and coordinate projections
items.statement: For n ∈ ℤ_{≥0}, [n] := {1, …, n}. For a product X = X_1 × ⋯ × X_r, π_i : X → X_i is the i-th projection. ⊆ denotes inclusion and ⊂ strict inclusion.
items.note: Pure notation. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Cubes Cube(X, S), projections π_T, pr_1, pr_2
items.statement: For X = X_1 × ⋯ × X_r and S ⊆ [r], Cube(X, S) := ∏_{i∈S} X_i² × ∏_{i∈[r]−S} X_i. For T ⊆ [r], π_T is the projection Cube(X, S) → ∏_{i∈T∩S} X_i² × ∏_{i∈T∩([r]−S)} X_i. pr_1, pr_2 : X_i² → X_i are the two projections.
items.note: The combinatorial cubes of Smith's method, used in §§4–6 and 8. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Faces x̄(T) of a cube point
items.statement: Let X = X_1 × ⋯ × X_r, S ⊆ [r], x̄ ∈ Cube(X, S) and T ⊆ S. Then x̄(T) is the set of ȳ ∈ Cube(X, T) with π_i(ȳ) ∈ {pr_1(π_i(x̄)), pr_2(π_i(x̄))} for all i ∈ S − T and π_{[r]−(S−T)}(x̄) = π_{[r]−(S−T)}(ȳ).
items.note: For T = ∅, x̄(∅) is the set of 2^{|S|} vertices of the cube x̄. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Absolute Galois group G_K
items.statement: For a field K, G_K denotes its absolute Galois group, a profinite group with the Krull topology.
items.note: Mathlib/FieldTheory/AbsoluteGaloisGroup.lean:43 at 082e2d3: def absoluteGaloisGroup := AlgebraicClosure K ≃ₐ[K] AlgebraicClosure K, with its Krull topology. The paper works inside a fixed ℚ^sep (item 27).

items.name: Places, completions, residue fields, odd places, K^unr, composita
items.statement: For a global field K, Ω_K is its set of places (finite and infinite). For v ∈ Ω_K, K_v is the completion and, for finite v, 𝔽_v is the residue field. A finite place is odd if it does not lie above (2). For a local field K, K^unr is its maximal unramified extension. · and ∏ may denote composita of fields.
items.note: GlobalNumberFields Layer 0 plans: 'Adopt Mathlib's finite and infinite place types and build a uniform API for ranging over all places'. LocalFieldsRamification Layer 2 plans 'The maximal unramified extension. Define K^{ur} ⊆ AlgebraicClosure K'.

items.name: Quadratic characters χ_a, χ_γ; 𝔽₂ as a trivial module
items.statement: For a ∈ ℚ^*, χ_a : G_ℚ → 𝔽₂ is the quadratic character of ℚ(√a). For a field K of characteristic 0 and γ ∈ K^*, χ_γ : G_K → 𝔽₂ is the quadratic character of K(√γ). 𝔽₂ is viewed as a discrete G_ℚ-module with trivial action.
items.note: ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9 plans the Kummer isomorphism 'kummerIso : Kˣ ⧸ (Kˣ)ⁿ ≅ H¹(G_K, μₙ)'. With n = 2 and μ₂ ≅ 𝔽₂, χ_γ is the image of γ.

items.name: Cl(K) is the narrow class group
items.statement: Throughout, Cl(K) denotes the narrow class group of a number field K: invertible fractional ideals modulo principal ideals with a totally positive generator.
items.note: Tau Ceti f790474, TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/NarrowClassGroup/Basic.lean:83: 'The narrow class group Cl⁺(K): invertible fractional ideals of 𝓞 K modulo the principal ideals with a totally positive generator'. GlobalNumberFields Layer 2 also plans it. The paper's ordinary class group appears only in item 5.

items.name: N(φ) and the field of definition L(φ)
items.statement: For a profinite group G, a discrete space X and a continuous map φ : G → X, N(φ) is the largest open normal subgroup of G through which φ factors (it exists: at least one exists by continuity, and the subgroups through which φ factors are closed under products). When G is a Galois group, L(φ) is the fixed field of N(φ), the field of definition of φ.
items.note: The paper leaves existence as an exercise; the argument in parentheses is mine. The notation N(χ) clashes with the twisted module N(χ) of §2 (issues file). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Up_{K/ℚ}(p) and Up_{K/ℚ}(a)
items.statement: For a prime p ramified in a quadratic field K/ℚ, Up_{K/ℚ}(p) is the unique place of K above p. For a positive squarefree integer a all of whose prime factors ramify in K/ℚ, Up_{K/ℚ}(a) is the unique integral ideal of K of norm a.
items.note: In §3 (p. 21) Up_{ℚ(χ_i)/ℚ}(2) is also used when (2) is inert in ℚ(χ_i) (χ_i ∘ i_2^* = χ_5), which goes beyond this definition. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: ℚ(A) for a set of quadratic characters
items.statement: For a set A of quadratic characters G_ℚ → 𝔽₂, ℚ(A) is the fixed field of ⋂_{χ∈A} ker(χ).
items.note: Multiquadratic Layer 0 plans 'K(√d₁,…,√dₙ)/K is Galois with group (ℤ/2)ⁿ … the intermediate fields correspond to 𝔽₂-subspaces'. ℚ(A) = ℚ(√a : χ_a ∈ A).

items.name: Squarefree integers of any sign
items.statement: An integer n is squarefree if p ∣ n implies p² ∤ n for every prime p; squarefree integers may be negative.
items.note: Mathlib/Algebra/Squarefree/Basic.lean:42 at 082e2d3: Squarefree r := ∀ x, x * x ∣ r → IsUnit x. On ℤ this agrees with the paper, including sign and n = 0, which is not squarefree in either.

items.name: Fixed separable closures and decomposition embeddings
items.statement: Fix a separable closure ℚ^sep of ℚ and, for each place v of ℚ, a separable closure ℚ_v^sep of ℚ_v and an embedding i_v : ℚ^sep → ℚ_v^sep. Restriction along i_v gives a continuous injective homomorphism i_v^* : G_{ℚ_v} → G_ℚ. All number fields are taken inside ℚ^sep.
items.note: Standard decomposition-group setup. NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 5 plans the global–local dictionary at finite places but not this fixed choice for every v. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The maximal pro-2 quotient 𝒢_ℚ^{pro-2}
items.statement: ℚ^{pro-2} is the union of all finite Galois subextensions of ℚ^sep/ℚ of 2-power degree. 𝒢_ℚ^{pro-2} := Gal(ℚ^{pro-2}/ℚ), and π_{pro-2} : G_ℚ → 𝒢_ℚ^{pro-2} is the natural projection.
items.note: ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 3 plans 'maximalProPQuotient p G := G ⧸ proPKernel p G … LocalGaloisGroups applies this universal quotient to an absolute Galois group'. The paper's Galois-theoretic description is that quotient for p = 2.

items.name: Inertia groups I_v and the odd places 𝒫
items.statement: For a finite place v of ℚ, I_v := ker(G_{ℚ_v} → G_{𝔽_v}) = Gal(ℚ_v^sep/ℚ_v^unr) is the inertia group. 𝒫 denotes the set of odd (finite) places of ℚ.
items.note: LocalFieldsRamification Layer 4 plans 'Inertia. Define I_K = Gal(Kˢ/K^{ur}), and prove that it is closed and normal'.

items.name: Proposition 2.1 (odd inertia is pro-cyclic ℤ₂ in the pro-2 quotient)
items.statement: For every v ∈ 𝒫, I_v(2) := π_{pro-2}(i_v^*(I_v)) ⊆ 𝒢_ℚ^{pro-2} is isomorphic to ℤ₂ as a topological group.
items.note: Proof: for odd v, the maximal pro-2 extension of ℚ_v is ⋃_k ℚ_v(ζ_{2^k}, π^{1/2^k}) (2.1), so the maximal pro-2 quotient of I_v is ℤ₂. Its map to 𝒢_ℚ^{pro-2} is injective because K = ⋃_k ℚ(ζ_{2^k}, a^{1/2^k}), with v(a) = 1, is pro-2 and ℚ_v·i_v(K) is that maximal extension. LocalFieldsRamification Layer 4 plans the local input, 'I_K/P_K ≅ … Ẑ^{(p')}(1)' and its specialization at ℓ = 2; the global injectivity is not planned. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Fixed inertia generators σ_v, σ_2(1), σ_2(2)
items.statement: For each v ∈ 𝒫 fix a topological generator σ_v of I_v(2) ≅ ℤ₂. Put I_2(2) := π_{pro-2}(i_2^*(I_2)) and fix σ_2(1), σ_2(2) ∈ I_2(2) with χ_{−1}(σ_2(1)) = 1, χ_{−1}(σ_2(2)) = 0, χ_2(σ_2(1)) = 0 and χ_2(σ_2(2)) = 1. These exist because ℚ(ζ_8)/ℚ is totally ramified at (2).
items.locator: §2, running text after Proposition 2.1, p. 8 (arXiv v1)
items.note: These choices underlie the 'normalized' expansion maps. The paper calls elements of I_v(2) 'involutions' when they have order ≤ 2. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 2.2 (minimal topological generators of 𝒢_ℚ^{pro-2})
items.statement: The set 𝔊 := {σ_v : v ∈ 𝒫} ∪ {σ_2(1), σ_2(2)} topologically generates 𝒢_ℚ^{pro-2}, and no proper subset of 𝔊 does.
items.note: Proof: by the Frattini argument (Φ(G) = G²[G, G] for a finite 2-group) it suffices to generate Gal(M/ℚ) for each quadratic M. Every nontrivial quadratic character is ramified at a finite place (Minkowski). For minimality use χ_{p*} (p* = ±p ≡ 1 mod 4), χ_{−1} and χ_2. ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 3 plans the 'Burnside basis theorem. A subset generates G topologically if and only if its image generates G/Φ(G) topologically'; this arithmetic application is not planned. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 2.3(a) (odd ramification read off from σ_v)
items.statement: Let L/ℚ be a finite Galois subextension of ℚ^{pro-2}/ℚ and v ∈ 𝒫. Then v is unramified in L iff the image of σ_v in Gal(L/ℚ) is trivial. More precisely, the ramification index of v in L/ℚ equals the order of the image of σ_v in Gal(L/ℚ).
items.note: Proof: the ramification index is |(proj ∘ i_v^*)(I_v)|, and this projection factors through 𝒢_ℚ^{pro-2}. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 2.3(b) (ramification at 2 and σ_2(1), σ_2(2))
items.statement: Let L/ℚ be a finite Galois subextension of ℚ^{pro-2}/ℚ. If (2) is unramified in L/ℚ, then σ_2(1) and σ_2(2) have trivial image in Gal(L/ℚ). More precisely, the ramification index of (2) in L/ℚ is divisible by |⟨images of σ_2(1), σ_2(2) in Gal(L/ℚ)⟩|.
items.note: Only divisibility is claimed at 2, since σ_2(1) and σ_2(2) need not generate I_2(2). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ), N = ℚ₂/ℤ₂ and the twisted modules N(χ)
items.statement: Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) := Hom_cont(G_ℚ, 𝔽₂) is the set of quadratic characters of ℚ. N := ℚ₂/ℤ₂, with the discrete topology and trivial G_ℚ-action. For χ ∈ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ), N(χ) is the discrete G_ℚ-module N with σ ·_χ n := (−1)^{χ(σ)} n.
items.note: Notation from [Smith]. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Cocy(G_ℚ, N(χ)), N(x) and the coboundaries d_x
items.statement: Cocy(G_ℚ, N(χ)) is the group of continuous 1-cocycles G_ℚ → N(χ). For squarefree x, N(x) := N(χ_x). All these groups lie in the common ambient group Map_cont(G_ℚ, N) of continuous 1-cochains. For a continuous cochain ψ : G_ℚ → N, a squarefree x and σ, τ ∈ G_ℚ, d_x(ψ)(σ, τ) := −ψ(στ) + (−1)^{χ_x(σ)}ψ(τ) + ψ(σ). Then ψ ∈ Cocy(G_ℚ, N(χ_x)) iff d_x(ψ) ≡ 0.
items.note: ProfiniteCohomology Layer 2 plans the explicit complex: 'C1, C2, Z1, Z2 … `Z¹` vanishes at `1`'. The paper's key device is to vary the twist χ_x while keeping one ambient cochain group, as in Proposition 2.9.

items.name: Definition 2.4 (semidirect-product convention)
items.statement: In N ⋊ 𝔽₂ and N[2^s] ⋊ 𝔽₂ (s ∈ ℤ_{≥0}), the nontrivial element of 𝔽₂ acts on N by −id; so these are generalized dihedral groups.
items.note: Convention. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 2.5(i) (cocycles as homomorphisms to N ⋊ 𝔽₂)
items.statement: Let χ ∈ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ). If ψ ∈ Cocy(G_ℚ, N(χ)), then σ ↦ (ψ(σ), χ(σ)) is a continuous homomorphism G_ℚ → N(χ) ⋊ 𝔽₂. Conversely, if ψ : G_ℚ → N is a continuous cochain for which σ ↦ (ψ(σ), χ(σ)) is a homomorphism, then ψ ∈ Cocy(G_ℚ, N(χ)). For ψ ∈ Cocy(G_ℚ, N(χ)), the restriction ψ|_{G_{ℚ(χ)}} is a continuous homomorphism.
items.note: Elementary. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 2.5(ii) (field of definition contains ℚ(χ))
items.statement: Let ψ ∈ Cocy(G_ℚ, N(χ)). If ψ(G_{ℚ(χ)}) ⊄ N[2], then the field of definition L(ψ) contains ℚ(χ).
items.note: Proof: if σ ∈ N(ψ) and 2ψ(τ) ≠ 0, then ψ(τ) = ψ(στ) = (−1)^{χ(σ)}ψ(τ), so χ(σ) = 0. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Unramified cocycles Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ))
items.statement: For ψ ∈ Cocy(G_ℚ, N(χ)), the image of ψ is finite and ψ|_{G_{ℚ(χ)}} ∈ (G_{ℚ(χ)}^{ab})^∨[2^∞]. Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ)) is the preimage of Cl(ℚ(χ))^∨[2^∞] under ψ ↦ ψ|_{G_{ℚ(χ)}}. Here Cl(ℚ(χ))^∨ is identified, via Artin reciprocity for the narrow class group, with the characters of G_{ℚ(χ)} unramified at all finite places.
items.locator: §2.1, running text after Proposition 2.5, p. 10 (arXiv v1)
items.note: The narrow Hilbert class field and 'gal_rayClassField_equiv_rayClassGroup' are planned in ClassFieldTheory Layer 13; this definition is not. The Hilbert class field of a quadratic field is generalized dihedral over ℚ. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 2.6(i) (unramified cocycles split over the dual class group)
items.statement: Let χ ∈ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) be non-trivial (the printed statement omits χ ≠ 0; see note) and s ∈ ℤ_{≥0}. Then the restriction map Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ))[2^s] → Cl(ℚ(χ))^∨[2^s] is a split surjection of abelian groups, and its kernel is isomorphic to ℤ/2^sℤ.
items.note: As printed the hypothesis χ ≠ 0 is missing; for χ = 0 the kernel is 0 (issues file). The kernel consists of the cocycles factoring through Gal(ℚ(χ)/ℚ), determined by their value in N(χ)[2^s] at a lift of the generator. Surjectivity uses Proposition 2.3 to find an involution in Gal(L/ℚ) lifting the generator of Gal(ℚ(χ)/ℚ). Multiquadratic Layer 3 plans the input that 'the nontrivial automorphism acts on Cl(K) by inversion'. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 2.6(ii) (divisibility of unramified cocycles)
items.statement: Let χ ∈ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) be non-trivial and s ∈ ℤ_{≥0}. For every ψ ∈ Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ))[2^s]: ψ ∈ 2·Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ))[2^{s+1}] if and only if ψ|_{G_{ℚ(χ)}} ∈ 2·Cl(ℚ(χ))^∨[2^{s+1}].
items.note: Follows from the splittings at levels s and s + 1, since 2·(kernel at level s + 1) = kernel at level s. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Remark 2.7 (lifting through all cocycles)
items.statement: Let χ ∈ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) be non-trivial, s ∈ ℤ_{≥0} and ψ ∈ Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ))[2^s]. Suppose (2) is unramified in L(ψ)/ℚ, or (2) has residue field degree 1 in L(ψ)/ℚ. Then ψ ∈ 2·Cocy(G_ℚ, N(χ))[2^{s+1}] if and only if ψ|_{G_{ℚ(χ)}} ∈ 2·Cl(ℚ(χ))^∨[2^{s+1}]. Unramified lifts are not required.
items.note: Stated without proof. The paper says the proof is given inside the proof of Theorem 5.10 and reused in Theorem 5.11, outside this range. I saw the odd-prime and dyadic arguments there (TeX 1987–2009). The printed hypothesis refers to L(ψ) before ψ is introduced. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Definition 2.8 (raw cocycle)
items.statement: Let χ ∈ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) be non-trivial and s ∈ ℤ_{≥0}. A raw cocycle (for N(χ)) is a sequence (ψ_i)_{0≤i≤s} with ψ_i ∈ Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ))[2^i] and 2·ψ_{i+1} = ψ_i for 0 ≤ i ≤ s − 1. Equivalently it is a single ψ_s ∈ Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ)) with 2^s ψ_s = 0, with ψ_i := 2^{s−i}ψ_s. By convention ψ_j := 0 for j < 0.
items.locator: §2.1, Definition 2.8 and following paragraph, pp. 11–12 (arXiv v1)
items.note: The basic object of Smith's method. Since ψ_0 ∈ Cocy_unr[1] = 0, ψ_1 is a genus-type quadratic character of ℚ that is unramified over ℚ(χ). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The cube C, the cochains χ_H and the faces C_T
items.statement: Let s ∈ ℤ_{>0}, let (p_i(1), p_i(2))_{i∈[s]} be 2s distinct primes coprime to the squarefree integer d_0, and C := {p_1(1), p_1(2)} × ⋯ × {p_s(1), p_s(2)} × {d_0}. A point x ∈ C is identified with the squarefree integer d_0 ∏_{i∈[s]} π_i(x). For a finite set H of squarefree integers, χ_H : G_ℚ → 𝔽₂ is σ ↦ ∏_{x∈H} χ_x(σ), a product in 𝔽₂ also used as a {0, 1}-valued indicator. For T ⊆ [s], C_T := {x ∈ C : π_i(x) = p_i(2) for all i ∈ T}.
items.locator: §2.1, running text before Proposition 2.9, p. 12 (arXiv v1)
items.note: χ_H is the product of the characters, i.e. the indicator that all χ_x(σ) = 1; it is not the character of ∏H. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 2.9 (Smith's key cocycle calculation)
items.statement: Let j ∈ ℤ_{>0}, C as above, and for each x ∈ C let ψ_j(x) be a raw cocycle for N(x), with ψ_i(x) = 2^{j−i}ψ_j(x) and ψ_i(x) = 0 for i < 0. Let x_0 := d_0 ∏_{i∈[s]} p_i(1) (the printed statement says 'x_0 ∈ C', see note). Then for all σ, τ ∈ G_ℚ, in Map_cont(G_ℚ, N): d_{x_0}(∑_{x∈C} ψ_j(x))(σ, τ) = ∑_{∅≠T⊆[s]} χ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈T}}(σ) · (−1)^{|T|+1+χ_{x_0}(σ)} · ∑_{x∈C_T} ψ_{j−|T|}(x)(τ).
items.note: The printed hypothesis 'Let x_0 ∈ C' is too general. The proof's step −(−1)^{χ_{xx_0}(σ)} + 1 = −(−1)^{|T_x∩T_σ|} + 1 needs T_{x_0} = ∅. For s = 1 and x_0 = p_1(2)d_0 the two sides involve ψ_{j−1}(p_1(1)d_0) and ψ_{j−1}(p_1(2)d_0) respectively (issues file). Every application takes x_0 = d_0∏p_i(1) (TeX 1167, 1876). The proof expands 1 − (−1)^{|T|} = ∑_{∅≠U⊆T}(−1)^{|U|+1}2^{|U|}. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Remark 2.10 (sums of cocycles live in Map_cont(G_ℚ, N))
items.statement: Sums ∑_{x∈C} ψ_j(x) of cocycles for different twists N(x) are taken in the ambient group Map_cont(G_ℚ, N) of continuous cochains, where they are generally not cocycles for any single N(x).
items.note: Convention used throughout. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Corollary 2.11 (cocycle calculation with one vertex removed)
items.statement: Let j ∈ ℤ_{>0}, C as above and x_0 := d_0∏_{i∈[s]} p_i(1) (printed: x_0 ∈ C). Let ψ_j(x) be a raw cocycle for N(x) for each x ∈ C − {x_0}. Then d_{x_0}(∑_{x∈C, x≠x_0} ψ_j(x))(σ, τ) = ∑_{∅≠T⊆[s]} χ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈T}}(σ) · (−1)^{|T|+1+χ_{x_0}(σ)} · ∑_{x∈C_T} ψ_{j−|T|}(x)(τ).
items.note: Proof: set ψ_j(x_0) := 0 and apply Proposition 2.9. It carries the same x_0 caveat. For x_0 = d_0∏p_i(1), x_0 ∉ C_T for T ≠ ∅. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Definition 2.12 (expansion map with support X and pointer χ_0)
items.statement: Let X ⊆ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) be a finite linearly independent set and χ_0 ∈ X. Write 𝔽₂^Y for the free 𝔽₂-vector space on a set Y, and let 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}} act on the group ring 𝔽₂[𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}}] by translation. An expansion map with support X and pointer χ_0 is a continuous homomorphism ψ : G_ℚ → 𝔽₂[𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}}] ⋊ 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}} with two properties. First, π_χ ∘ ψ = χ for every χ ∈ X − {χ_0}, where π_χ is the χ-coordinate of 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}}. Second, π ∘ ψ = χ_0, where π is the unique nontrivial character vanishing on {0} ⋊ 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}} (the augmentation of the group ring).
items.note: Nothing in the atlas plans expansion maps; they are central to Smith's method and [KP2]. ψ solves the embedding problem of the wreath product 𝔽₂ ≀ 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}} over ℚ(X). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Expansion maps are surjective; the target is a wreath product
items.statement: Every expansion map ψ with support X and pointer χ_0 is surjective, because it surjects onto the Frattini quotient. Moreover 𝔽₂[𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}}] ⋊ 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}} ≅ 𝔽₂ ≀ 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}} (regular wreath product).
items.locator: §2.2, running text after Definition 2.12, p. 14 (arXiv v1)
items.note: The wreath-product isomorphism is 'not used'. Mathlib/GroupTheory/RegularWreathProduct.lean:45 (082e2d3) has structure RegularWreathProduct D Q, i.e. (Q → D) × Q, but not this identification. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: t-coordinates φ_Y(ψ) and the reconstruction formula (2.2)
items.statement: Sending t_x ↦ e_0 + e_x (x ∈ X − {χ_0}, where e_0 is the identity of 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}}) gives 𝔽₂[𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}}] ≅ 𝔽₂[t_x : x ∈ X − {χ_0}]/(t_x² : x ∈ X − {χ_0}). This ring has 𝔽₂-basis the squarefree monomials t_Y := ∏_{y∈Y} t_y, Y ⊆ X − {χ_0}. The t_Y-coordinate of ψ is a continuous cochain φ_Y(ψ) : G_ℚ → 𝔽₂, and ψ(g) = (∑_{Y⊆X−{χ_0}} φ_Y(ψ)(g) t_Y, (χ(g))_{χ∈X−{χ_0}}) (2.2).
items.note: The translation by a vector c acts as multiplication by ∏_{χ: c_χ=1}(1 + t_χ) = ∑_S χ_S t_S. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Coboundary operator d on 𝔽₂-valued cochains
items.note: ProfiniteCohomology Layer 2 plans the explicit differentials with 'd ∘ d = 0 (`B1_le_Z1`, `B2_le_Z2`)' in low degree; over 𝔽₂ the signs disappear.

items.name: Smith's recursion (2.3) for the coordinates of an expansion map, and its converse
items.statement: If ψ is an expansion map with support X and pointer χ_0, then φ_∅(ψ) = χ_0, and for every Y ⊆ X − {χ_0} and g_1, g_2 ∈ G_ℚ: (dφ_Y(ψ))(g_1, g_2) = ∑_{∅⊊S⊆Y} χ_S(g_1) φ_{Y−S}(ψ)(g_2) (2.3), where χ_S := ∏_{χ∈S} χ. Conversely, a family (φ_Y)_{Y⊆X−{χ_0}} of continuous cochains satisfying (2.3) with φ_∅ = χ_0 defines by (2.2) an expansion map with support X and pointer χ_0.
items.note: Checked here: it from the semidirect-product law: φ_Y(g_1g_2) = φ_Y(g_1) + ∑_{S⊆Y} χ_S(g_1)φ_{Y−S}(g_2). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Uniqueness of the normalized expansion map ψ(𝔊)
items.statement: For every finite linearly independent X ⊆ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) and χ_0 ∈ X there is at most one expansion map ψ(𝔊) with support X and pointer χ_0 such that φ_Y(ψ(𝔊))(σ) = 0 for every non-empty Y ⊆ X − {χ_0} and every σ ∈ 𝔊.
items.note: Proof: (2.2) fixes ψ on 𝔊, and 𝔊 topologically generates 𝒢_ℚ^{pro-2} (Proposition 2.2), through which ψ factors because its target is a 2-group. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Normalized expansion maps φ_{S;d}(𝔊)
items.statement: If ψ(𝔊) exists, φ_{S;d}(𝔊) := φ_{X−{χ_0}}(ψ(𝔊)), where S is the set of squarefree integers corresponding to X − {χ_0} and d is the squarefree integer corresponding to χ_0. Thus for s ≥ 0, a set S of s squarefree integers and a squarefree a_{s+1} with S ∪ {a_{s+1}} spanning an (s+1)-dimensional subspace of ℚ^*/ℚ^{*2}, there is at most one such cochain φ_{S;a_{s+1}}(𝔊). One says that φ_{S;a_{s+1}}(𝔊) exists when there is one. These cochains are the normalized expansion maps.
items.note: Later the paper also writes ψ_{A;a}(𝔊) for the homomorphism ψ(𝔊) itself (e.g. Proposition 2.15's proof) without defining it. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Lemma 2.13(i) (additivity in the pointer)
items.statement: Let s ∈ ℤ_{≥1}, S a set of s squarefree integers, and x_1, x_2, x_3 squarefree integers with x_1x_2 = x_3 in ℚ^*/ℚ^{*2} (and, implicitly, S ∪ {x_3} linearly independent in ℚ^*/ℚ^{*2}). If φ_{S;x_1}(𝔊) and φ_{S;x_2}(𝔊) exist, then φ_{S;x_3}(𝔊) exists and φ_{S;x_3}(𝔊) = φ_{S;x_1}(𝔊) + φ_{S;x_2}(𝔊).
items.note: This implicitly needs S ∪ {x_3} to be linearly independent in ℚ^*/ℚ^{*2}, or φ_{S;x_3} is undefined (issues file). Proof by induction on s using (2.3). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Lemma 2.13(ii) (additivity in a support entry)
items.statement: Let A = {a_1, …, a_s}, B = {b_1, …, b_s}, C = {c_1, …, c_s} be sets of squarefree integers such that, for some j ∈ [s], a_i = b_i = c_i for all i ∈ [s] − {j} and a_jb_j = c_j in ℚ^*/ℚ^{*2}. Let x be squarefree with C ∪ {x} spanning an (s + 1)-dimensional subspace of ℚ^*/ℚ^{*2} (a hypothesis the statement omits). If φ_{A;x}(𝔊) and φ_{B;x}(𝔊) exist, then φ_{C;x}(𝔊) exists and φ_{C;x}(𝔊) = φ_{A;x}(𝔊) + φ_{B;x}(𝔊).
items.note: The proof is omitted ('similar'). It carries the same implicit independence hypothesis for C ∪ {x}. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The field M(ψ) below the centre
items.statement: For an expansion map ψ with support X (|X| ≥ 2) and pointer χ_0, M(ψ) := ℚ(X) · ∏_{Y⊊X−{χ_0}} L(φ_Y(ψ)), also written M(φ_{X−{χ_0}}(ψ)).
items.locator: §2.2, Proposition 2.14 and following line, p. 16 (arXiv v1)
items.note: L(φ_∅(ψ)) = ℚ(χ_0). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 2.14 (field of definition of an expansion map)
items.statement: Let X ⊆ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) be finite, linearly independent, |X| ≥ 2, χ_0 ∈ X, and ψ an expansion map with support X and pointer χ_0. Then: L(φ_{X−{χ_0}}(ψ)) = (ℚ^sep)^{ker ψ}; it is a multiquadratic extension of ℚ(X − {χ_0}) cut out by the quadratic characters φ_Y(ψ)|_{G_{ℚ(X−{χ_0})}}, Y ⊆ X − {χ_0}; L(φ_{X−{χ_0}}(ψ))/M(ψ) is a central 𝔽₂-extension; and Gal(L(φ_{X−{χ_0}}(ψ))/M(ψ)) is the centre of Gal(L(φ_{X−{χ_0}}(ψ))/ℚ).
items.note: The proof is 'left to the reader'. Checked here: the first claim: every nontrivial normal subgroup of the 2-group 𝔽₂ ≀ 𝔽₂^m (m ≥ 1) contains its order-2 centre ⟨t_top⟩, and translating by it changes φ_top. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 2.15(i) (normalized expansion fields are multiquadratic over the base)
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and let a_1, …, a_{n+1} be squarefree, pairwise coprime and ≠ 1, with a_i ≡ 1 mod 8 for i ∈ [n]. Suppose φ_{{a_1,…,a_n};a_{n+1}}(𝔊) exists. Then L(φ_{{a_1,…,a_n};a_{n+1}}(𝔊))/ℚ({√a_i : i ∈ [n]}) is a multiquadratic extension containing ℚ(√a_{n+1}).
items.note: Immediate from Proposition 2.14. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 2.15(ii) (normalized expansion fields are unramified at finite places)
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and let a_1, …, a_{n+1} be squarefree, pairwise coprime and ≠ 1, with a_i ≡ 1 mod 8 for i ∈ [n], and suppose φ_{{a_1,…,a_n};a_{n+1}}(𝔊) exists. Then L(φ_{{a_1,…,a_n};a_{n+1}}(𝔊))/ℚ({√a_i : i ∈ [n+1]}) is unramified at all finite places.
items.locator: §2.2, Proposition 2.15 (second claim), p. 16; proof p. 17 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Proof: odd v coprime to all a_i have σ_v ↦ 1. At (2), each φ_T ∘ i_2^* (T ≠ ∅) is an unramified character, so ψ ∘ i_2^* factors through ker(χ_5, χ_{a_{n+1}}). For odd v ∣ a_{i_0}, ψ(σ_v) is an involution. The printed 'i_0 ∈ [n]' should read '[n+1]' (issues file). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 2.16 (inductive existence criterion for normalized expansion maps)
items.statement: Let a_1, …, a_{s+1} be odd, squarefree, pairwise coprime integers with a_1, …, a_s > 1 and a_{s+1} ≠ 1, such that (a_j/p) = 1 for all distinct i, j ∈ [s+1] and all primes p ∣ a_i (2.4). Suppose that for every j ∈ [s], φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]−{j}};a_{s+1}}(𝔊) exists and every prime p ∣ a_j splits completely in L(φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]−{j}};a_{s+1}}(𝔊)). Then φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]};a_{s+1}}(𝔊) exists.
items.note: Proof: θ(σ, τ) := ∑_{∅≠S⊆[s]} (∏_{j∈S}χ_{a_j}(σ)) φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]−S};a_{s+1}}(𝔊)(τ) is a 2-cocycle. Its class is trivial at ∞ (a_i > 0), at odd places (by (2.4) and splitting), and so at 2 by Hilbert reciprocity (item 64). Choose φ with dφ = θ and twist by the quadratic character matching φ on 𝔊. This is a central embedding problem with a local–global obstruction. InverseGalois IG.4 plans only general 'weak and proper solutions of finite embedding problems'. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Remark 2.17 (converse of Proposition 2.16)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses on a_1, …, a_{s+1} of Proposition 2.16, if φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]};a_{s+1}}(𝔊) exists, then for each j ∈ [s] φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]−{j}};a_{s+1}}(𝔊) exists and every prime p ∣ a_j splits completely in its field of definition.
items.note: Asserted, and neither proved nor used. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Local–global principle for H²(G_ℚ, 𝔽₂) with the reciprocity sum (used in Proposition 2.16)
items.statement: A class in H²(G_ℚ, 𝔽₂) is zero iff its restriction to H²(G_{ℚ_v}, 𝔽₂) is zero for every place v. If the restrictions vanish at all v ≠ (2), they vanish at (2) too, by Hilbert reciprocity. Moreover H²(Gal(ℚ_v^unr/ℚ_v), 𝔽₂) = H²(Ẑ, 𝔽₂) = 0, so classes inflated from an unramified quotient vanish locally.
items.note: ClassFieldTheory Layer 10 plans '`eq_zero_of_localInv_eq_zero` is exactness at `Br K` (Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether), `sumLocalInv_eq_zero` is exactness in the middle'. QuadraticFormInvariants Layer 7 plans 'ι : Br(K)[2] ≃ H²(G_K, μ₂)'. The vanishing of H²(Ẑ, 𝔽₂) belongs to cohomological dimension (ProfiniteCohomology Layer 11).

items.name: The degenerate expansion map φ_{a;a}(𝔊) for a ∈ 𝒟
items.statement: Let a ∈ 𝒟. Then χ_a ∪ χ_a = 0 in H²(G_ℚ, 𝔽₂), and there is a unique map φ_{a;a}(𝔊) : G_ℚ → 𝔽₂ with (dφ_{a;a}(𝔊))(σ, τ) = χ_a(σ)·χ_a(τ) that vanishes on every element of 𝔊.
items.locator: §2.2, running text before Lemma 2.18, p. 18 (arXiv v1)
items.note: χ_a ∪ χ_a = χ_a ∪ χ_{−1} corresponds to the quaternion algebra (a, −1), which splits because a ∈ 𝒟 is a sum of two squares. QuadraticFormInvariants 7B plans the 'symbol as a cup product', but not this instance. Uniqueness: two such maps differ by a character vanishing on 𝔊, hence 0. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: φ_{a;a}(𝔊) is a ℤ/4ℤ-character; its ramification
items.statement: Identify ℤ/4ℤ with 𝔽₂ × 𝔽₂ under (x, y) * (x', y') = (x + x' + yy', y + y'). For a ∈ 𝒟, σ ↦ (φ_{a;a}(𝔊)(σ), χ_a(σ)) is a ℤ/4ℤ-character. If a > 1, L(φ_{a;a}(𝔊)) is a cyclic quartic field with quadratic subfield ℚ(√a). An odd place v ramifies in it iff v ∣ a, and then with ramification index 4; the same holds for v = (2) when 2 ∣ a. If 2 ∤ a (so a ≡ 1 or 5 mod 8), (2) is unramified in it. For a ≡ 5 mod 8 this is shown by comparison with the unramified ℤ/4ℤ-character of ℚ₂ (field ℚ_16).
items.note: Says nothing about the infinite place (see item 67). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Lemma 2.18 (the cyclic quartic field L(φ_{a;a}(𝔊)))
items.statement: Let a ∈ 𝒟 with a > 1. Then L(φ_{a;a}(𝔊))/ℚ is a ℤ/4ℤ-extension that ramifies exactly at the finite places where ℚ(√a)/ℚ ramifies, each with ramification index 4.
items.note: The printed statement says 'places'. The infinite place can ramify although ℚ(√a) is real: for a = 5 the field is ℚ(ζ_5) (issues file). 'Finite' is added here. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The Artin pairing ⟨−, −⟩_{Art_s(A)} of a finite abelian 2-group
items.statement: Let A be a finite abelian 2-group, s ∈ ℤ_{≥1} and A^∨ := Hom(A, ℚ₂/ℤ₂). Define ⟨−, −⟩_{Art_s(A)} : 2^{s−1}·A[2^s] × 2^{s−1}·A^∨[2^s] → 𝔽₂ by ⟨a, χ⟩ := ψ(a) for any ψ ∈ A^∨ with 2^{s−1}ψ = χ. The value does not depend on the choice of ψ, and it lies in 𝔽₂ = (½ℤ)/ℤ because a ∈ A[2].
items.note: The k-th Artin pairing of Smith's method. The intro's notation ⟨b, χ_a⟩_{k,ℚ(√d)} and Art_{k,ℚ(√d)} refers to it. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Kernels of the Artin pairing
items.statement: The left and right kernels of ⟨−, −⟩_{Art_s(A)} are 2^s·A[2^{s+1}] and 2^s·A^∨[2^{s+1}] respectively. Indeed ⟨−, −⟩_{Art_s(A)} = ⟨−, −⟩_{Art_1(2^{s−1}A)}, identifying (2^{s−1}A)^∨ with 2^{s−1}A^∨ by precomposition with multiplication by 2^{s−1}.
items.note: Hence rk_{2^s} A = dim of 2^{s−1}A[2^s] minus the dimension of the left kernel. Checked here: the case s = 1 directly. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Art_s(x) for a quadratic field and its Galois interpretation
items.statement: For squarefree x ≠ 1, ⟨−, −⟩_{Art_s(x)} := ⟨−, −⟩_{Art_s(Cl(ℚ(√x))[2^∞])}, with Cl the narrow class group. Cl(ℚ(√x))[2^∞] is identified with the maximal 2-quotient of Cl(ℚ(√x)), and by the Artin map with Gal(H_{2^∞}(ℚ(√x))/ℚ(√x)). Here H_{2^∞}(K) is the largest abelian 2-power extension of K unramified at all finite places. So ⟨b, χ⟩_{Art_s(x)} is the Artin symbol of the 2-torsion class b in a cyclic degree-2^s extension of ℚ(√x), unramified at finite places, whose character ψ satisfies 2^{s−1}ψ = χ.
items.note: ClassFieldTheory Layer 13 plans 'narrowHilbertClassField' and 'gal_rayClassField_equiv_rayClassGroup'. The pairing Art_s(x) is not planned. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Standing setup for higher Rédei reciprocity
items.statement: Let n ∈ ℤ_{≥1}, A ⊆ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) with |A| = n, and χ_1 ≠ χ_2 in Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) − A. Put A_1 := A ∪ {χ_1} and A_2 := A ∪ {χ_2}. For finite Galois L/ℚ, Ram(L/ℚ) is the set of places of ℚ that ramify in L. Assume: the n sets Ram(ℚ(χ)/ℚ), χ ∈ A, are non-empty, pairwise disjoint and do not contain ∞, so ℚ(A) is totally real and A is linearly independent; and Ram(ℚ(χ_1)/ℚ) and Ram(ℚ(χ_2)/ℚ) are non-empty and disjoint from ⋃_{χ∈A} Ram(ℚ(χ)/ℚ), so each χ_i is independent of A.
items.note: Generalizes [KP3]. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The 4-tuple (A_1, A_2, ψ_1, ψ_2) and its cochains φ_{i,B}
items.statement: ψ_1, ψ_2 : G_ℚ ↠ 𝔽₂[𝔽₂^A] ⋊ 𝔽₂^A are expansion maps with supports A_1, A_2 and pointers χ_1, χ_2. Put φ_{i,B} := φ_B(ψ_i) for B ⊆ A, so that φ_{i,∅} = χ_i. By Proposition 2.14, L(ψ_i)/M(ψ_i) is a central 𝔽₂-extension (i = 1, 2).
items.note: L(ψ_i) is the fixed field of ker ψ_i. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Coprimality constraints on the pointers
items.statement: The pointers χ_1, χ_2 satisfy the coprimality constraints if: (i) Ram(ℚ(χ_1)/ℚ) ∩ Ram(ℚ(χ_2)/ℚ) ⊆ {(2)}; (ii) inv_2(χ_1 ∪ χ_2) = 0, i.e. the local Hilbert symbol of χ_1, χ_2 at 2 is trivial; (iii) χ_1(σ_2(2)) = 0 or χ_2(σ_2(2)) = 0; (iv) (2) splits completely in ℚ(A)/ℚ.
items.note: (i) also excludes ∞ from both ramification sets, so at most one pointer is odd (imaginary). (iii) says that at most one of the pointer radicands d_1, d_2 is even. The 'Rédei admissible 4-tuple as above' in Definition 3.1 includes these constraints. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Local coordinates at 2 are characters
items.statement: For a 4-tuple as above with (2) split completely in ℚ(A), φ_{T'}(ψ_1) ∘ i_2^* and φ_{T'}(ψ_2) ∘ i_2^* are quadratic characters G_{ℚ₂} → 𝔽₂ for every T' ⊆ A.
items.locator: §3.1, running text before Definition 3.1, p. 21 (arXiv v1)
items.note: By (2.3), since each χ ∈ A is locally trivial at 2. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Definition 3.1 (Rédei admissible 4-tuple; pointer vector; base set)
items.statement: A 4-tuple (A_1, A_2, ψ_1, ψ_2) as above (standing setup and coprimality constraints) is Rédei admissible if four conditions hold. (1) If ∞ splits completely in ℚ(A_1 ∪ A_2)/ℚ, then ∞ splits completely in M(ψ_1)M(ψ_2)/ℚ. (2) Whenever {i, j} = {1, 2} and ∞ ramifies in L(ψ_i)/ℚ, ∞ splits completely in M(ψ_j)/ℚ. (3) Whenever {i, j} = {1, 2} and a place w of ℚ(A) above v ∈ 𝒫 ramifies in L(ψ_i)/ℚ(A), v splits completely in M(ψ_j)/ℚ and v is unramified in L(ψ_j)/ℚ. (4) If L(ψ_1)L(ψ_2)/ℚ is ramified at (2), there are i, j with {i, j} = {1, 2} such that: ψ_i is a normalized expansion map with χ_i(σ_2(2)) = 0 and φ_T(ψ_i) ∘ i_2^* = 0 for every ∅ ≠ T ⊊ A; and χ_i ∘ i_2^* is orthogonal to φ_{T'}(ψ_j) ∘ i_2^* under the local Hilbert pairing at (2) for every T' ⊆ A. (χ_1, χ_2) is the pointer vector and A the base set.
items.note: Checked in §§4–5 via profitable and governing triples. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Well-definedness of Art(v, L(ψ_2)/ℚ) at odd ramified places of χ_1
items.statement: For a Rédei admissible 4-tuple, every v ∈ Ram(ℚ(χ_1)/ℚ) ∩ 𝒫 is unramified in L(ψ_2)/ℚ and splits completely in M(ψ_2). So the Artin class Art(v, L(ψ_2)/ℚ) lies in Gal(L(ψ_2)/M(ψ_2)), the centre of Gal(L(ψ_2)/ℚ), which has order 2, and is a well-defined element of 𝔽₂. The same holds with 1 and 2 swapped.
items.locator: §3.1, running text after Definition 3.1, p. 21 (arXiv v1)
items.note: From condition (3), since v is unramified in ℚ(A) and ramified in ℚ(χ_1) ⊆ L(ψ_1). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Well-definedness of Art(∞, L(ψ_j)/ℚ)
items.statement: If {i, j} = {1, 2} and ∞ ramifies in ℚ(χ_i)/ℚ, then ∞ splits completely in M(ψ_j)/ℚ, so Art(∞, L(ψ_j)/ℚ) lies in the centre Gal(L(ψ_j)/M(ψ_j)) ≅ 𝔽₂ and is well defined.
items.note: From condition (2), since ℚ(χ_i) ⊆ L(ψ_i). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Well-definedness of the dyadic symbol Art((2), L(ψ_i)/ℚ)
items.statement: Suppose (2) ramifies in L(ψ_1)L(ψ_2)/ℚ, and let {i, j} be as in condition (4) of Definition 3.1. If χ_i ∘ i_2^* = 0, then (2) splits completely in M(ψ_i)/ℚ and is unramified in L(ψ_i)/ℚ, so Art((2), L(ψ_i)/ℚ) ∈ Gal(L(ψ_i)/M(ψ_i)) ≅ 𝔽₂. If χ_i ∘ i_2^* ≠ 0, then L(ψ_i)/ℚ(χ_i) is unramified at Up_{ℚ(χ_i)/ℚ}(2) (Proposition 2.15), which splits completely in M(ψ_i)/ℚ(χ_i). Then Art((2), L(ψ_i)/ℚ) denotes Art(Up_{ℚ(χ_i)/ℚ}(2), L(ψ_i)/ℚ(χ_i)) ∈ 𝔽₂. If χ_i ∘ i_2^* = χ_5, then χ_j(σ_2(2)) = 0.
items.note: The last claim is (5, d_j)_2 = v_2(d_j) mod 2 together with orthogonality. Only the index i of condition (4) gets a dyadic symbol; see item 90 and the issues file. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Reduced ramification set R̃am
items.statement: For a quadratic field ℚ(√d)/ℚ with d squarefree: R̃am(ℚ(√d)/ℚ) := Ram(ℚ(√d)/ℚ) − {(2)} if d has even 2-adic valuation, and R̃am(ℚ(√d)/ℚ) := Ram(ℚ(√d)/ℚ) otherwise. Equivalently, a finite v lies in R̃am iff v(d) is odd, and ∞ lies in R̃am iff d < 0.
items.note: The 'equivalently' is (3.4) plus the case of ∞. Printed '∖ (2)' means ∖ {(2)}. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 3.2 (higher Rédei reciprocity)
items.statement: Let (A_1, A_2, ψ_1, ψ_2) be a Rédei admissible 4-tuple with pointer vector (χ_1, χ_2), satisfying the standing hypotheses and coprimality constraints. Then, in 𝔽₂: ∑_{v ∈ R̃am(ℚ(χ_1)/ℚ)} Art(v, L(ψ_2)/ℚ) = ∑_{v' ∈ R̃am(ℚ(χ_2)/ℚ)} Art(v', L(ψ_1)/ℚ). Each Art(v, L(ψ_j)/ℚ) is the Artin class in the centre Gal(L(ψ_j)/M(ψ_j)) ≅ 𝔽₂; at v = (2) with χ_j ∘ i_2^* ≠ 0 it means Art(Up_{ℚ(χ_j)/ℚ}(2), L(ψ_j)/ℚ(χ_j)).
items.note: It strengthens the reciprocity law of [KP3]. For n = 1 it is the classical Rédei reciprocity [a, b, c] = [a, c, b], itself a generalization of quadratic reciprocity. Proof: Hilbert reciprocity for (α_{1,A}, α_{2,A}) over ℚ(A), with the local computations of Proposition 3.6 and the parity lemma Corollary 3.4. The dyadic bookkeeping in the proof needs repair, but the statement holds (issues file). No stage plans it; CA.1 plans 'source-scoped higher reciprocity through class field theory' only in general terms. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Kummer classes α_{i,B}
items.statement: For i ∈ {1, 2} and B ⊆ A, φ_{i,B}|_{G_{ℚ(B)}} is a quadratic character (by (2.3)), and α_{i,B} ∈ ℚ(B)^*/ℚ(B)^{*2} is its Kummer class; α_{i,∅} = d_i with χ_i = χ_{d_i}. Moreover φ_{i,A}|_{G_{ℚ(A)}} generates a free 𝔽₂[Gal(ℚ(A)/ℚ)]-module of rank 1 whose field is L(ψ_i). So L(ψ_i) is the Galois closure over ℚ of ℚ(A)(√α_{i,A}), and L(ψ_i) = M(ψ_i)(√α_{i,A}).
items.note: Kummer theory is planned (ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9); these classes are not. The paper also uses that α_{i,A} is a G_ℚ-invariant class in M(ψ_i)^*/M(ψ_i)^{*2}. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 3.3 (norm compatibility of the Kummer classes)
items.statement: For all i ∈ {1, 2} and all B ⊆ A: N_{ℚ(A)/ℚ(B)}(α_{i,A}) = α_{i,B} in ℚ(B)^*/ℚ(B)^{*2}.
items.note: It generalizes the link between D_4-extensions and conics [Stevenhagen, Rédei symbols, §5]. Proof: reduce to B = A − {a}. By Kummer theory, the norm is the corestriction, computed by (3.1)–(3.2) (item 83), the identity (3.3) (item 84), and (2.3) at (σ, σ). The displayed identity in the proof has a σ where τ belongs (issues file). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Corestriction of characters from an index-2 subgroup
items.statement: Let G_1 ⊆ G_2 be profinite groups with [G_2 : G_1] = 2, and let χ : G_1 → 𝔽₂, χ' : G_2 → 𝔽₂ be continuous characters. Then cor_{G_1}^{G_2}(χ) = χ' iff χ(σ²) = χ'(σ) (3.1) and χ(στσ^{−1}) + χ(τ) = χ'(τ) (3.2) for all σ ∈ G_2 − G_1 and τ ∈ G_1.
items.note: This is the transfer formula with transversal {1, σ}. ProfiniteCohomology Layer 6 plans 'Corestriction in degrees 0, 1, 2. The three formulas of §3, for a variable transversal'. Layer 9 plans the norm/corestriction link 'corestriction H¹(G_L, μₙ) → H¹(G_K, μₙ) corresponds to the norm N_{L/K}' (kummerIso_norm).

items.name: Conjugation identity (3.3) and the square identity
items.note: (3.3): in the image of ψ_i, σ acts on 𝔽₂[𝔽₂^A] ⋊ {0} as multiplication by 1 + t_a, so 1 + σ acts as t_a; compare t_A-coefficients. The square identity is (2.3) at (σ, σ). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Corollary 3.4(a) (parity of odd valuations at split finite places)
items.statement: Let i ∈ {1, 2} and let v be a finite place of ℚ that splits completely in ℚ(A)/ℚ. Then v ∈ R̃am(ℚ(χ_i)/ℚ) iff |{w ∈ Ω_{ℚ(A)} : w ∣ v, w(α_{i,A}) ≡ 1 mod 2}| is odd.
items.note: From (3.4), v ∈ R̃am ⟺ v(α_{i,∅}) odd, and from (3.5), ∑_{w|v} w(α_{i,A}) ≡ v(α_{i,∅}) mod 2, via Proposition 3.3 with B = ∅. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Corollary 3.4(b) (parity of negative real embeddings)
items.statement: Let i ∈ {1, 2}. Then ∞ ∈ R̃am(ℚ(χ_i)/ℚ) iff |{σ : ℚ(A) → ℝ : σ(α_{i,A}) < 0}| is odd.
items.note: The proof is left to the reader: the sign of N_{ℚ(A)/ℚ}(α_{i,A}) = α_{i,∅} is the product of the signs. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Hilbert pairing (−, −)_K and (−, −)_v
items.statement: For a local field K, (−, −)_K is the Hilbert pairing on K^*/K^{*2}, written additively with values in 𝔽₂. For a place v of a number field L, (−, −)_v := (−, −)_{L_v}.
items.locator: §3.2, running text before Lemma 3.5, p. 24 (arXiv v1)
items.note: QuadraticFormInvariants 6C plans '`hilbertSymbol a b : ℤˣ` is `+1` when `∃ x y : K, b = x² − a y²`', symmetric and bimultiplicative. ClassFieldTheory Layer 14 plans the real invariants 'infiniteHilbertInvariantAt'.

items.name: Lemma 3.5 (Hilbert symbol against the unramified class)
items.statement: Let p be a finite place of ℚ, K a finite extension of ℚ_p, and α the class in K^*/K^{*2} of the unramified quadratic extension K(√α). Then (α, −)_K : K^*/K^{*2} → 𝔽₂ equals v_K(−) mod 2.
items.note: QuadraticFormInvariants 6B plans 'Evaluation against the unramified class. For Δ as above and every b : Kˣ, (Δ, b)_K = (−1)^{v_K(b)}', and 6C 'the value against the unramified class is the closed (Δ, b)_K = (−1)^{v_K(b)} of 6B'. The paper's proof sends a uniformizer to Frobenius under the local Artin map (ClassFieldTheory Layer 6). Its label 'Hilbert symbols at 2' is broader than 2.

items.name: w(α) at real places
items.statement: For a real place w of a number field L, given by σ : L → ℝ, and α ∈ L^*: w(α) := 0 if σ(α) > 0, and 1 otherwise. At finite w, w(α) is the valuation.
items.note: Makes Proposition 3.6(b)–(c) uniform in finite and real places. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Artin symbols at places ramified in L(ψ_1)/ℚ(A) (remark before Proposition 3.6)
items.statement: If some w ∈ Ω_{ℚ(A)} above a place v of ℚ ramifies in L(ψ_1)/ℚ(A), then Art(v, L(ψ_2)/ℚ) is a well-defined element of 𝔽₂, and symmetrically. This is correct for v ∈ 𝒫 (condition (3)) and v = ∞ (condition (2)). At v = (2) it holds only when i = 2 in condition (4).
items.locator: §3.2, running text before Proposition 3.6, p. 24 (arXiv v1)
items.note: The printed statement covers v = (2) with no restriction. If (2) ∈ Ram(χ_1) and χ_2 = χ_{2m} (so i = 1 is forced), L(ψ_2) is ramified at (2), and Art((2), L(ψ_2)/ℚ) is undefined (issues file). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 3.6(a.1) (unramified finite places)
items.statement: Let v be a finite place of ℚ and w ∈ Ω_{ℚ(A)} a place above v that is unramified in L(ψ_1)·L(ψ_2)/ℚ(A). Then (α_{1,A}, α_{2,A})_w = 0.
items.note: Both classes are unramified at w, and by Lemma 3.5 two unramified classes pair trivially. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 3.6(a.2) (real places, pointers even)
items.statement: Suppose ∞ ∉ Ram(ℚ(χ_1)/ℚ) ∪ Ram(ℚ(χ_2)/ℚ). Then (α_{1,A}, α_{2,A})_w takes the same value for all w ∈ Ω_{ℚ(A)} above ∞.
items.note: By condition (1), ∞ splits completely in M(ψ_1)M(ψ_2). Each α_{i,A} is G_ℚ-invariant modulo squares of the totally real M(ψ_i), so its sign is the same at all real embeddings. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 3.6(b) (places above 2)
items.statement: Suppose (2) ramifies in L(ψ_1)L(ψ_2)/ℚ, and let {i, j} = {1, 2} be as in condition (4) of Definition 3.1. Then (α_{1,A}, α_{2,A})_w = w(α_{j,A}) · Art((2), L(ψ_i)/ℚ) in 𝔽₂ for every w ∈ Ω_{ℚ(A)} above (2).
items.note: Proof: move to the place 𝔱 fixed by i_2. Write σ^{−1}(α_{h,A}) = α_{h,A}γ_h with γ_h in the span of the α_{h,T}, T ⊊ A. γ_i is locally in ⟨α_{i,∅}⟩, which is orthogonal to all α_{j,T}. α_{i,A} is locally unramified (ψ_i normalized), so Lemma 3.5 applies. The proof cites Proposition 3.3 for the γ_h step, but that step uses the Galois-module structure (issues file). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 3.6(c) (odd and real places ramified in L(ψ_i)/ℚ(A))
items.statement: Let {i, j} = {1, 2}, let v ≠ (2) be a place of ℚ, and let w ∈ Ω_{ℚ(A)} above v ramify in L(ψ_i)/ℚ(A). Then (α_{1,A}, α_{2,A})_w = w(α_{i,A}) · Art(v, L(ψ_j)/ℚ) in 𝔽₂.
items.note: Finite v: v splits completely in M(ψ_j) and is unramified in L(ψ_j), so α_{j,A} lands in one unramified class c at all embeddings, with c trivial iff Art(v, L(ψ_j)/ℚ) = 0; then apply Lemma 3.5. v = ∞: the sign of α_{j,A} is constant, and positive iff Art(∞, L(ψ_j)/ℚ) = 0. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Hilbert reciprocity over ℚ(A) ((3.7))
items.statement: For α, β ∈ ℚ(A)^*: ∑_{w∈Ω_{ℚ(A)}} (α, β)_w = 0 in 𝔽₂. In the proof it is applied to α_{1,A}, α_{2,A}.
items.note: ClassFieldTheory Layer 14 plans 'ClassFieldTheory.hilbertProductFormula in additive cohomological form: the sum of the local `ZMod 2` invariants is zero', for number fields.

items.name: Grouping step in the proof of Theorem 3.2
items.statement: Places of ℚ(A) unramified in L(ψ_1)L(ψ_2)/ℚ(A) contribute 0 to (3.7). Finite ones contribute 0 by (a.1). The 2^n real places contribute 2^n copies of one value by (a.2), which is 0 since n ≥ 1. For a rational place v below some w ramified in L(ψ_1)/ℚ(A), with v ∈ 𝒫 ∪ {∞} (or v = (2) with i = 2 in condition (4)), v splits completely in ℚ(A). Then ∑_{w|v} (α_{1,A}, α_{2,A})_w = Art(v, L(ψ_2)/ℚ) if v ∈ R̃am(ℚ(χ_1)/ℚ), and 0 otherwise, by Proposition 3.6(b)–(c) and Corollary 3.4; symmetrically for ψ_2. Grouping (3.7) by rational places gives Theorem 3.2.
items.note: At v = (2) the right bookkeeping uses Proposition 3.6(b): ∑_{w|2} = v_2(α_{j,∅}) · Art((2), L(ψ_i)/ℚ). The printed argument attributes this to the 'L(ψ_1)-ramified' case whether or not i = 2 (issues file). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Profitable-triple cube C, base point x₀ and sub-cubes C_{p_i(h)}, C_T
items.statement: Let s ∈ ℤ_{≥1}; let p_1(1), p_1(2), …, p_s(1), p_s(2) be 2s distinct positive odd primes with p_i(1)p_i(2) ≡ 1 mod 8 for each i ∈ [s]; let d₀ be a positive squarefree integer coprime to ∏_{i∈[s]} p_i(1)p_i(2). Put C := {p_1(1), p_1(2)} × ⋯ × {p_s(1), p_s(2)} × {d₀}, identifying ((p_i(f(i)))_{i∈[s]}, d₀) (f: [s] → [2]) with the squarefree integer d₀·∏_{i=1}^{s} p_i(f(i)), and x₀ := d₀·∏_{i=1}^{s} p_i(1). For i ∈ [s], h ∈ [2]: C_{p_i(h)} := {x ∈ C : π_i(x) = p_i(h)}; for T ⊆ [s] and f: T → {1,2}: C_{(p_i(f(i)))_{i∈T}} := {x ∈ C : π_i(x) = p_i(f(i)) ∀ i ∈ T}; C_T := {x ∈ C : π_i(x) = p_i(2) for all i ∈ T}.
items.note: No atlas stage plans Smith's method; atlas grep for 'reflection principle', 'Rédei', 'additive system', 'governing field', 'Ramsey' finds nothing relevant. The C_T convention agrees with §2 (before Proposition 2.9). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Triple (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) (equation (4.1))
items.statement: With C, x₀ as in the §4 setup, let a be a divisor of d₀. A triple (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) consists of, for each x ∈ C − {x₀}, a raw cocycle ψ_{s+1}(x) for N(x) (so ψ_{s+1}(x) ∈ Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ_x)), 2^{s+1}ψ_{s+1}(x) = 0, and ψ_j(x) := 2^{s+1−j}ψ_{s+1}(x), ψ_j := 0 for j ≤ 0) satisfying (4.1): ψ_1(x) = 2^s·ψ_{s+1}(x) = χ_a.
items.note: No atlas stage plans Smith's method; atlas grep for 'reflection principle', 'Rédei', 'additive system', 'governing field', 'Ramsey' finds nothing relevant. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Remark 4.1 (the lifted character χ_a has a > 0)
items.statement: In a triple (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}), equation (4.1) forces a > 0: since s + 1 ≥ 2, (4.1) gives χ_a ∪ χ_{−x} = 0 in H²(G_ℚ, 𝔽₂) for each x ∈ C − {x₀}; as x > 0, the Hilbert symbol (a, −x)_∞ = 1 forces a > 0.
items.note: No atlas stage plans Smith's method; atlas grep for 'reflection principle', 'Rédei', 'additive system', 'governing field', 'Ramsey' finds nothing relevant. Checked: the obstruction to lifting χ to a cocycle for N(χ_x)[4] is χ ∪ χ + χ_x ∪ χ = χ ∪ χ_{−x}. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Definition 4.2 (profitable triple)
items.statement: A triple (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) is profitable if for each i ∈ [s]: (1) (∑_{x∈C_T} ψ_{s+1−|T|}(x))(σ_{p_i(2)}) = 0 for every T ⊆ [s] with i ∈ T; (2) ∑_{x∈C_{p_i(2)}} ψ_{s−1}(x) = 0 (equation (4.2)); (3) the normalized expansion map φ_{{p_j(1)p_j(2) : j∈[s]−{i}}; p_i(1)p_i(2)}(𝔊) exists; (4) every prime l | d₀ splits completely in L(φ_{{p_j(1)p_j(2) : j∈[s]−{i}}; p_i(1)p_i(2)}(𝔊))/ℚ; (5) (2) and ∞ split completely in M(φ_{{p_j(1)p_j(2) : j∈[s]−{i}}; p_i(1)p_i(2)}(𝔊))/ℚ.
items.note: No atlas stage plans Smith's method; atlas grep for 'reflection principle', 'Rédei', 'additive system', 'governing field', 'Ramsey' finds nothing relevant. Central new notion of the paper (no analogue in Smith). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Remark 4.3 (condition (2) propagates to all codimensions)
items.statement: If ∑_{x∈C_{p_i(2)}} ψ_{s−1}(x) = 0 for every i ∈ [s] (condition (2) of Definition 4.2), then ∑_{x∈C_T} ψ_{s−|T|}(x) = 0 for every ∅ ≠ T ⊆ [s]. Proof sketch: apply the coboundary (Proposition 2.9 on the sub-cube C_{p_i(2)}) to (4.2), evaluate at σ with χ_{p_j(1)p_j(2)}(σ) = 1 and χ_{p_k(1)p_k(2)}(σ) = 0 for k ∉ {i, j}, obtaining ∑_{x∈C_{{i,j}}} ψ_{s−2}(x) = 0, and iterate.
items.note: No atlas stage plans Smith's method; atlas grep for 'reflection principle', 'Rédei', 'additive system', 'governing field', 'Ramsey' finds nothing relevant. The printed displayed coboundary has an index slip (C_T, ψ_{s−|T|} for C_{T∪{i}}, ψ_{s−1−|T|}); Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 4.4 (local coincidence of the quadratic fields of a profitable cube)
items.statement: Let (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) be a profitable triple. If p is a prime divisor of d₀ or p = 2, then ℚ_p(√x) = ℚ_p(√x₀) for every x ∈ C. Moreover, for each i ∈ [s], h ∈ [2] and all x, x′ ∈ C_{p_i(h)}, ℚ_{p_i(h)}(√x) = ℚ_{p_i(h)}(√x′). (Proof: every odd p | d₀ splits in ℚ(√(p_i(1)p_i(2))) by condition (4); p_j(1)p_j(2) is a square mod p_i(h) for i ≠ j since φ_{p_j(1)p_j(2); p_i(1)p_i(2)}(𝔊) exists, so χ_{p_j(1)p_j(2)} ∪ χ_{p_i(1)p_i(2)} = 0.)
items.note: No atlas stage plans Smith's method; atlas grep for 'reflection principle', 'Rédei', 'additive system', 'governing field', 'Ramsey' finds nothing relevant. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Lemma 4.5(i) (unramified primes stay unramified in composita of raw cocycles)
items.statement: Let S be a set of squarefree integers all > 1 such that the decomposition group of (2) in K := ℚ({√x : x ∈ S}) is cyclic; let k ≥ 1 and let ψ_{k+1}(x) be a raw cocycle for N(x) for each x ∈ S. If a prime p does not ramify in K, then p is unramified in ∏_{x∈S} L(ψ_{k+1}(x)).
items.note: No atlas stage plans Smith's method; atlas grep for 'reflection principle', 'Rédei', 'additive system', 'governing field', 'Ramsey' finds nothing relevant. Proof in source: 'Straightforward.' Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Lemma 4.5(ii), first claim (ramification index at most 2)
items.statement: Same hypotheses as Lemma 4.5(i). If p ramifies in K, then the ramification index of p in ∏_{x∈S} L(ψ_{k+1}(x)) equals 2 (as used: is at most 2).
items.note: No atlas stage plans Smith's method; atlas grep for 'reflection principle', 'Rédei', 'additive system', 'governing field', 'Ramsey' finds nothing relevant. 'equals 2' should be 'is at most 2'; Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Lemma 4.5(ii), second claim (residue degree 1 at primes ramified in every ℚ(√x))
items.statement: Same hypotheses as Lemma 4.5(i), and assume all decomposition groups of K/ℚ are cyclic (as used: the decomposition group of p in K/ℚ is cyclic). If p ramifies in ℚ(√x) for every x ∈ S, then the residue field degree of p in ∏_{x∈S} L(ψ_k(x)) equals 1.

The applications (TeX 1355, 1369, 1389, 1549, 2174) verify cyclicity only at p; the global hypothesis generally fails for S = C − {x₀}. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The cochains ψ_T(C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}})
items.statement: For a profitable triple and ∅ ⊆ T ⊊ [s], ψ_T(C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) := ∑_{x∈C_{[s]−T}} ψ_{|T|+1}(x) ∈ Map_cont(G_ℚ, N). The same formula defines ψ_{[s]} = ∑_{x∈C} ψ_{s+1}(x) once a raw cocycle ψ_{s+1}(x₀) is also given.

items.name: Theorem 4.6(a) (point gain: a raw cocycle at x₀)
items.statement: Let (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) be a profitable triple. Then there exists a raw cocycle ψ_{s+1}(x₀) for N(x₀) such that ∑_{x∈C} ψ_i(x) = 0 for each i ∈ [s] (equation (4.3)). In particular 2^s ψ_{s+1}(x₀) = χ_a, so χ_a ∈ 2^s·Cl(ℚ(√x₀))^∨[2^{s+1}].

The 'in particular' is how Theorems 5.2, 5.3 use it. For s = 1 the proof invokes Theorem 3.2 with empty base set; Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 4.6(b) (the attached tuple is an expansion map)
items.statement: For ψ_{s+1}(x₀) as in Theorem 4.6(a), the tuple (ψ_T(C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}))_{T⊆[s]} is an expansion map ψ(C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) with support {χ_{p_i(1)p_i(2)} : i ∈ [s]} ∪ {χ_a} and pointer χ_a.

items.name: Theorem 4.6(c) (ramification of the attached expansion map)
items.statement: If v ∈ 𝒫 (an odd place) ramifies in L(ψ(C, χ_a, …))/ℚ({√(p_i(1)p_i(2)) : i ∈ [s]}), then v | d₀. Every v ∈ Ω_ℚ has ramification index at most 2 in L(ψ(C, χ_a, …))/ℚ.

items.name: Theorem 4.6(d) (local shape at 2 of the attached expansion map)
items.statement: For every T ⊆ [s], φ_T(ψ(C, χ_a, …))∘i₂^* = ψ_T(C, χ_a, …)∘i₂^* is a quadratic character of G_{ℚ₂} in span{χ₅, χ_{x₀}}. If (2) ramifies in ℚ(√x₀)/ℚ, then for every T ⊊ [s] it lies in span{χ_{x₀}}.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 4.6, step 1: ψ_s(x₀) := −∑_{x≠x₀} ψ_s(x) is an unramified raw cocycle
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 4.6, ψ_s(x₀) := −∑_{x∈C, x≠x₀} ψ_s(x) (equation (4.4)) is a 1-cocycle for N(x₀) with 2^{s−1}ψ_s(x₀) = χ_a; L(ψ_s(x₀)) ⊆ ∏_{x∈C, x≠x₀} L(ψ_s(x)) (equation (4.5)); and L(ψ_s(x₀))ℚ(√x₀)/ℚ(√x₀) is unramified at all finite places (at places above p_i(2) because (ψ_s(x₀), χ_{x₀})(σ_{p_i(2)}) = id by condition (1) of Definition 4.2 and Proposition 2.3). Hence ψ_s(x₀) is a raw cocycle for N(x₀) lifting χ_a.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 4.6, step 2: reduction to splitting of p_i(1)
items.statement: A raw cocycle ψ_{s+1}(x₀) with 2ψ_{s+1}(x₀) = ψ_s(x₀) exists iff i_p(L(ψ_s(x₀))) ⊆ ℚ_p(√x₀) for every prime p ramified in ℚ(√x₀)/ℚ (equation (4.6)), by §2.3 and Proposition 2.6. This holds for p | d₀ (and p = 2 if x₀ ≡ 3 mod 4) by Lemma 4.5 and (4.5); for p = p_i(1) it reduces to p_i(1) splitting completely in L(∑_{x∈C_{p_i(2)}} ψ_s(x))/ℚ.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 4.6, step 3: the face expansion map E and splitting of p_i(2)
items.statement: For i ∈ [s] put C̃ := C_{p_i(2)}. By (4.2), Remark 4.3 and Proposition 2.9, E := (∑_{x∈C̃_{[s]−{i}−T}} ψ_{|T|+1}(x))_{T⊆[s]−{i}} is an expansion map with support {χ_{p_j(1)p_j(2)} : j ∈ [s] − {i}} ∪ {χ_a} and pointer χ_a; σ_{p_i(2)} maps to the identity under E (condition (1) of Definition 4.2), and p_i(2) splits completely in L(E) (Lemma 4.5).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 4.6, step 5: Rédei admissibility and splitting of p_i(1)
items.statement: For i ∈ [s], the 4-tuple ({χ_{p_j(1)p_j(2)} : j ∈ [s]−{i}} ∪ {χ_a}, {χ_{p_j(1)p_j(2)} : j ∈ [s]}, E, (φ_{{p_j(1)p_j(2) : j∈T}; p_i(1)p_i(2)}(𝔊))_{T⊆[s]−{i}}) with pointer vector (χ_a, χ_{p_i(1)p_i(2)}) is Rédei admissible (Definition 3.1). Theorem 3.2, with the vanishing Artin symbols of primes of a in L(φ) (condition (4)) and Art(p_i(2), L(E)/ℚ) = 0, gives that p_i(1) splits completely in L(E).

items.name: Attached raw cocycle and attached expansion map of a profitable triple
items.statement: The raw cocycle ψ_{s+1}(x₀) and the expansion map ψ(C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) produced by Theorem 4.6 are called the raw cocycle and the expansion map attached to the profitable triple.

items.name: Special integers and special cubes
items.statement: A squarefree integer d > 1 is special if it has no prime divisor ≡ 3 mod 4. A cube C (as in §4) is special if all its elements are special.

items.name: Definition 5.1 (−1-profitable triple)
items.statement: Let (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) be a special profitable triple. It is −1-profitable if (1) φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈[s]}; −1}(𝔊) exists; (2) every odd prime divisor of d₀ splits completely in M(φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈[s]}; −1}(𝔊))/ℚ; (3) (√x) ∈ 2^s·Cl(ℚ(√x))[2^{s+1}] for each x ∈ C; (4) the place (1+i) of ℚ(i) splits completely in M(φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈[s]}; −1}(𝔊))/ℚ(i). Here M(φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}}(𝔊)) = ℚ({χ_{a_i} : i ∈ [s]})·∏_{T⊊[s]} L(φ_{{a_i : i∈T}; a_{s+1}}(𝔊)).

items.name: Theorem 5.2(a) (reflection principle for ∞: membership and splitting)
items.statement: Let (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) be a −1-profitable triple. Then χ_a ∈ 2^s·Cl(ℚ(√x₀))^∨[2^{s+1}]; each odd prime p | a splits completely in M(φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈[s]}; −1}(𝔊))/ℚ; and (1+i) splits completely in M(φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈[s]}; −1}(𝔊))/ℚ(i).

items.name: Theorem 5.2(b) (reflection principle for ∞: the identity)
items.statement: Let (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) be a −1-profitable triple. Then ∑_{x∈C} ⟨(√x), χ_a⟩_{Art_{s+1}(x)} = ∑_{p|a} φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈[s]}; −1}(𝔊)(Frob(p)), where for p = 2 (if 2 | a) Frob(2) is read as the Artin symbol of Up_{ℚ(i)/ℚ}(2) (conventions after Definition 3.1).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 5.2, step: equation (5.1)
items.statement: With ψ_{s+1}(x₀) and ψ(C, χ_a, …) attached to the triple, ⟨(√x), χ_a⟩_{Art_{s+1}(x)} = ψ_{s+1}(x)(i_∞^*(Frob(∞))) for each x ∈ C, hence ∑_{x∈C} ⟨(√x), χ_a⟩_{Art_{s+1}(x)} = ψ_{[s]}(C, χ_a, …)(i_∞^*(Frob(∞))), Frob(∞) the generator of Gal(ℚ_∞^{sep}/ℚ_∞).

items.name: Ramification index e_p(F/ℚ) and residue degree f_p(F/ℚ)
items.statement: For a finite Galois F/ℚ and a prime p, e_p(F/ℚ) := #(proj(G_ℚ → Gal(F/ℚ))∘i_p^*)(I_p) and f_p(F/ℚ) := #(proj(G_ℚ → Gal(F/ℚ))∘i_p^*)(G_{ℚ_p}) / e_p(F/ℚ).

items.name: Definition 5.4 (Pellian expansion map)
items.statement: Let s ∈ ℤ_{≥1} and let a_1, …, a_{s+1} be pairwise coprime special squarefree integers > 1. An expansion map (φ_{{a_i : i∈T}; a_{s+1}})_{T⊆[s]} with support {a_1, …, a_{s+1}} and pointer a_{s+1} is Pellian if, writing φ := φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}}: (1) for each finite prime p ramified in L(φ)/ℚ, e_p(L(φ)/ℚ) = e_p(M(φ)/ℚ) = 2 and p ≢ 3 mod 4; (2) f_p(M(φ)/ℚ) = 1 for each finite prime p ramified in M(φ)/ℚ; (3) χ_{a_i} is locally trivial at 2 for all i ∈ [s]; (4) ∞ splits completely in M(φ)/ℚ; (5) φ_{{a_i : i∈T}; a_{s+1}}(σ₂(1)) = 0 for each T ⊊ [s]; (6) for each i ∈ [s], all prime divisors of a_i are unramified in L(φ_{{a_j : j∈[s]−{i}}; a_{s+1}})/ℚ.

items.name: Frobenius of Up(p) in a Pellian expansion map is well defined
items.statement: Let (φ_{{a_i : i∈T}; a_{s+1}})_{T⊆[s]} be Pellian and p | a_{s+1}. Then Up_{ℚ(√a_{s+1})/ℚ}(p) is unramified in L(φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}}) and splits completely in M(φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}}), so Frob(Up_{ℚ(√a_{s+1})/ℚ}(p)) is a well-defined element of Gal(L(φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}})/M(φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}})) ≅ 𝔽₂.
