items.name: Theorem 5.5 (the Pellian 'spin' symbol vanishes)
items.statement: Let s ∈ ℤ_{≥2}, let a_1, …, a_{s+1} be pairwise coprime special squarefree integers, and let (φ_{{a_i : i∈T}; a_{s+1}})_{T⊆[s]} be a Pellian expansion map with support {a_1, …, a_{s+1}} and pointer a_{s+1}. Then ∑_{p|a_{s+1}} φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}}(Frob(Up_{ℚ(√a_{s+1})/ℚ}(p))) = 0.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 5.5, step: the auxiliary cochain φ̃
items.statement: With K := ℚ({√a_i : i ∈ [s]−{1}}) and φ′ := φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]−{1}}; a_{s+1}}|_{G_K} (a quadratic character), the 2-cocycle θ := φ′ ∪ φ′ is locally trivial at every place of K (odd places: φ′ ramifies only where −1 is a local square; infinite places: condition (4); places above 2: condition (5) and the local fact at ℚ₂). Hence θ = dφ̃ for a continuous φ̃: G_K → 𝔽₂, and φ̃ can be chosen so that L(φ̃)/K is unramified outside S(K) ∪ Ram(φ′), where S(K) consists of the places above 2 and ∞ and a set S₁(K) of odd primes spanning Cl(K)/2Cl(K) at which χ_{a_1} is locally trivial.

items.name: Local fact at ℚ₂: characters with χ ∪ χ = 0
items.statement: The set of χ ∈ Hom_cont(G_{ℚ₂}, 𝔽₂) with χ ∪ χ = 0 in H²(G_{ℚ₂}, 𝔽₂) is the 2-dimensional subspace span{χ₂, χ₅}, which is also the space of characters vanishing at σ₂(1). Equivalently, (a, a)_{ℚ₂} = 1 iff a ∈ ⟨2, 5⟩·ℚ₂^{×2} (since (a, a) = (a, −1), (2,2) = (5,5) = 1).
items.note: QFI 6C plans 'the Gram matrix on the 𝔽₂-basis {−1, 2, 5} of ℚ_2ˣ/(ℚ_2ˣ)²' with '(−1,−1) = −1 and (2,5) = −1, with every other basis pairing +1', and 'hilbertSymbol_self'; the subspace statement is the orthogonal complement of −1 there. The identification with {χ : χ(σ₂(1)) = 0} is definitional (choice of σ₂(1) in §2).

items.name: Hasse principle for H²(G_K, 𝔽₂)
items.statement: For a number field K, a class in H²(G_K, 𝔽₂) whose restrictions to H²(G_{K_v}, 𝔽₂) vanish for all places v is zero; so a 2-cocycle θ locally trivial everywhere is dφ̃ for a continuous 1-cochain φ̃: G_K → 𝔽₂, unique up to Hom_cont(G_K, 𝔽₂).
items.note: CFT Layer 10 plans '`eq_zero_of_localInv_eq_zero` is exactness at `Br K` (Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether)'; QFI 7B plans the comparison Br(K)[2] ≅ H²(G_K, 𝔽₂) ('brauer2EquivH2'). Also used in Prop 2.16 (outside this range).

items.name: Hilbert reciprocity for H²(G_K, 𝔽₂)
items.statement: For a number field K and a class θ̃ ∈ H²(G_K, 𝔽₂), ∑_{v∈Ω_K} inv_v(θ̃) = 0. Applied to the 2-cocycle θ̃(σ, τ) := φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}}(σ)·φ′(τ) + χ_{a_1}(σ)·φ̃(τ) of G_K.
items.note: CFT Layer 10 plans '`sumLocalInv_eq_zero` is exactness in the middle'; Layer 14 plans 'ClassFieldTheory.hilbertProductFormula'; QFI 7B gives Br(K)[2] ≅ H²(G_K, 𝔽₂). θ̃ is a sum of two cup products, so the Brauer-group form (Layer 10) is the one needed. That θ̃ is a cocycle is the paper's 'quick calculation' (item below).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 5.5, step: local invariants of θ̃ away from a_1
items.statement: θ̃ is a 2-cocycle of G_K. Its local invariants: inv_v(θ̃) = 0 at every infinite place; the places of K above p | a_{s+1} contribute in total φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}}(Frob(Up_{ℚ(√a_{s+1})/ℚ}(p))) (Corollary 3.4 gives an odd number of places where φ′ is locally χ_{a_{s+1}}); inv_v(θ̃) = 0 at finite v whose residue field is a nontrivial extension of 𝔽_q (equation (5.2)); and the places above primes q ∤ a_1 with f_v = 1 contribute 0 in total (pointwise 0 if q is unramified in L(φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}}); an even number of places with equal nonzero-or-zero invariant otherwise, by Corollary 3.4).

items.name: H²(Ẑ, 𝔽₂) = 0 (unramified local classes have invariant 0)
items.statement: H²(Ẑ, 𝔽₂) = 0; hence if a 2-cocycle of G_{K_v} (v finite) is inflated from Gal(K_v^{unr}/K_v) ≅ Ẑ, its local invariant is 0.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 5.5, step: places above a_1 and the quartic character
items.statement: For q | a_1, φ′ is locally trivial at each v | q (conditions (2) and (6)), θ̃ is locally χ_{a_1} ∪ φ̃, and with the epimorphism ψ̃ := (φ̃, φ′): G_K ↠ ℤ/4ℤ ((a₁,b₁)*(a₂,b₂) = (a₁+a₂+b₁b₂, b₁+b₂)) the places above q contribute ∑_{v|q} ψ̃(Frob(v)) = (N_{K/ℚ}ψ̃)(Frob(q)). By Proposition 3.3, N_{K/ℚ}ψ̃ is a ℤ/4ℤ-character lifting χ_{a_{s+1}}, so equals (φ_{a_{s+1}; a_{s+1}}(𝔊) + χ, χ_{a_{s+1}}) (Lemma 2.18) with χ a quadratic character ramified only at primes splitting completely in ℚ(√a_1).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 5.5, step: comparison with the case s = 1
items.statement: Hilbert reciprocity for θ̃ gives ∑_{p|a_{s+1}} φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}}(Frob(Up_{ℚ(√a_{s+1})/ℚ}(p))) = ∑_{q|a_1} (φ_{a_{s+1}; a_{s+1}}(𝔊) + χ)(Frob(q)); the same analysis for φ_{a_1; a_{s+1}} (s = 1) identifies this with ∑_{p|a_{s+1}} φ_{a_1; a_{s+1}}(Frob(Up_{ℚ(√a_{s+1})/ℚ}(p))), which is 0 for s ≥ 2 because L(φ_{a_1; a_{s+1}}) ⊆ M(φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}}) and Up(p) splits completely there.

items.name: Standard-reflection setup: cube with s+1 coordinates; triples of type 1 and type 2
items.statement: Let s ∈ ℤ_{≥1}, C := {p_1(1), p_1(2)} × ⋯ × {p_{s+1}(1), p_{s+1}(2)} × {d₀} with 2s+2 distinct primes coprime to the positive squarefree d₀, such that p_i(1)p_i(2) ≡ 1 mod 8 and p_i(1)p_i(2) is a square modulo every odd prime factor of d₀ for every i ∈ [s] (the proofs use this for every i ∈ [s+1]); a | d₀; x₀ := d₀·∏_{i=1}^{s+1} p_i(1); points identified with squarefree integers. For each x ∈ C − {x₀} let ψ_{s+1}(x) be a raw cocycle for N(x). The triple (C, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}, χ_a) is of type 1 if 2^s·ψ_{s+1}(x) = χ_a for all x ∈ C − {x₀}, and of type 2 if 2^s·ψ_{s+1}(x) = χ_{π_{s+1}(x)·a} for all x ∈ C − {x₀}.

items.name: Definition 5.9 (governing triple)

items.name: Proof of Theorem 5.10, step: a ramified lift forces an unramified lift (Remark 2.7)
items.statement: Let ψ_{s+1}(x₀) := −∑_{x≠x₀} ψ_{s+1}(x), a 1-cocycle for N(x₀) (not necessarily unramified) with 2ψ_{s+1}(x₀) = ψ_s(x₀). For each odd p | x₀, (ψ_{s+1}(x₀), χ_{x₀})∘i_p^* factors through the pro-2 tame quotient; as σ_p maps to an involution (n, 1), the image of G_{ℚ_p(√x₀)} commutes with (n, 1) and so lies in N(x₀)[2]; hence ψ_s(x₀)(Frob(Up_{ℚ(√x₀)/ℚ}(p))) = 0. At 2 (if ramified) the same follows from (5.4). Hence ψ_s(x₀) = 2ψ′_{s+1}(x₀) for a raw cocycle ψ′_{s+1}(x₀).

items.name: Theorem 5.11(a) (governing triples: point gain)
items.statement: Let (C, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}, χ_a) be a governing triple. Then χ_{p_{s+1}(1)·a} ∈ 2^s·Cl(ℚ(√x₀))^∨[2^{s+1}].

items.name: Theorem 5.11(b) (governing triples: splitting of primes of b)

Then every p | b splits completely in M(φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈[s]}; p_{s+1}(1)p_{s+1}(2)}(𝔊))/ℚ and is unramified in L(φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈[s]}; p_{s+1}(1)p_{s+1}(2)}(𝔊))/ℚ.

items.name: Definition 6.1 (additive system)
items.statement: Let X_1, …, X_r be nonempty finite sets, X = X_1 × ⋯ × X_r and S ⊆ [r]. An additive system on (X, S) is a tuple (C_T, C_T^{acc}, F_T, A_T)_{T⊆S} with: C_T^{acc} ⊆ C_T ⊆ Cube(X, T) (printed reversed), F_T: C_T → A_T a function, A_T a finite 𝔽₂-vector space; C_T^{acc} = {x̄ ∈ C_T : F_T(x̄) = 0}, and C_T = {x̄ ∈ Cube(X, T) : x̄(T − {i}) ⊆ C^{acc}_{T−{i}} for all i ∈ T} for ∅ ≠ T ⊆ S; and whenever x̄₁, x̄₂, x̄₃ ∈ C_T, i ∈ T and p₁, p₂, p₃ ∈ X_i satisfy π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄₁) = π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄₂) = π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄₃), π_i(x̄₁) = (p₁, p₂), π_i(x̄₂) = (p₂, p₃), π_i(x̄₃) = (p₁, p₃), then F_T(x̄₁) + F_T(x̄₂) = F_T(x̄₃) (equation (6.1)).

Recalled from Smith, Definition 3.1 (cited as [Smith, Section 3–4]). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 6.2 (density of C_S^acc in an additive system)
items.statement: Let X_1, …, X_r be nonempty finite sets, X = ∏X_i, S ⊆ [r], and (C_T, C_T^{acc}, F_T, A_T)_{T⊆S} an additive system on (X, S) with |A_T| ≤ a for all T ⊆ S; let δ be the density of C_∅^{acc} in X. Then |C_S^{acc}| / |Cube(X, S)| ≥ δ^{2^{|S|}}·a^{−3^{|S|}}.

items.name: Lemma 6.3 (Ramsey: product sets inside dense subsets)
items.statement: Let X_1, …, X_r be nonempty finite sets, X = ∏X_i, and Y ⊆ X with |Y| ≥ δ|X|, where 2^{−r−1} > δ > 0. Let b ≥ 1 be an integer with b ≤ (log min_{i∈[r]} |X_i| / (5 log δ^{−1}))^{1/(r−1)}. Then there are Z_i ⊆ X_i with |Z_i| = b for all i ∈ [r] such that Z_1 × ⋯ × Z_r ⊆ Y.

Cited: Smith Lemma 4.1 (Smith's d, r are the paper's r, b). Needs r ≥ 2 (exponent 1/(r−1)). Mathlib 082e2d3 has only the definition SimpleGraph.zarankiewicz, no Kővári–Sós–Turán bound. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Remark 6.4 (sharpness of Lemma 6.3)
items.statement: For a random subset Y of [2^N]^r, a fixed product Z_1 × ⋯ × Z_r with |Z_i| = b lies in Y with probability (1/2)^{b^r}, and there are at most 2^{Nrb} such products; hence if b > (rN)^{1/(r−1)}, a random Y fails the conclusion of Lemma 6.3 with positive probability, so the lemma is sharp up to the constant.

items.name: Degenerate cubes, the map Σ and Add(X, S)
items.statement: Let X = X_1 × ⋯ × X_r, S ⊆ [r], V = Map(X, 𝔽₂), W = Map(Cube(X, S), 𝔽₂). x̄ ∈ Cube(X, S) is degenerate if pr₁(π_i(x̄)) = pr₂(π_i(x̄)) for some i ∈ S. Σ: V → W is the linear map ΣF(x̄) = ∑_{x∈x̄(∅)} F(x) if x̄ is not degenerate and 0 if x̄ is degenerate; Add(X, S) := im Σ. For Y ⊆ X, Σ: Map(Y, 𝔽₂) → Map(Cube(X, S), 𝔽₂) is ΣF(x̄) = ∑_{x∈x̄(∅)} F(x) if x̄ is not degenerate and x̄(∅) ⊆ Y, and 0 otherwise (printed: 'if x̄ is degenerate').

items.name: Lemma 6.5 (dimension of Add(X, S))
items.statement: Let X_1, …, X_r be finite nonempty sets, X = ∏X_i, S ⊆ [r]. Then dim_{𝔽₂} Add(X, S) = ∏_{i∈S}(|X_i| − 1)·∏_{i∈[r]−S}|X_i|.

items.name: C(𝔄) and (a, S)-acceptable additive systems
items.statement: For an additive system 𝔄 = (C_T, C_T^{acc}, F_T, A_T)_{T⊆S} on (X, S), C(𝔄) := ⋂_{i∈S} {x̄ ∈ Cube(X, S) : x̄(S − {i}) ∩ C^{acc}_{S−{i}} ≠ ∅}. 𝔄 is (a, S)-acceptable if |A_T| ≤ a for all T ⊆ S and x̄ ∈ C(𝔄) implies x̄(∅) ⊆ C_∅^{acc}.

items.name: Proposition 6.6 (Smith's combinatorial equidistribution)
items.statement: There is an absolute constant A > 0 such that: for nonempty finite X_1, …, X_r, X = ∏X_i, S ⊆ [r], a ≥ 2 and 0 < ε < a^{−1} with log min_{i∈S}|X_i| ≥ A·6^r·log ε^{−1}, there is g ∈ Add(X, S) such that for every (a, S)-acceptable additive system 𝔄 on (X, S) and every F: C_∅^{acc} → 𝔽₂ with ΣF(x̄) = g(x̄) for all x̄ ∈ C(𝔄), |C_∅^{acc}|/2 − ε|X| ≤ |F^{−1}(0)| ≤ |C_∅^{acc}|/2 + ε|X|.

items.name: K(X) and existence of cube expansion maps φ_{x̄; d}
items.statement: For nonempty finite sets X_1, …, X_r of odd primes, K(X_1 × ⋯ × X_r) is the compositum of the ℚ(√p), p ∈ ⋃_j X_j. For x̄ ∈ Cube(X, S) and an integer d ≠ 1 coprime to all elements of X, φ_{x̄; d} exists if x̄ is degenerate or if φ_{{pr₁(π_i(x̄))·pr₂(π_i(x̄)) : i ∈ S}; d}(𝔊) exists; for degenerate x̄ its field of definition is ℚ.

items.name: Lemma 6.7 (degrees of the layers M_S)
items.statement: Let r ≥ 1, X_1, …, X_r disjoint nonempty finite sets of odd primes with product X, i ∈ [r], and suppose φ_{π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄))pr₂(π_i(x̄))} exists for all x̄ ∈ Cube(X, [r]). For S ⊆ [r] − {i} let M_S := K(X)·∏_{x̄∈Cube(X, S∪{i})} L(φ_{π_S(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄))pr₂(π_i(x̄))}). Then for all 0 ≤ j ≤ r − 2, log₂[∏_{S⊆[r]−{i}, |S|=j+1} M_S : ∏_{S′⊆[r]−{i}, |S′|=j} M_{S′}] = ∑_{S⊆[r]−{i}, |S|=j+1} ∏_{k∈S∪{i}} (|X_k| − 1).

'very similar to [Smith, Proposition 2.4]'. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Basis(X, T) and the commutator operator β_j
items.statement: Enumerate X_k = {p_{k,1}, …, p_{k,|X_k|}} and set T_{k,l} = {p_{k,l}, p_{k,l+1}} (l ∈ [|X_k| − 1]). For T ⊆ [r] − {i}, Basis(X, T) is the set of x̄ ∈ Cube(X, T ∪ {i}) with {pr₁(π_k(x̄)), pr₂(π_k(x̄))} = T_{k,l} for some l, for every k ∈ T ∪ {i}; x̄₁ ∼ x̄₂ if these pairs agree as sets for all k. For φ ∈ Map(G_{M_j}, 𝔽₂) and σ₁, …, σ_{j+2} ∈ G_ℚ, β_jφ := φ([σ₁, [σ₂, [⋯[σ_{j+1}, σ_{j+2}]]]]), well defined since Gal(M_j/ℚ) has nilpotency class j + 1 (M_j := ∏_{|S′|=j} M_{S′}).

items.name: Proof of Lemma 6.7, step: β_j formula and independence of the basis characters
items.statement: For S ⊆ [r] − {i} with |S| = j + 1 and x̄ ∈ Basis(X, S), writing φ = φ_{π_S(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄))pr₂(π_i(x̄))}: φ([σ, τ]) = dφ(σ, τ) + dφ(τ, σ) on G_{M_j}, and β_jφ = ∑_{f} ∏_{k=1}^{j+2} χ_{pr₁(π_{f(k)}(x̄))pr₂(π_{f(k)}(x̄))}(σ_k), the sum over bijections f: [j+2] → S ∪ {i} with f(j+1) = i or f(j+2) = i. Since the (j+2)-linear maps ∏_m χ_{p_{k_m,l_m}p_{k_m,l_m+1}}(σ_m) are linearly independent, the characters {φ_x̄ : x̄ ∈ Basis(X, S)/∼, |S| = j+1} are independent and span Gal(M_{j+1}/M_j)^∨.

items.name: Lemma 6.8(a) (degree of M_∘(X))
items.statement: Let r ≥ 1, X_1, …, X_r disjoint nonempty finite sets of odd primes with product X, i ∈ [r], and assume φ_{π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄))pr₂(π_i(x̄))} exists for all x̄ ∈ Cube(X, [r]). With M_∘(X) := K(X)·∏_{S⊊[r]−{i}} ∏_{x̄∈Cube(X, S∪{i})} L(φ_{π_S(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄))pr₂(π_i(x̄))}), [M_∘(X) : K(X)] = ∏_{∅⊊S⊊[r]−{i}} 2^{∏_{j∈S∪{i}}(|X_j| − 1)} (equation (6.3)).

items.name: Lemma 6.8(b) (disjointness of M_∘ for boxes meeting in one point per coordinate)
items.statement: With X as in Lemma 6.8(a), let Y_1, …, Y_r be disjoint nonempty finite sets of odd primes with product Y such that φ_{π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄))pr₂(π_i(x̄))} exists for all x̄ ∈ Cube(Y, [r]), |X_j ∩ Y_j| = 1 for all j ∈ [r] and X_j ∩ Y_k = ∅ for j ≠ k. Then M_∘(X) ∩ M_∘(Y) = ℚ(√p_1, …, √p_r), p_j the unique element of X_j ∩ Y_j.

items.name: Lemma 6.9 (Gal(M/M_∘) ≅ Add(X, [r]))
items.statement: Let r ≥ 2, X_1, …, X_r disjoint nonempty finite sets of odd primes with product X, i ∈ [r], and assume φ_{π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄))pr₂(π_i(x̄))} exists for all x̄ ∈ Cube(X, [r]). With M_∘ as in Lemma 6.8 and M := K(X)·∏_{x̄∈Cube(X, [r])} L(φ_{π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄))pr₂(π_i(x̄))}), the map sending σ ∈ Gal(M/M_∘) to g_σ: x̄ ↦ φ_{π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄))pr₂(π_i(x̄))}(σ) is a group isomorphism Gal(M/M_∘) ≅ Add(X, [r]); in particular |Gal(M/M_∘)| = 2^{∏_{j∈[r]}(|X_j| − 1)}.

items.name: Lemma 6.10(a) (constant pointer d: degree of the top layer)
items.statement: Let r ≥ 1, X_1, …, X_r disjoint nonempty finite sets of odd primes, X = ∏X_i, d ≠ 1 squarefree coprime to all primes in X, and suppose φ_{x̄; d} exists for all x̄ ∈ Cube(X, [r]) (and, as needed for M_∘(X), φ_{π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄))pr₂(π_i(x̄))} exists for all i and x̄). With M_∘(X) := K(X)·∏_{i∈[r]}∏_{x̄∈Cube(X,[r])} L(φ_{π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄))pr₂(π_i(x̄))}) · ∏_{T⊊[r]}∏_{x̄∈Cube(X,T)} L(φ_{x̄; d}) and M(X) := M_∘(X)·∏_{x̄∈Cube(X,[r])} L(φ_{x̄; d}), [M(X) : M_∘(X)] = 2^{∏_{j∈[r]}(|X_j| − 1)}.

items.name: Lemma 6.10(b) (constant pointer d: degree of M_∘(X))

items.name: Proof of Lemma 6.10, step: the pointer relation
items.statement: For x̄ ∈ Cube(X, S) with |S| ≥ 1, ∑_{i∈S} φ_{π_{S−{i}}(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄))pr₂(π_i(x̄))} = χ_{{pr₁(π_j(x̄))pr₂(π_j(x̄)) : j ∈ S}} (product of the quadratic characters), which is why i ≠ max(S) in Lemma 6.10(b); via β_{|S|−2} there are no further relations, because for every ∅ ⊊ T ⊊ S some bijection f: [|S|] → S has exactly one of f(|S|−1), f(|S|) in T.
