items.name: Standing convention for §§7–8: product spaces of primes read as squarefree integers
items.statement: X₁, …, X_r are pairwise disjoint, non-empty sets of primes, every prime ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4), and X = X₁ × ⋯ × X_r. The map X → 𝒟, (x₁, …, x_r) ↦ x₁⋯x_r, is injective, and an element of X is identified with the squarefree integer x₁⋯x_r. Here 𝒟 is the set of squarefree d > 0 all of whose prime divisors are ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4), and 𝒟(N) = {d ∈ 𝒟 : d < N}.
items.note: Notation only. 𝒟 and 𝒟(N) are from §1 (TeX 160). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: N-nice elements of 𝒟 (Definition 7.1)
items.statement: Let N ≥ 10^1000 and d ∈ 𝒟, with prime divisors p₁ < ⋯ < p_r. Put D₁ := e^{(log log N)^{1/10}} and C₀ := √(log log log N). Then d is N-nice if all three hold: (1) p_i > D₁ implies 2p_i < p_{i+1}; (2) (7.1) |½ log log p_i − i| < C₀^{1/5} · max(i, C₀)^{4/5} for all 1 ≤ i < r/3; (3) there is an i with r^{1/2}/2 < i < r/2 and log p_i ≥ (log log p_i)² · log log log N · Σ_{j=1}^{i−1} log p_j.
items.note: Condition (1) is vacuous for i = r. Condition (3) is used only in §8, where it provides k_gap (8.3). Adapted from [CKMP, §4] and [Smith, §5]. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: 𝒟_r(N) and ω(d)
items.statement: ω(d) is the number of distinct prime divisors of d, and 𝒟_r(N) := {d ∈ 𝒟(N) : ω(d) = r}.
items.note: Printed inside Definition 7.1. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 7.2(a): few d ∈ 𝒟(N) have ω(d) far from ½ log log N, (7.2)
items.statement: Σ_{r : |r − ½ log log N| ≥ (log log N)^{2/3}} |𝒟_r(N)| ≪ |𝒟(N)| / (log log N)^{1/100}.
items.note: The source prints a union ⋃ in front of the cardinalities |𝒟_r(N)|. The left side is a sum. The proof is one line ('follows from the Erdős–Kac theorem'). Turán–Kubilius for ω restricted to 𝒟 already gives the bound, with exponent 1/3 in place of 1/100. ProbabilisticAndMetricNumberTheory:PM.1 plans 'source-scoped Hardy-Ramanujan/Erdos-Kac theorems' for ω on all integers. No stage plans this restricted form, whose mean ½ log log N comes from the density ½ of primes ≡ 1 mod 4. Route: a source of ProbabilisticAndMetricNumberTheory PM.1 (normal order and limit laws).

items.name: Theorem 7.2(b): Sathe–Selberg-type bounds for |𝒟_r(N)|, (7.3)
items.statement: For every A > 0 there are C₁, C₂, N₀ > 0 such that for all integers 1 ≤ r ≤ A log log N and all N ≥ N₀: C₁ · (N / log N) · (½ log log N)^{r−1} / (r − 1)! ≤ |𝒟_r(N)| ≤ C₂ · (N / log N) · (½ log log N)^{r−1} / (r − 1)!.
items.note: Cited from [CKMP, p. 13]. This is a Sathe–Selberg/Selberg–Delange count for squarefree integers with r prime factors, all ≡ 1 or 2 mod 4. The source leaves r ≥ 1 implicit. Route: a source of AnalyticNumberTheory (AN.2 exceptional zeros and uniform prime number theorems, AN.4 effective Chebotarev and Dedekind zeta functions, AN.5 mean values of multiplicative functions).

items.name: Theorem 7.2(c): almost every d with typical ω(d) is N-nice
items.statement: If r satisfies (7.4) |r − ½ log log N| < (log log N)^{2/3}, then |{d ∈ 𝒟_r(N) : d is not N-nice}| / |𝒟_r(N)| ≪ e^{−(log log log N)^{1/4}}.
items.note: Cited from [CKMP, Theorem 4.1], based on [Smith, Theorem 5.4]. The source gives no proof. The inputs are the Poisson/Selberg–Delange model for the prime factors of a typical d. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Prebox (Definition 7.3)
items.statement: A prebox is a pair (X, P), where P, X₁, …, X_r are pairwise disjoint sets of primes, all ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4), and X = X₁ × ⋯ × X_r, such that there are reals 2 < s₁ < t₁ < s₂ < t₂ < ⋯ < s_r < t_r with X_i ⊆ (s_i, t_i] for all i ∈ [r] and P ⊆ (1, s₁].
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The isomorphism ι : 𝔽₂ → {±1}
items.statement: ι is the unique group isomorphism from (𝔽₂, +) to ({±1}, ·), namely ι(0) = 1 and ι(1) = −1.
items.locator: §7.2, running text before Definition 7.4, p. 60 (arXiv v1)
items.note: A one-line definition. No named Mathlib equivalence was checked, so this is not claimed as library. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Symbol index sets M_r, M_{r,P} and the fibre X(a) (Definition 7.4)
items.statement: Let (X, P) be a prebox. Put M_r := {(i, j) : i, j ∈ [r], i < j} and M_{r,P} := [r] × P. For subsets ℳ_r ⊆ M_r and ℳ_{r,P} ⊆ M_{r,P} and a map a : ℳ_r ⊔ ℳ_{r,P} → 𝔽₂, X(a) is the set of (x₁, …, x_r) ∈ X with (x_i/x_j) = ι(a(i, j)) for all (i, j) ∈ ℳ_r and (x_i/p) = ι(a(i, p)) for all (i, p) ∈ ℳ_{r,P}. Here (·/·) is the Legendre symbol.
items.note: P may contain 2, and then (x_i/2) must be read as the Kronecker symbol. Since s₁ > 2, no X_i contains 2. For primes ≡ 1 mod 4 the symbol is symmetric by quadratic reciprocity, and the source uses this silently (see the reciprocity item). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Exceptional set 𝒮(c), its enumeration d₁, d₂, … and the constant c_Landau (Definition 7.5)
items.statement: For a real 0 < c < 0.5, 𝒮(c) is the set of squarefree integers d such that L(s, χ_d) has a real zero s with 1 − c/log(|d| + 4) ≤ s ≤ 1. List 𝒮(c) as d₁, d₂, … with |d₁| ≤ |d₂| ≤ ⋯. A constant c_Landau > 0 is fixed for the rest of the paper such that |d_i|² ≤ |d_{i+1}| for all i. It exists by the Landau item.
items.note: The source says 𝒮(c) is conjecturally empty. Route: a source of AnalyticNumberTheory (AN.2 exceptional zeros and uniform prime number theorems, AN.4 effective Chebotarev and Dedekind zeta functions, AN.5 mean values of multiplicative functions).

items.name: Landau's theorem on the repulsion of exceptional real zeros
items.statement: There is c_Landau > 0 such that, if 𝒮(c_Landau) = {d₁, d₂, …} is listed with |d₁| ≤ |d₂| ≤ ⋯, then |d_i|² ≤ |d_{i+1}| for all i.
items.note: Stated without proof ('By Landau's theorem'). It follows from Landau's bound: two distinct real primitive characters χ₁, χ₂ cannot both have real zeros > 1 − c/log(|d₁d₂|). AN.2 plans only that 'possible exceptional zeros are labelled', not this statement. Route: a source of AnalyticNumberTheory (AN.2 exceptional zeros and uniform prime number theorems, AN.4 effective Chebotarev and Dedekind zeta functions, AN.5 mean values of multiplicative functions).

items.name: Siegel-free preboxes
items.statement: A prebox (X, P) is Siegel-free above a real t > 0 if there are no index i with |d_i| > t and no x ∈ X such that d_i divides x · ∏_{p∈P} p. Here d₁, d₂, … enumerate 𝒮(c_Landau).
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 7.6: Legendre symbols equidistribute in a prebox when the conditions to P sit on large primes
items.statement: Let c₁, …, c₈ > 0 with c₃ > 1, c₅ > 3, c₆ > 1 and 1/8 > c₈ + (c₇ log 2)/2 + 1/c₁ + c₂c₄/2. There is an effectively computable A > 0, depending only on c₁, …, c₈, such that the following holds. Let (X, P) be a prebox with s₁ > A that is Siegel-free above some t with s₁ > t > A. Let ℳ_r ⊆ M_r, ℳ_{r,P} ⊆ M_{r,P} and a : ℳ_r ⊔ ℳ_{r,P} → 𝔽₂. Let 1 ≤ k ≤ r be an integer such that (i, p) ∈ ℳ_{r,P} implies i > k. Assume (7.5): X_i = {p ∈ (s_i, t_i] : p ≡ 1 mod 4 and (p/p′) = ι(a(i, p′)) for all (i, p′) ∈ ℳ_{r,P}} for all i > k. Assume also (i) |P| ≤ log t_i − i for all i ∈ [r]; (ii) t₁ > r^{c₁} and t_k < e^{t₁^{c₂}}; (iii) |X_i| ≥ 2^{c₃ i} · t_i / (log t_i)^{c₄} for all i ∈ [r]; (iv) if k ≠ r, then t_{k+1} > max(e^{(log t₁)^{c₅}}, e^{t^{c₆}}); (v) k ≤ ⌈c₇ log t₁⌉, and t_j > e^{(log t_i)^{c₅}} for all i ≤ r and all j with i + c₇ log t_i ≤ j ≤ r. Then ||X(a)| − |X|/2^{|ℳ_r|}| ≤ r|X| / (t₁^{c₈+1/c₁} · 2^{|ℳ_r|}) ≤ |X| / (t₁^{c₈} · 2^{|ℳ_r|}).
items.note: Directly based on [Smith, Prop. 6.3]. Effectivity of A uses an effective lower bound for Siegel zeros (Watkins). The proof is by induction on r, moving x₁ into P; see the three key-step items below. The second inequality uses (ii) and c₁ > 8. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Key step in Proposition 7.6: the split X_i(a, x₁) is balanced for i > k, (7.6)
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 7.6 with r > 1, for x₁ ∈ X₁ and 2 ≤ i ≤ r put X_i(a, x₁) := {p ∈ X_i : (x₁/p) = ι(a(1, i))} if (1, i) ∈ ℳ_r, and X_i(a, x₁) := X_i otherwise. If A is large enough, then ||X_i(a, x₁)| − ½|X_i|| ≤ |X_i|/t₁ for every i > k with (1, i) ∈ ℳ_r.
items.note: Proof: the effective Chebotarev bound (7.7) in K = ℚ(√−1, √x₁, √p : p ∈ P). This uses (7.8) 1 − β ≫ (log t_i)^{−1/2}, from the Siegel-free hypothesis, (iv) and c₆ > 1. It also uses (7.9) log|D| ≪ (|P| + 2) log t₁ ≪ (log t_i)^{2/c₅}, from (i) and (iv), together with [K:ℚ] ≪ t₁ and c₅ > 3. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Prime number theorem for a quadratic character, uniform in the conductor, with an exceptional-zero term (7.7)
items.statement: Let D ≠ 1 be squarefree, let χ be the quadratic character of Gal(ℚ(√D)/ℚ), and let β be the exceptional real zero of L(s, χ_D) if there is one. Then Σ_{s_i < p < t_i} χ(Frob_p) ≪ t_i^β + t_i · exp(−c log t_i / (√(log t_i) + log|D|)) · (log t_i|D|)⁴ for an absolute constant c > 0. The t_i^β term is absent when there is no exceptional zero.
items.note: Cited as [IK, Theorem 5.13]. AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4 plans to 'Connect … Hecke characters and completed L-functions to the analytic class-number formula and Chebotarev', and Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layer 14 plans natural density. Neither plans an error term uniform in the conductor. AN.2 plans the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions only for a fixed modulus ('specifies whether modulus is fixed'). This is the analytic input the brief calls 'Chebotarev'. No stage plans it. The source uses no Siegel–Walfisz theorem in §§7–8. Route: a source of AnalyticNumberTheory (AN.2 exceptional zeros and uniform prime number theorems, AN.4 effective Chebotarev and Dedekind zeta functions, AN.5 mean values of multiplicative functions).

items.name: Effective lower bound for an exceptional zero
items.statement: For every ε > 0 there is an effectively computable c(ε) > 0 such that, if D ≠ 1 is squarefree and β is a real zero of L(s, χ_D), then 1 − β ≥ c(ε) |D|^{−1/2−ε}.
items.note: Stated without reference. It follows from the class number formula and h ≥ 1; it is weaker than Siegel's ineffective bound but effective. This is what makes A in Propositions 7.6 and 7.8 effective (Watkins). Route: a source of AnalyticNumberTheory (AN.2 exceptional zeros and uniform prime number theorems, AN.4 effective Chebotarev and Dedekind zeta functions, AN.5 mean values of multiplicative functions).

items.name: Key step in Proposition 7.6: few bad x₁, (7.10)
items.statement: Choose reals c₉, c₁₀ with c₉ + c₁₀ < 1/4 − c₂c₄, c₉ > c₇ log 2 + c₈ + 1/c₁ and c₁₀ > c₈ + 1/c₁; these exist by the hypothesis on c₁, …, c₈. Call x₁ ∈ X₁ bad if ||X_i(a, x₁)| − ½|X_i|| ≥ |X_i|/t₁^{c₁₀} for some (1, i) ∈ ℳ_r (by (7.6) such i satisfy i ≤ k). Let X₁^bad be the set of bad x₁. Then |X₁^bad| ≤ k|X₁| / t₁^{c₉}.
items.note: Proof: the bilinear Legendre-symbol estimate (7.11) with ε < 1/4 − c₂c₄ − c₉ − c₁₀. The displayed intermediate inequality has a sign slip in the exponent of t₁. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Bilinear Legendre-symbol estimate from the large sieve (Smith, Prop. 6.6), and (7.11)
items.statement: For every ε > 0 and all sets of odd primes X₁ ⊆ (s₁, t₁] and X_i ⊆ (s_i, t_i] with t₁ < s_i: Σ_{x₁∈X₁} |Σ_{x_i∈X_i} (x₁/x_i)| ≪_ε t_i · t₁^{3/4+ε}. Under hypotheses (ii) and (iii) of Proposition 7.6 (with i ≤ k), this gives (7.11): Σ_{x₁∈X₁} |Σ_{x_i∈X_i} (x₁/x_i)| ≪_ε |X₁| · |X_i| / t₁^{1/4 − c₂c₄ − ε}.
items.note: Cited as 'the large sieve', see [Smith, Prop. 6.6]. SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.2 plans 'additive and multiplicative large-sieve inequalities … bilinear decompositions'. The classical multiplicative large sieve plus Cauchy–Schwarz gives the bound only when t_i ≥ t₁^{3/2}. For t₁ < t_i < t₁^{3/2} one needs Heath-Brown's large sieve for quadratic characters, and no stage plans it; the only 'Heath-Brown' hit in the atlas is his prime identity in ES.4. The bound is used again, in iterated form, in §8.4 ('We will now repeatedly apply the large sieve'). Route: a source of SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.2 (large sieve and bilinear sums).

items.name: Key step in Proposition 7.6: the induction that moves x₁ into P, (7.12)–(7.16)
items.statement: Split ||X(a)| − |X|/2^{|ℳ_r|}| by the value of x₁ (7.12). For bad x₁, apply the induction hypothesis to the prebox (X₂ × ⋯ × X_k × X_{k+1}(a, x₁) × ⋯ × X_r(a, x₁), P ∪ {x₁}). Take k_new ≥ k − 1 minimal with t_{k_new+2} > max(e^{(log t₂)^{c₅}}, e^{t^{c₆}}), and k_new = r − 1 if there is none. This gives (7.13): Σ_{x ∈ X(a), π₁(x) ∈ X₁^bad} 1 ≤ k · 2^{−|ℳ_r|+k+1} · |X|/t₁^{c₉} ≤ |X| / (t₁^{c₈+1/c₁} · 2^{|ℳ_r|+2}). For good x₁, apply it to X(x₁) := X₂(a, x₁) × ⋯ × X_r(a, x₁) with P ∪ {x₁}. With M the number of pairs (1, j) ∈ ℳ_r, this gives (7.14) ||X(x₁)(a)| − |X(x₁)|/2^{|ℳ_r|−M}| ≤ (r − 1)|X(x₁)| / (t₁^{c₈+1/c₁} 2^{|ℳ_r|−M}) and (7.15) |2^M|X(x₁)| − |X|/|X₁|| ≤ |X| / (100 t₁^{c₈+1/c₁}|X₁|). Hence (7.16): the good part is within (r − ¼)|X| / (t₁^{c₈+1/c₁} 2^{|ℳ_r|}) of |X|/2^{|ℳ_r|}.
items.note: (7.15) uses r < t₁^{1/c₁}, k ≤ ⌈c₇ log t₁⌉ and c₁₀ > c₈ + 1/c₁. When k_new > k − 1, the new prebox violates the hypothesis '(i, p) ∈ ℳ_{r,P} ⇒ i > k_new'. The fix is to drop those pairs, which the trimmed X_i already satisfy. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Quadratic reciprocity for a prime ≡ 1 (mod 4), used silently in Propositions 7.6 and 7.8
items.statement: If p and q are primes with p ≡ 1 (mod 4) and q ≠ 2, then (q/p) = (p/q). The source uses this to identify X_i(a, x₁) = {p ∈ X_i : (x₁/p) = ι(a(1, i))} with a set of the form (7.5) in the prime p′ = x₁, and to treat the Legendre symbols between primes ≡ 1 mod 4 as symmetric.
items.note: Checked at Mathlib 082e2d3: legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity_one_mod_four (hp : p % 4 = 1) (hq : q ≠ 2) : legendreSym q p = legendreSym p q. The same law with a Kronecker symbol at 2 would be needed if x₁ = 2 or 2 ∈ P. ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.1 plans 'quadratic reciprocity'.

items.name: Permutations 𝒫_r, 𝒫_r(k) and their action σ(a) on symbol maps
items.statement: 𝒫_r is the set of permutations of [r], and 𝒫_r(k) := {σ ∈ 𝒫_r : σ(i) = i for all i > k}. For a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,P} → 𝔽₂ set a(j, i) := a(i, j) for j > i, and define σ(a)(i, j) := a(σ⁻¹(i), σ⁻¹(j)) and σ(a)(i, p) := a(σ⁻¹(i), p).
items.locator: §7.2, running text after Proposition 7.6, p. 65 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Truncated fibres X^trun_{k₀,k₁}(σ, a) and the count C(k₀, k₁)
items.statement: For integers k₁ ≥ k₀ ≥ 0, X^trun_{k₀,k₁}(σ, a) is the set of x = (x₁, …, x_r) ∈ X such that (x_i/x_j) = ι(a(σ⁻¹(i), σ⁻¹(j))) for all i, j ∈ [k₁] with σ⁻¹(i) < σ⁻¹(j) and min(i, j) ≤ k₀, and (x_i/p) = ι(a(σ⁻¹(i), p)) for all (i, p) ∈ [k₁] × P. The number of such pairs {i, j} is C(k₀, k₁) := ½(k₀² − k₀) + k₀(k₁ − k₀), which does not depend on σ.
items.locator: §7.2, running text before Lemma 7.7, pp. 65–66 (arXiv v1)
items.note: X^trun imposes the conditions of σ(a) that involve the small primes. Compare [Smith, Prop. 6.7]. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Lemma 7.7: second moment of the number of admissible permutations
items.statement: Let (X, P) be a prebox and let 0 ≤ k₀ ≤ k₁ ≤ k₂ ≤ r be integers with 2^{k₀+|P|+1} k₁² < k₂. Then for every x ∈ X: Σ_{a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,P} → 𝔽₂} (k₂!/2^{C(k₀,k₁)+k₁|P|} − |{σ ∈ 𝒫_r(k₂) : x ∈ X^trun_{k₀,k₁}(σ, a)}|)² ≤ (2^{k₀+|P|+1} k₁²/k₂) · 2^{−2C(k₀,k₁) − 2k₁|P| + |M_r ⊔ M_{r,P}|} · (k₂!)².
items.note: Purely combinatorial. The proof computes the first moment (7.17) exactly and bounds the second moment (7.18) via I_{k₁,k₂}(σ₁, σ₂), S(σ₁, σ₂), T(σ₁, σ₂) and a geometric series. There is a factorial typo in the count of injections. Compare [Smith, Prop. 6.7]. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 7.8: equidistribution of Legendre symbols after averaging over permutations of the small indices
items.statement: Let c₁, …, c₁₂ > 0 with c₃ > 1, c₅ > 3, c₆ > 1, 1/8 > c₈ + (c₇ log 2)/2 + 1/c₁ + c₂c₄/2, c₁₀ log 2 + 2c₁₁ + 2c₁₂ < 1 and c₁₁ + c₁₂ < c₉. There is an effectively computable A > 0, depending only on c₁, …, c₁₂, such that the following holds. Let (X, P) be a prebox in which each X_i is the set of primes ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4) in (s_i, t_i]. Let 0 ≤ k₀ < k₁ < k₂ ≤ r be integers with k₂ > A, and let (X, P) be Siegel-free above some t with s_{k₀+1} > t > A. Assume (i) |P| ≤ log t_i − i for k₀ < i ≤ r; (ii) t_{k₀+1} > r^{c₁} and t_{k₁} < e^{t_{k₀+1}^{c₂}}; (iii) |X_i| ≥ 2^{|P|+c₃ i} · k₂^{c₉} · t_i / (log t_i)^{c₄} for k₀ < i ≤ r; (iv) t_{k₁+1} > max(e^{(log t_{k₀+1})^{c₅}}, e^{t^{c₆}}); (v) k₁ − k₀ ≤ ⌈c₇ log t_{k₀+1}⌉, and t_j > e^{(log t_i)^{c₅}} for all k₀ < i ≤ r and all j with i + c₇ log t_i ≤ j ≤ r; (vi) k₀ + |P| < c₁₀ log k₂ and log k₁ < c₁₁ log k₂. Then Σ_{a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,P} → 𝔽₂} |k₂! · |X| / 2^{|M_r ⊔ M_{r,P}|} − Σ_{σ∈𝒫_r(k₂)} |X(σ(a))|| ≤ k₂! · |X| · (k₂^{−c₁₂} + t_{k₀+1}^{−c₈}).
items.note: Directly based on [Smith, Theorem 6.4]. The proof starts by reducing to |X_i| = 1 for i ≤ k₀. Both applications (Theorem 7.13 and (8.10)) use boxes whose first k factors are singletons, so the hypothesis that each X_i is a full interval of primes is needed only for i > k₀. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Key steps in Proposition 7.8: trimmed factors, the good case and bad pairs, (7.19)–(7.23)
items.statement: Reduce to X_i = {x_i} for i ∈ [k₀]. Lemma 7.7 and Cauchy–Schwarz give (7.19): the replacement of Σ_σ |X(σ(a))| by Σ_σ |X^trun_{k₀,k₁}(σ, a)| / 2^{|M_r ⊔ M_{r,P}| − C(k₀,k₁) − k₁|P|} costs at most k₂!|X| / (2k₂^{c₁₂}). For i > k₀ let X_i^trim(σ, a) := {x_i ∈ X_i : (x_i/p) = ι(a(σ⁻¹(i), p)) for all p ∈ P, and (x_i/x_j) = ι(a(σ⁻¹(i), σ⁻¹(j))) for all j ∈ [k₀]}. The Chebotarev density theorem gives (7.20): ||X_i^trim(σ, a)| − |X_i|/2^{k₀+|P|}| ≤ |X_i|/t_{k₀+1} for all i > k₁. If |X′_i| ≥ |X_{i+k₀}| / (2^{k₀+|P|} k₂^{c₉}) for all i, where X′ is X^trun viewed as a prebox with P′ = P ∪ {x₁, …, x_{k₀}}, then Proposition 7.6 applied to (X^trim_{k₀+1} × ⋯ × X^trim_r, P′) gives (7.21). Otherwise (σ, a) is bad at some i ∈ [k₁ − k₀]; grouping a into the ≤ 2^{k₀+|P|} classes of ∼_{σ,j} gives (7.22), and the good pairs give (7.23).
items.note: The displayed application of Proposition 7.6 has the wrong power of 2 on its right-hand side. (7.20) is the effective Chebotarev bound of (7.7) again. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The Siegel threshold D_Siegel
items.statement: D_Siegel := e^{(log log N)^{1/100}} (to be compared with D₁ = e^{(log log N)^{1/10}} from Definition 7.1).
items.locator: §7.3, running text before Definition 7.9, p. 71 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: (N, k, r)-boxes X(𝐭) (Definition 7.9)
items.statement: Let N ≥ 10^1000, let r be a positive integer, let 0 ≤ k ≤ r, and let C_compr be a real with 100 ≤ C_compr ≤ (log N)^100. Let 𝐭 = (p₁, …, p_k, s_{k+1}, …, s_r), where the p_i are primes ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4) and the s_j are reals, with p₁ < ⋯ < p_k < D₁ ≤ s_{k+1} < ⋯ < s_r and s_i < (2/3) s_{i+1} for all k < i < r. Then X(𝐭) := X₁ × ⋯ × X_r with X_i = {p_i} for 1 ≤ i ≤ k, and X_i the set of primes ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4) in (s_i, s_i(1 + 1/C_compr)] for k < i ≤ r. A product space X is an (N, k, r)-box if X = X(𝐭) for some 𝐭 and X ⊆ 𝒟(N).
items.note: The source asserts that for N large the X_i are disjoint and non-empty. Non-emptiness fails near the top of the allowed range of C_compr; it holds for the later choice C_compr = (log log N)^{50}. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Excellent boxes
items.statement: An (N, k, r)-box X is excellent if some d ∈ X is N-nice and {α ∏_{i∈S} π_i(x) : x ∈ X, S ⊆ [r], α ∈ {1, −1}, |α ∏_{i∈S} π_i(x)| > D_Siegel} ∩ 𝒮(c_Landau) = ∅.
items.note: An excellent box is Siegel-free above D_Siegel (with P = ∅). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 7.10: reduction from 𝒟_r(N) to boxes
items.statement: Let N ≥ 10^1000 be real and let r be a positive integer satisfying (7.4). Let V, W ⊆ 𝒟_r(N), let δ be a real number (not introduced in the source), and let ε > 0 with |W| > (1 − ε)|𝒟_r(N)|. Suppose ||V ∩ X| − δ|X|| ≤ ε|X| for every integer k and every (N, k, r)-box X with X ∩ W ≠ ∅. Then |V| = δ|𝒟_r(N)| + O((ε + e^{−(log log log N)^{1/4}}) · |𝒟_r(N)| + |𝒟_r(N) − 𝒟_r(N / (1 + 1/C_compr)^r)|).
items.note: This is [Smith, Prop. 6.9]; the proof is closer to Watkins. Proof: the boxes with s_i on the grid e_i = D₁(1 + 1/C_compr)^i that meet W are pairwise disjoint. They cover every d ∈ 𝒟_r(N) except those that fail the first nice condition, lie outside W, or satisfy d ≥ N(1 + 1/C_compr)^{−r}. Theorem 7.2(c) bounds the non-nice d. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Remark 7.11: the boundary layer is small
items.statement: If (log N)^{1−ε} ≥ C_compr ≥ r^{1+ε}, then |𝒟_r(N) − 𝒟_r(N(1 + 1/C_compr)^{−r})| ≪_ε |𝒟_r(N)| / r^ε.
items.note: Stated without proof ('one can show'), and not used later: the paper uses the trivial bound in the next item. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Remark 7.11: the trivial boundary bound and the asymptotic for |𝒟(N)|
items.statement: Summed over r, the boundary layers satisfy Σ_r |𝒟_r(N) − 𝒟_r(N(1 + 1/C_compr)^{−r})| ≤ |𝒟(N)| − |𝒟(N(1 + 1/C_compr)^{−r_max})|, where r_max is the largest r considered; the source writes r here. Moreover |𝒟(N)| = C · N / √(log N) · (1 + O(1/log N)) for some constant C > 0.
items.note: The asymptotic is 'the classical asymptotic formula', a Landau–Ramanujan-type count for squarefree integers whose prime factors are all ≡ 1 or 2 mod 4. No stage plans it; the atlas search for Landau–Ramanujan and sums of two squares finds nothing relevant. Route: a source of AnalyticNumberTheory (AN.2 exceptional zeros and uniform prime number theorems, AN.4 effective Chebotarev and Dedekind zeta functions, AN.5 mean values of multiplicative functions).

items.name: Fixed choice C_compr := (log log N)^{50}
items.statement: From §7.3 on, C_compr := (log log N)^{50}. Theorem 7.10 holds equally with any congruence conditions on the radicands, such as odd or even radicands, so all proofs also work when ordering by discriminant.
items.locator: §7.3, running text after Remark 7.11, p. 73 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Proposition 7.12: boxes that touch a large Siegel modulus are rare
items.statement: Let N ≥ t ≥ 10^1000 be reals and let r be a positive integer satisfying (7.4). Let f₁, f₂, f₃, … be squarefree integers > t with f_{i+1} > f_i². Put W(f_i) := {x ∈ 𝒟_r(N) : there are an (N, k, r)-box X and x′ ∈ X with f_i | x′ and x ∈ X}. If log N ≥ (log t)³, then |⋃_{i≥1} W(f_i)| ≪ |𝒟_r(N)| / log t.
items.note: Compare [Smith, Prop. 6.10]. It is applied with f_i = |d_i| > D_Siegel and t = D_Siegel. The proof uses (7.3) and splits at f_i < N^{2/3}. It contains the slip f_i > t^{2^i} for t^{2^{i−1}}. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: D_{2,n} and P_Sym(r, n)
items.statement: D_{2,n} := {d ∈ 𝒟 : rk₄ Cl(ℚ(√d)) = n}, where Cl is the narrow class group and rk₄ A = dim_{𝔽₂} 2A[4]. P_Sym(r, n) is the probability that a uniformly random symmetric r × r matrix over 𝔽₂ has kernel of dimension n.
items.locator: §7.3, running text before Theorem 7.13, p. 74 (arXiv v1)
items.note: rk₄ (and rk_{2^k} in §8) is never defined in the source; the standard meaning is assumed. Route: a source of ArithmeticStatistics (ST.0 families, ST.3 class groups, ST.5 random-matrix distributions).

items.name: Theorem 7.13: the 4-rank distribution in 𝒟, with an effective error term
items.statement: For every real N ≥ 10^1000 and every integer n ≥ 0: |D_{2,n} ∩ 𝒟(N)| / |𝒟(N)| = lim_{s→∞} P_Sym(s, n) + O(e^{−(log log log N)^{1/4}}), with an effectively computable implied constant.
items.note: Without an error term this is [FK1, Cor. 2] (Fouvry–Klüners). [CKMP, Thm 5.15] has an error term with an ineffective constant, and Watkins has the best known error term. Theorem 7.13 also gives Stevenhagen's Conjecture 3.4(ii). ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3 plans 'selected counting and class-group moment/distribution theorems' with sources Bhargava–Shankar and Cohen–Lenstra. It does not plan this theorem. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: MacWilliams' count of symmetric matrices over 𝔽₂ and the limit of P_Sym
items.statement: For each n ≥ 0, lim_{s→∞} P_Sym(s, n) exists and |P_Sym(r − 1, n) − lim_{s→∞} P_Sym(s, n)| ≪ e^{−(log log log N)^{1/4}} for all r satisfying (7.4); the difference is in fact exponentially small in r. Both follow from MacWilliams' explicit formula for the number of symmetric r × r matrices over 𝔽₂ of each rank.
items.note: Cited as [MacWilliams 1969], 'the explicit formulas in [Williams]'. §8 uses the same count to bound the proportion of a with dim V_{a,2} > n_max. ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5 plans 'random-matrix distributions … and the measure on the limiting space', but not this count. Route: a source of ArithmeticStatistics (ST.0 families, ST.3 class groups, ST.5 random-matrix distributions).

items.name: Proof of Theorem 7.13: Proposition 7.8 on excellent boxes, (7.24)–(7.25)
items.statement: Let W be the set of N-nice d ∈ 𝒟_r(N) lying in no W(d_i) with |d_i| > D_Siegel. Theorem 7.2 and Proposition 7.12 with t = D_Siegel give |𝒟_r(N)| − |W| ≪ |𝒟_r(N)| e^{−(log log log N)^{1/4}}. By Theorem 7.10 it suffices to show (7.24): |D_{2,n} ∩ X| / |X| = P_Sym(r − 1, n) + O(e^{−(log log log N)^{1/4}}) for every excellent (N, k, r)-box X. Apply Proposition 7.8 to (X, ∅) with (c₁, …, c₁₂) = (100, 10^{−9}, 5, 10^6, 5, 5, 1/100, 1/100, 5, 1/5, 1/5, 1/5), k₀ = k, k₁ the least integer with t_{k₁+1} > max(e^{(log t_{k+1})^5}, e^{t^5}), and k₂ = r. Its hypotheses follow from (7.1) and (7.4) for N large. The result is (7.25): Σ_{a : M_r → 𝔽₂} |r! · |X| / 2^{r(r−1)/2} − Σ_{σ∈𝒫_r} |X(σ(a))|| ≤ r! · |X| · (r^{−1/5} + t_{k+1}^{−1/100}). With (7.27) and the permutation invariance of dim ker A(a), this gives (7.24).
items.note: The constants satisfy every constraint of Proposition 7.8 (checked: 0.024 < 1/8, 0.94 < 1, 0.4 < 5). Here t is the Siegel parameter, implicitly D_Siegel. Proposition 7.8 formally requires every X_i to be an interval of primes, but for i ≤ k the X_i of a box are singletons. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The Rédei matrix A(a) and the reduced matrix A′(a), (7.26)
items.statement: For a : M_r → 𝔽₂ let A(a) be the r × r matrix over 𝔽₂ whose (i, j) entry is a(i, j) = a(j, i) for i ≠ j, with diagonal (7.26) a(i, i) := Σ_{k≠i} a(i, k). Then A(a) is symmetric with all row sums 0, and a ↦ A(a) is a bijection from maps M_r → 𝔽₂ onto symmetric r × r matrices with zero row sums. Deleting the last row and column gives A′(a), and a ↦ A′(a) is a bijection onto all symmetric (r − 1) × (r − 1) matrices. For σ ∈ 𝒫_r, dim ker A(σ(a)) = dim ker A(a).
items.note: Elementary linear algebra over 𝔽₂. Mathlib has matrices and kernels but not this bijection. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Rédei's 4-rank formula (7.27)
items.statement: Let X be a product space of primes ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4) and let a : M_r → 𝔽₂. If x ∈ X(a), then rk₄ Cl(ℚ(√x)) = −1 + dim_{𝔽₂} ker A(a) = dim_{𝔽₂} ker A′(a), where Cl is the narrow class group.
items.note: Attributed to 'classical work of Rédei', with no reference or proof. The second equality is linear algebra (zero row and column sums). The first is Rédei–Reichardt theory. Tau Ceti Multiquadratic Layer 3 plans only the 2-rank ('The 2-rank formula = t − 1 … is a theorem about the narrow class group'). No stage plans the 4-rank. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: D_{k,n}, D_{k,n}(N) and P(m, n, j)
items.statement: For k ≥ 2 and n ≥ 0, D_{k,n} := {d ∈ 𝒟 : rk_{2^k} Cl(ℚ(√d)) = n and (√d) ∈ 2^{k−1} Cl(ℚ(√d))}, with Cl the narrow class group and rk_{2^k} A = dim_{𝔽₂} 2^{k−1}A[2^k]. D_{k,n}(N) := {d ∈ D_{k,n} : d < N}. P(m, n, j) is the probability that a uniformly random m × n matrix over 𝔽₂ has right kernel of dimension j.
items.note: For k = 2 the condition (√d) ∈ 2Cl holds for every d ∈ 𝒟, since R lies in the kernel of the Rédei matrix, so this agrees with the D_{2,n} of §7. rk_{2^k} is not defined in the source. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The constants A_Comb and c
items.statement: A_Comb > 0 is a real number for which Proposition 6.6 (Smith's equidistribution theorem for acceptable additive systems) holds, and c := 1/(A_Comb · 10^{10}).
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 8.1: the 2^{m+1}-rank given the 2^m-rank (Markov chain), with the class of (√d)
items.statement: There are reals A, N₀ > 0 such that for all reals N > N₀, all integers m ≥ 2 and all integers n₂, …, n_{m+1} ≥ 0: ||⋂_{i=2}^{m+1} D_{i,n_i}(N)| − (P(n_m, n_m, n_{m+1}) / 2^{n_m}) · |⋂_{i=2}^{m} D_{i,n_i}(N)|| ≤ A · |𝒟(N)| / (log log log log N)^{c/(m² 6^m)}.
items.note: The main technical theorem. The case m = 2 is [CKMP, Thm 6.1] (next item); the paper proves m ≥ 3 through Theorems 8.2, 8.7, 8.8, 8.10 and 8.13. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The case m = 2 of Theorem 8.1 ([CKMP, Theorem 6.1])
items.statement: Theorem 8.1 holds for m = 2: the joint distribution of the 4-rank, the 8-rank and the condition (√d) ∈ 4Cl(ℚ(√d)) in 𝒟.
items.note: Cited, not reproved. §8.1 also needs the box-level form. For m = 2 no reflection principle for the self-pairing is needed, since Theorem 5.6 requires s ≥ 2. The 8-rank has governing fields and the 16-rank has none ([KM, Thm 3], [FIMR]). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 8.1 implies Theorem 1.1 (Stevenhagen's conjecture)
items.statement: Theorem 8.1 implies Stevenhagen's Conjecture 3.4(i) (the next items). Conjecture 3.4(ii) follows from [FK1, Cor. 2] or Theorem 7.13. By the argument after [Stevenhagen, Conj. 3.4], the two give Theorem 1.1: lim_{X→∞} |𝒟^−(X)| / |𝒟(X)| = 1 − α with α = ∏_{j odd} (1 − 2^{−j}), where 𝒟^−(X) is the set of d ∈ 𝒟 with d < X for which x² − dy² = −1 is soluble.
items.locator: §8, proof that Theorem 8.1 implies Theorem 1.1, p. 76 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Similar to [KP3, App. A]. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Stevenhagen's conditional densities P₂^±(m), P₂(m), P₃(m, n)
items.statement: For integers m ≥ 0: P₂^−(m) := liminf_{X→∞} |𝒟^−(X) ∩ D_{2,m}(X)| / |D_{2,m}(X)| and P₂^+(m) := limsup_{X→∞} of the same ratio. P₂(m) is their common value when they agree. For m ≥ n ≥ 0, P₃(m, n) := lim_{X→∞} |𝒟^−(X) ∩ D_{2,m}(X) ∩ D_{3,n}(X)| / |D_{2,m}(X) ∩ D_{3,n}(X)| when the limit exists.
items.locator: §8, proof that Theorem 8.1 implies Theorem 1.1, p. 76 (arXiv v1)
items.note: The source writes X for the height here; X also denotes boxes. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Stevenhagen's Conjecture 3.4(i): P₂(m) = 1/(2^{m+1} − 1), (8.1)–(8.2)
items.statement: For every integer m ≥ 0, P₂^−(m) = P₂^+(m) = 1/(2^{m+1} − 1). Proof from Theorem 8.1: P₂^−(m) = P₂^+(m), so P₂(m) exists. The Markov chain gives that P₃(m, n) exists and equals P₂(n) for m ≥ n ≥ 0. Decomposing by the 8-rank gives the recursion (8.2): P₂(m) = Σ_{n=0}^{m} P₃(m, n) · P(m, m, n) / 2^m = Σ_{n=0}^{m} P₂(n) · P(m, m, n) / 2^m. With P₂(0) = 1 and the [KP3, (A.2)] identity, induction gives (8.1).
items.locator: §8, proof that Theorem 8.1 implies Theorem 1.1, (8.1), (8.2), p. 76 (arXiv v1)
items.note: The source says P₂^− = P₂^+ follows from Theorem 8.1 but gives no argument. It needs the uniform decay in k of the proportion with rk_{2^k} ≥ 1, as in [KP3, App. A]. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The identity [KP3, (A.2)]
items.locator: §8, proof that Theorem 8.1 implies Theorem 1.1, p. 76 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Quoted from [KP3, eq. (A.2)]. Checked for m = 1: (1/2 + 1/6)/2 = 1/3. Route: a source of ArithmeticStatistics (ST.0 families, ST.3 class groups, ST.5 random-matrix distributions).

items.name: Theorem 8.2: Theorem 8.1 on excellent boxes, for m ≥ 3
items.statement: There are reals A, N₀ > 0 such that for all reals N > N₀, all integers m ≥ 3, all integers n₂, …, n_{m+1} ≥ 0, all integers r satisfying (7.4), all integers 0 ≤ k ≤ r and all excellent (N, k, r)-boxes X: ||X ∩ ⋂_{i=2}^{m+1} D_{i,n_i}(N)| − (P(n_m, n_m, n_{m+1}) / 2^{n_m}) · |X ∩ ⋂_{i=2}^{m} D_{i,n_i}(N)|| ≤ A · |X| / (log log log log N)^{c/(m² 6^m)}.
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 8.2 implies Theorem 8.1
items.statement: By (7.2) and Remark 7.11 it suffices to prove Theorem 8.1 for 𝒟_r(N) with r satisfying (7.4), up to an extra error A′ · |𝒟_r(N) − 𝒟_r(N(1 + 1/C_compr)^{−r})|. Apply Theorem 7.10 twice. The sets are V = 𝒟_r(N) ∩ ⋂_{i=2}^{m+1} D_{i,n_i}(N) and V′ = 𝒟_r(N) ∩ ⋂_{i=2}^{m} D_{i,n_i}(N). The set W is the N-nice elements of 𝒟_r(N) that lie in no W(d_i) with |d_i| > D_Siegel; Theorem 7.2(c) and Proposition 7.12 bound |W|, and boxes meeting W are excellent. For such X, applying Theorem 8.2 for i = 2, …, m and then (7.24) gives ||V ∩ X| − (∏_{i=2}^{m} P(n_i, n_i, n_{i+1}) / 2^{n_i}) · P_Sym(r − 1, n₂) · |X|| ≤ 3A|X| / (log log log log N)^{c/(m² 6^m)}, and likewise for V′. Here one may assume (log log log log N)^{c/(m² 6^m)} ≥ 2.
items.locator: §8.1, proof that Theorem 8.2 implies Theorem 8.1, pp. 77–78 (arXiv v1)
items.note: The telescoping uses the case i = 2, which Theorem 8.2 (m ≥ 3) does not cover. It must come from a box-level form of [CKMP, Thm 6.1]. The restatement of (7.2) here has N in place of |𝒟(N)|. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The gap index k_gap of an excellent box, (8.3)
items.statement: Let X be an excellent (N, k, r)-box. Fix x = (x₁, …, x_r) ∈ X and an integer k_gap with r^{1/2}/2 < k_gap + 1 < r/2 and (8.3) log x_{k_gap+1} ≥ (log log x_{k_gap+1})² · log log log N · Σ_{j=1}^{k_gap} log x_j. These exist by the third condition of N-niceness.
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: a-consistency, X(a, Q) and X_j(a, Q) (Definition 8.3)
items.statement: Let X = X₁ × ⋯ × X_r be a product space, S ⊆ [r], Q ∈ ∏_{i∈S} X_i and a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,∅} → 𝔽₂ (with a(j, i) := a(i, j)). Q is a-consistent if (π_i(Q)/π_j(Q)) = ι(a(i, j)) for all distinct i, j ∈ S. X(a, Q) := {x ∈ X(a) : π_S(x) = Q}. For j ∈ [r] − S, X_j(a, Q) := {p ∈ X_j : (π_i(Q)/p) = ι(a(i, j)) for all i ∈ S}.
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The kernel V_{a,2}, the vector R and (N, m)-generic maps (Definition 8.4)
items.statement: For a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,∅} → 𝔽₂, V_{a,2} ⊆ 𝔽₂^r is the kernel of the symmetric matrix A(a) of (7.26). Its left and right kernels coincide and contain R := (1, …, 1). a is (N, m)-generic for a box X if three conditions hold. (1) (8.4) dim V_{a,2} ≤ n_max := ⌊√((10c / (m² 6^m)) · log log log log log N)⌋. (2) (8.5) |X_j(a, Q)| ≥ |X_j| / (log s_{k+1})^{100} for all j > k, where Q is the unique element of X₁ × ⋯ × X_k, and Q is a-consistent. (3) Let α_pre := #{i ∈ ℤ : k_gap/2 ≤ i ≤ k_gap}. For all w ∈ V_{a,2} ∖ ⟨R⟩ and all j ∈ 𝔽₂: (8.6) ||{i ∈ [r] : k_gap/2 ≤ i ≤ k_gap, π_i(w) = j}| − α_pre/2| ≤ k_gap / log log log N, and (8.7) ||{i ∈ [r] : k_gap < i ≤ 2k_gap, π_i(w) = j}| − k_gap/2| ≤ k_gap / log log log N.
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Lemma 8.5: joint balance of several kernel vectors
items.statement: Let a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,∅} → 𝔽₂ be (N, m)-generic for a box X, and let w₁, …, w_d, R ∈ V_{a,2} be linearly independent. Then for every 𝐯 ∈ 𝔽₂^d: ||{i ∈ [r] : k_gap/2 ≤ i ≤ k_gap, π_i(w_j) = π_j(𝐯) for all 1 ≤ j ≤ d}| − α_pre/2^d| ≤ 3^d k_gap / log log log N, and ||{i ∈ [r] : k_gap < i ≤ 2k_gap, π_i(w_j) = π_j(𝐯) for all 1 ≤ j ≤ d}| − k_gap/2^d| ≤ 3^d k_gap / log log log N.
items.note: Compare [CKMP, Lemma 6.9]. The proof is by induction on d using (8.6)–(8.7) and the identity 2(f(𝐯) − α/2^d) = Σ_i (f(𝐯) + f(𝐯_i) − α/2^{d−1}) + (α/2^{d−2} − f(𝐯) − Σ_i f(𝐯_i)). Checked. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Valid and Pellian sequences of pairings (Definition 8.6)
items.statement: Let X be a box and a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,∅} → 𝔽₂. A sequence of bilinear pairings {Art_i : A_i × B_i → 𝔽₂}_{2≤i<m} is valid if A₂ = B₂ = V_{a,2}; the left kernel of Art_i is A_{i+1} and its right kernel is B_{i+1} for 2 ≤ i < m − 1; and R is in the right kernel of Art_i for 2 ≤ i < m. It is Pellian if moreover R is in the left kernel of Art_i for all 2 ≤ i < m. A_m and B_m are the left and right kernels of Art_{m−1}.
items.note: By induction dim A_i = dim B_i, so the count 2^{dim A_m (dim A_m − 1)} in Theorem 8.7 is the number of pairings with R in the right kernel. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The sequence of Artin pairings of x ∈ X(a), and X(a, {Art_i})
items.statement: For x ∈ X and k ≥ 1, Art_{k,x} : 2^{k−1}Cl(ℚ(√x))[2^k] × 2^{k−1}Cl^∨(ℚ(√x))[2^k] → 𝔽₂ is the Artin pairing of §2.3. Pull Art_{1,x} back along the genus-theory surjections to a pairing 𝔽₂^r × 𝔽₂^r → 𝔽₂. For x ∈ X(a) its left and right kernels both equal V_{a,2}, which gives surjections V_{a,2} → 2Cl(ℚ(√x))[4] and V_{a,2} → 2Cl^∨(ℚ(√x))[4] and a pairing V_{a,2} × V_{a,2} → 𝔽₂. Iterating gives a valid sequence {Art_{i,x}}_{i≥2}. For a valid sequence {Art_i}_{2≤i<m}, X(a, {Art_i}_{2≤i<m}) := {x ∈ X(a) : the Artin pairings of x equal {Art_i}_{2≤i<m}}.
items.note: The Artin pairing Art_s(A) is defined in §2.3. Here Cl is the narrow class group. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Genus theory: ramified primes and genus characters span Cl[2] and Cl^∨[2]
items.statement: Let x = p₁⋯p_r ∈ 𝒟 with p₁ < ⋯ < p_r, and let Cl be the narrow class group of ℚ(√x). The maps 𝔽₂^r → Cl(ℚ(√x))[2], (e₁, …, e_r) ↦ class of Up_{ℚ(√x)/ℚ}(∏ p_i^{e_i}), and 𝔽₂^r → Cl^∨(ℚ(√x))[2], (e₁, …, e_r) ↦ Σ e_i χ_{p_i}, are surjective.
items.note: Used without proof ('Genus theory gives natural surjections'). Tau Ceti Multiquadratic Layer 3 plans the genus field with 'Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl(K)/Cl(K)²' and warns that 'The 2-rank formula = t − 1 … is a theorem about the narrow class group'; that is the surjection onto Cl^∨[2] = (Cl/Cl²)^∨. Layer 2 plans 'the ambiguous-class-number formula', the input for the ramified-prime surjection onto Cl[2].

items.name: Negative Pell and Pellian sequences
items.statement: For x ∈ X(a), the negative Pell equation u² − x v² = −1 is soluble if and only if the sequence of Artin pairings of x is Pellian, that is, R lies in the left kernel of Art_{i,x} for every i ≥ 2. Equivalently, the class of (√x) in the narrow class group is trivial.
items.note: Stated without proof. Under the surjection 𝔽₂^r → Cl[2], R maps to the class of (√x), which lies in 2^i Cl for all i if and only if it is trivial ([FK1, Lemma 1], §1). A finite sequence (2 ≤ i < m) that is Pellian gives only a necessary condition. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 8.7: the next Artin pairing is uniformly distributed
items.statement: There are reals A, N₀ > 0 with the following property. Take reals N > N₀, integers m ≥ 3, integers r satisfying (7.4), integers 0 ≤ k ≤ r, excellent (N, k, r)-boxes X, maps a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,∅} → 𝔽₂ that are (N, m)-generic for X, Pellian sequences {Art_k}_{2≤k<m}, and bilinear pairings Art_m : A_m × B_m → 𝔽₂ with R in the right kernel. Then ||X(a, {Art_k}_{2≤k≤m})| − |X(a, {Art_k}_{2≤k<m})| / 2^{dim_{𝔽₂} A_m · (dim_{𝔽₂} A_m − 1)}| ≤ A · |X(a)| / (log log log log N)^{100c/(m 6^m)}.
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 8.7 implies Theorem 8.2: non-generic maps are negligible, (8.8)–(8.11)
items.statement: There is an absolute A′ > 0 with (8.8): Σ_{a not (N, m)-generic} |X(a)| ≤ A′ · |X| · 2^{−2c · log log log log log N / (m² 6^m)}. The proof has three parts. (a) The maps a failing (8.5) contribute at most Σ_{j>k} 2^k |X| / (log s_{k+1})^{100} (8.9). This uses the classes of a ∼_j a′ ⟺ a(i, j) = a′(i, j) for all i ≤ k, and k ≤ (1/5) log log log N, which follows from (7.1). (b) Proposition 7.8, with k₂ the largest integer < k_gap/2, gives (8.10): Σ_a |k₂! |X| / 2^{|M_r|+|M_{r,∅}|} − Σ_{σ∈𝒫_r(k₂)} |X(σ(a))|| ≤ k₂! |X| / k₂^{b₁} ≤ k₂! |X| / (log log N)^{b₁b₂} for absolute b₁, b₂ > 0. Conditions (8.4), (8.6) and (8.7) are 𝒫_r(k₂)-invariant, so (8.8) reduces to the proportion (8.11) of a failing them. (c) That proportion is O(2^{−2c · log log log log log N / (m² 6^m)}), by the MacWilliams count for (8.4) and by Hoeffding plus the kernel-vector count for (8.6)–(8.7). Finally, generic a are split over the ≤ 2^{m n_max²} sequences of Artin pairings and Theorem 8.7 is applied.
items.locator: §8.2, proof that Theorem 8.7 implies Theorem 8.2, (8.8)–(8.12), pp. 81–83 (arXiv v1)
items.note: The trivial bound in (a) has |X| where |X_j| is meant under the union. The TeX label of (8.10) is 'eTheorem5.9', left over from an older numbering; it is not printed. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Hoeffding's inequality (for (8.12))
items.statement: For w uniform in 𝔽₂^r and j ∈ 𝔽₂, the proportion of w with ||{i ∈ [r] : k_gap/2 ≤ i ≤ k_gap, π_i(w) = j}| − α_pre/2| > k_gap / log log log N is O(e^{−(log log log N)^{−2} · k_gap}), and likewise for the range k_gap < i ≤ 2k_gap.
items.locator: §8.2, proof that Theorem 8.7 implies Theorem 8.2, (8.12), p. 82 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Checked at Mathlib 082e2d3. ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF.measure_sum_ge_le_of_iIndepFun bounds μ.real {ω | ε ≤ Σ_{i∈s} X_i ω} by exp(−ε²/(2 Σ c_i)) for independent sub-Gaussian X_i. ProbabilityTheory.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_mem_Icc_of_integral_eq_zero (Hoeffding's lemma) makes centred variables with values in [a, b] sub-Gaussian with parameter ((b − a)/2)². The application to independent uniform bits (two-sided, via ±) is a direct specialisation, not a named declaration.

items.name: A fixed non-constant vector rarely lies in V_{a,2}
items.statement: For every w ∈ 𝔽₂^r ∖ ⟨R⟩, the proportion of maps a : M_r → 𝔽₂ with w ∈ V_{a,2} is O(2^{−r}).
items.locator: §8.2, proof that Theorem 8.7 implies Theorem 8.2, p. 82 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Stated without proof. The proportion is exactly 2^{1−r}. The condition A(a)w = 0 says Σ_{j≠i} a(i, j)(w_i + w_j) = 0 for each i. This is the boundary map of the complete bipartite graph between w⁻¹(0) and w⁻¹(1), a connected graph because w ≠ 0, R, so the r conditions have rank r − 1. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 8.8 implies Theorem 8.7 (orthogonality of characters)
items.statement: Let 𝒜 be the 𝔽₂-space of bilinear pairings A_m × B_m → 𝔽₂ with R in the right kernel. For Art_m ∈ 𝒜, |X(a, {Art_k}_{2≤k≤m})| = |𝒜|^{−1} Σ_{F ∈ 𝒜^∨} Σ_{x ∈ X(a, {Art_k}_{2≤k<m})} ι(F(Art_{m,x}) − F(Art_m)). So Theorem 8.7 follows from the bound of Theorem 8.8 for every non-trivial F.
items.locator: §8.2, running text before Theorem 8.8, p. 83 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Only asserted ('a straightforward application of orthogonality of characters'). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 8.8: character sums of the m-th Artin pairing
items.statement: There are reals A, N₀ > 0 with the following property. Take reals N > N₀, integers m ≥ 3, integers r satisfying (7.4), integers 0 ≤ k ≤ r, excellent (N, k, r)-boxes X, maps a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,∅} → 𝔽₂ that are (N, m)-generic for X, Pellian sequences {Art_k}_{2≤k<m}, and non-trivial linear maps F : {A_m × B_m → 𝔽₂ bilinear with R in the right kernel} → 𝔽₂. Then |Σ_{x ∈ X(a, {Art_k}_{2≤k<m})} ι(F(Art_{m,x}))| ≤ A · |X(a)| / (log log log log N)^{100c/(m 6^m)}.
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Adapted bases and the matrix of Art_{m,x} (Definition 8.9, first part)
items.statement: For 2 ≤ i ≤ m, C_i := A_i ∩ B_i, d_i := dim_{𝔽₂} C_i − 1 and n_i := dim_{𝔽₂} A_i − 1. Choose a basis v₁, …, v_{n_m}, R of A_m and a basis w₁, …, w_{n_m}, R of B_m with v_i = w_i for 1 ≤ i ≤ d_m, so that v₁, …, v_{d_m}, R is a basis of C_m. Extend to a basis w₁, …, w_{n₂}, R of V_{a,2} such that w₁, …, w_{n_i}, R is a basis of B_i for every 2 ≤ i ≤ m. Mat(a, b, K) is the set of a × b matrices over a field K. Art_{m,x} becomes the matrix in Mat(n_m + 1, n_m + 1, 𝔽₂) with (i, j) entry Art_{m,x}(v_i, w_j) for i, j ∈ [n_m], whose last row and column record pairing with R. Since R is in the right kernel, it is also viewed in Mat(n_m + 1, n_m, 𝔽₂).
items.note: The bases require R ∈ A_m ∩ B_m, which holds for Pellian sequences. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The four cases I–IV of a non-trivial functional F (Definition 8.9, second part)
items.statement: E_{j₃,j₄} is the matrix unit and F_{j₁,j₂} : Mat(n_m + 1, n_m, 𝔽₂) → 𝔽₂ is the linear map sending E_{j₃,j₄} to 1 exactly when (j₃, j₄) = (j₁, j₂). Every F is Σ_{1≤j₁≤n_m+1, 1≤j₂≤n_m} c_{j₁,j₂} F_{j₁,j₂}. For F ≠ 0 choose (j₁, j₂) with c_{j₁,j₂} = 1 by the first case that applies. Case I: j₁ ≤ n_m and one of n_m ≥ j₁ > d_m, n_m ≥ j₂ > d_m, or (1 ≤ j₁, j₂ ≤ d_m and c_{j₂,j₁} = 0). Case II: c_{n_m+1,j} = 1 for some j, and (j₁, j₂) := (n_m + 1, j). Case III: c_{j,j} = 1 for some j, and (j₁, j₂) := (j, j). Case IV: some j₁ ≠ j₂ with c_{j₁,j₂} = c_{j₂,j₁} = 1, which always exists when F ≠ 0 and Cases I–III fail.
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Sets of variable indices S for F and the index i_Cheb (Definition 8.9, third part)
items.statement: Put G := {i : k_gap/2 ≤ i ≤ k_gap}, H := {i : k_gap < i ≤ 2k_gap} and Z₀ := G ∩ ⋂_{l=1}^{n₂} {i ∈ [r] : π_i(w_l) = 0}. S is a set of variable indices for F if, according to its case: Case I: |S| = m + 1, with m − 1 elements in Z₀; one element in G ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, (j₂ ≤ d_m ⇒ l ≠ j₂)} {π_i(v_l) = 0} ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, l ≠ j₂} {π_i(w_l) = 0} ∩ {π_i(w_{j₂}) = 1}; and one element in H ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, l ≠ j₁} {π_i(v_l) = 0} ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, (j₁ ≤ d_m ⇒ l ≠ j₁)} {π_i(w_l) = 0} ∩ {π_i(v_{j₁}) = 1}. Case II: |S| = m, with m − 1 elements in Z₀ and one element in H ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, (j₂ ≤ d_m ⇒ l ≠ j₂)} {π_i(v_l) = 0} ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, l ≠ j₂} {π_i(w_l) = 0} ∩ {π_i(w_{j₂}) = 1}. Case III (j = j₁ = j₂): |S| = m, with m − 1 elements in G ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n₂, l ≠ j} {π_i(w_l) = 0} ∩ {π_i(w_j) = 1} and one element in H ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m} {π_i(v_l) = π_i(w_l) = 0}. Case IV: |S| = m, with m − 1 elements in G ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n₂, l ≠ j₂} {π_i(w_l) = 0} ∩ {π_i(w_{j₂}) = 1} and one element in H ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, l ≠ j₁} {π_i(v_l) = π_i(w_l) = 0} ∩ {π_i(v_{j₁}) = 1}. i_Cheb is the unique element of S ∩ H.
items.note: Every vector of V_{a,2} = ⟨w₁, …, w_{n₂}, R⟩ is constant on Z₀, which is what the proofs of properties (b) use. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Variable indices exist; one may assume m < log log log log log log N, (8.13)
items.statement: One may assume (8.13) m < log log log log log log N, since otherwise Theorem 8.1 holds trivially. Then, for N large, Lemma 8.5 gives a set of variable indices S for every non-trivial F.
items.locator: §8.2, running text after Definition 8.9, (8.13), p. 85 (arXiv v1)
items.note: The linear independence needed in Lemma 8.5 holds: v₁, …, v_{n_m}, w_{d_m+1}, …, w_{n_m}, R is a basis of A_m + B_m. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The fibre X(a, Q, {Art_k}) over the fixed small non-variable primes
items.statement: For Q ∈ ∏_{i ∈ [k_gap] − S} X_i, X(a, Q, {Art_k}_{2≤k<m}) := {x ∈ X(a, {Art_k}_{2≤k<m}) : π_{[k_gap]−S}(x) = Q}.
items.locator: §8.2, running text before Theorem 8.10, p. 85 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 8.10: the character sum with all small non-variable primes fixed
items.statement: There are reals A, N₀ > 0 with the following property. Take reals N > N₀, integers m ≥ 3, integers r satisfying (7.4), integers 0 ≤ k ≤ r, excellent (N, k, r)-boxes X, maps a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,∅} → 𝔽₂ that are (N, m)-generic for X, Pellian sequences {Art_k}_{2≤k<m}, non-trivial linear maps F : Mat(n_m + 1, n_m, 𝔽₂) → 𝔽₂, sets S of variable indices for F, and a-consistent Q ∈ ∏_{i ∈ [k_gap] − S} X_i with (8.14) |X_j(a, Q)| ≥ 4^{−m·k_gap} · |X_j| for all j ∈ S ∩ [k_gap]. Then |Σ_{x ∈ X(a, Q, {Art_k}_{2≤k<m})} ι(F(Art_{m,x}))| ≤ A · |X(a, Q)| / (log log log log N)^{100c/(m 6^m)}.
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 8.10 implies Theorem 8.8, (8.15)–(8.16)
items.statement: Split the sum of Theorem 8.8 over Q ∈ ∏_{i ∈ [k_gap] − S} X_i. The Q satisfying (8.14) are handled by Theorem 8.10. For the others, let Q′ be the unique element of X₁ × ⋯ × X_k. Proposition 7.6 bounds the number of a-consistent Q by 2|X′| / 2^{(k_gap − |S| − k)(k_gap − |S| − k − 1)/2}, where X′ = ∏_{i ∈ [k_gap] − S − [k]} X_i(a, Q′). Failing (8.14) gives ∏_{i ∈ S∩[k_gap]} |X_i(a, Q)| ≤ ∏_{i ∈ S∩[k_gap]} |X_i(a, Q′)| · (log s_{k+1})^{100m} / 4^{m k_gap}. Chebotarev gives |X_i(a, P × Q)| = |X_i(a, Q′)| 2^{−(k_gap − k)} (1 + O(e^{−k_gap})) for i > k_gap. Proposition 7.6 on the tail gives (8.15). The lower bound (8.16), 2|X(a)| ≥ ∏_{i∈[r]−[k]} |X_i(a, Q′)| / 2^{(r−k)(r−k−1)/2}, then shows the bad Q are negligible.
items.locator: §8.2, proof that Theorem 8.10 implies Theorem 8.8, (8.15), (8.16), pp. 86–87 (arXiv v1)
items.note: (8.16) is printed with exponent (r − k)(r − k − 1), missing the /2. The intermediate bound uses ∏_{i∈S} and max_P X(a, P × Q) where ∏_{i∈S∩[k_gap]} and |X(a, P × Q)| are meant. The proof ends 'The proposition follows', meaning Theorem 8.8. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: M_box, S′ and great product spaces (Definition 8.11)
items.statement: Put M_box := ⌊(log log log log N)^{1/(5(m+1))}⌋; by (8.13), M_box ≥ 2 for N large. Put S′ := S ∩ [k_gap], so S = S′ ∪ {i_Cheb}. For Z_i ⊆ X_i (i ∈ S′), Z := ∏_{i∈S′} Z_i is a great product space if all of the following hold. (1) |Z_i| = M_box and Z_i ⊆ X_i(a, Q) for all i ∈ S′. (2) (π_i(z)/π_j(z)) = ι(a(i, j)) for all z ∈ Z and all distinct i, j ∈ S′. (3) In Case I, let i_char be the unique index in S′ with π_{i_char}(w_{j₂}) = 1. For all T ⊆ S′ − {i_char} and all z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, T ∪ {i_char}), the expansion map φ_{π_T(z̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(z̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(z̄))} exists, and when T ⊊ S′ − {i_char} all primes of Q, (2) and ∞ split completely in it. (4) In Cases II–IV: for all T ⊆ S′, z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, T) and i ∈ T, the map φ_{π_{T−{i}}(z̄); pr₁(π_i(z̄)) pr₂(π_i(z̄))} exists with all primes of Q, (2) and ∞ split completely in it. Also, for all T ⊆ S′ and z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, T), the map φ_{π_T(z̄); −1} exists, and when T ⊊ S′ all odd primes of Q and Up_{ℚ(i)/ℚ}(2) split completely in it.
items.note: Expansion maps φ_{…;…} and their fields of definition L(φ) are defined in §2 and §6.3. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The fields M_∘(Z), M(Z), the sets X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z)) and the space Z̃
items.statement: In Case I: M_∘(Z) := ∏_{T ⊊ S′−{i_char}} ∏_{z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, T∪{i_char})} L(φ_{π_T(z̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(z̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(z̄))}), and M(Z) := ∏_{z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, S′)} L(φ_{π_{S′−{i_char}}(z̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(z̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(z̄))}). In Cases II–IV: M_∘(Z) := ∏_{i∈S′} ∏_{z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, S′)} L(φ_{π_{S′−{i}}(z̄); pr₁(π_i(z̄)) pr₂(π_i(z̄))}) · ∏_{T ⊊ S′} ∏_{z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, T)} L(φ_{π_T(z̄); −1}), and M(Z) := ∏_{z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, S′)} L(φ_{π_{S′}(z̄); −1}). Products of fields are composita. For i > k_gap, X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z)) is the set of p ∈ X_i(a, Q) that split completely in M_∘(Z) and satisfy (z/p) = ι(a(j, i)) for all j ∈ S′ and all z ∈ Z_j. This is a condition that Frob_p equal a given central element of the Galois group of M_∘(Z) · ℚ(√z : z ∈ {−1} ∪ {primes of Q} ∪ ⋃_j Z_j). For a great Z, Z̃ := Q × Z × ∏_{i>k_gap} X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z)).
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: The pre-space X_pre
items.statement: X_pre := ∏_{i∈S′} X_i(a, Q).
items.locator: §8.3, running text before Lemma 8.12, p. 88 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Lemma 8.12: an additive system that produces expansion maps
items.statement: For every W ⊆ X_pre there is an additive system (C_T, C_T^acc, F_T, A_T)_{T⊆S′} on (X_pre, S′) with the following properties. (1) C_∅^acc = W. (2) |A_T| ≤ 2^{(|S′|+100)·(k_gap+|S′|+100)} for all T ⊆ S′. (3) In Case I: if x̄ ∈ C_{S′}^acc, then φ_{π_{S′−{i_char}}(x̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(x̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(x̄))} exists. For i_char ∈ T ⊊ S′ and x̄ ∈ C_T^acc, the map φ_{π_{T−{i_char}}(x̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(x̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(x̄))} exists and all primes of Q, all primes in π_{S′−T}(x̄), (2) and ∞ split completely in it. (4) In Cases II–IV: if x̄ ∈ C_{S′}^acc, then φ_{π_{S′}(x̄); −1} exists. All odd primes of Q, all primes in π_{S′−T}(x̄) and Up_{ℚ(i)/ℚ}(2) split completely in φ_{π_T(x̄); −1} for all T ⊊ S′ and x̄ ∈ C_T^acc. For all T ⊆ S′, x̄ ∈ C_T^acc and i ∈ T, the map φ_{π_{T−{i}}(x̄); pr₁(π_i(x̄)) pr₂(π_i(x̄))} exists and all primes of Q, all primes in π_{S′−T}(x̄), (2) and ∞ split completely in it.
items.note: Proof (Case I): F_{{i}} records the Legendre symbols ((pr₁ pr₂)(π_i(x̄))/q) for q | Q, q in the other coordinates, and q = 2. For |T| > 1, F_T is the value of the new expansion map on the Frobenius at those places. Proposition 2.16 makes the map exist, Proposition 2.14 puts those Frobenius elements in the centre, and Lemma 2.13 gives additivity (6.1). The a-consistency needed for Proposition 2.16 comes from W ⊆ Z_pre in the application. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 8.13: character sums on great boxes
items.statement: There are reals A, N₀ > 0 with the following property. Take reals N > N₀, integers m ≥ 3, integers r satisfying (7.4), integers 0 ≤ k ≤ r, excellent (N, k, r)-boxes X, maps a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,∅} → 𝔽₂ that are (N, m)-generic for X, Pellian sequences {Art_k}_{2≤k<m}, non-trivial linear maps F : Mat(n_m + 1, n_m, 𝔽₂) → 𝔽₂, sets S of variable indices for F, a-consistent Q ∈ ∏_{i ∈ [k_gap] − S} X_i, and great product spaces Z. Then |Σ_{x ∈ X(a, Q, {Art_k}_{2≤k<m}) ∩ Z̃} ι(F(Art_{m,x}))| ≤ A · |X(a, Q) ∩ Z̃| / (log log log log N)^{100c/(m 6^m)}.
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 8.13 implies Theorem 8.10, step 1: a cover by great product spaces, and (8.17)
items.statement: Set R := ⌊e^{e^{k_gap/5}}⌋ (the letter R is reused) and let Z_pre be the set of a-consistent z ∈ X_pre. Choose a sequence Z₁, …, Z_t of maximal length with each Z_i ⊆ Z_pre great, |Z_i ∩ Z_j| ≤ 1 for i ≠ j, and each z ∈ Z_pre in at most R of the Z_i. Let Z_pre,bad be the set of z in fewer than R of the Z_i, and δ its density in X_pre. A greedy choice gives W ⊆ Z_pre,bad of density ≥ δ/(R M_box^m) with |W ∩ Z_i| ≤ 1. Proposition 6.2 with Lemma 8.12 gives C_{S′}^acc density ≥ δ′ := (δ / (2^{(|S′|+100)(k_gap+|S′|+100)} R M_box^m))^{3^m}. Via the injection of C_{S′}^acc into ⊔_{x₀∈W} W(x₀), some W(x₀) has density ≥ δ′. Maximality and the contrapositive of Lemma 6.3 then give 5 M_box^m > log min_{i∈S′} |X_i(a, Q)| / log δ′^{−1}. With |X_i(a, Q)| ≥ e^{e^{(3/10)k_gap}}, from (8.14) and (7.1), this yields (8.17) δ ≤ e^{−¼ e^{k_gap}}.
items.locator: §8.3, proof that Theorem 8.13 implies Theorem 8.10, (8.17), pp. 90–91 (arXiv v1)
items.note: The displayed argument supports only δ ≤ exp(−e^{(3/10 − o(1)) k_gap}), not (8.17) as printed; the weaker bound suffices. The injection has pr₁ and pr₂ swapped. Extending the sequence also needs expansion maps for all cubes of ∏ W_i, not only those through x₀; this uses additivity (Lemma 2.13) and is left implicit. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Theorem 8.13 implies Theorem 8.10, step 2: first and second moments of Λ, (8.18)–(8.22)
items.statement: Split off the x with π_{S′}(x) ∈ Z_pre,bad (8.18); they fit in the error term by (8.17) and two applications of Proposition 7.6. For x ∈ X(a, Q) with π_{S′}(x) ∉ Z_pre,bad, let Λ(x) := #{i ∈ [t] : x ∈ Z̃_i}. Two applications of Proposition 7.6 and the Chebotarev item give |X(a, Q) ∩ Z̃_i ∩ π_{S′}^{−1}(z)| = 𝟏_{z∈Z_i} · |X(a, Q) ∩ π_{S′}^{−1}(z)| / d(M_box, m)^{r−k_gap} · (1 + O(e^{−k_gap})). Hence (8.20) Σ Λ(x) = R |X(a, Q)| / d(M_box, m)^{r−k_gap} · (1 + O(e^{−k_gap})). Because |Z_i ∩ Z_j| ≤ 1 gives [L(Q) M_∘(Z_i) M_∘(Z_j) : L(Q)] = d(M_box, m)² (Lemmas 6.8, 6.10), also (8.21) Σ Λ(x)² = R² |X(a, Q)| / d(M_box, m)^{2(r−k_gap)} · (1 + O(e^{−k_gap})). By Chebyshev's inequality, outside a set of density O(e^{−k_gap/2}), (8.22) |Λ(x) − R / d(M_box, m)^{r−k_gap}| ≤ R e^{−k_gap/4} / d(M_box, m)^{r−k_gap}.
items.locator: §8.3, proof that Theorem 8.13 implies Theorem 8.10, (8.18)–(8.22), pp. 91–92 (arXiv v1)
items.note: In (8.21) the diagonal terms R|X(a, Q)| d^{−(r−k_gap)} are absorbed because R ≫ e^{k_gap} d^{r−k_gap}. The source does not say so, but it holds since log R = e^{k_gap/5} dominates (r − k_gap) log d. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Chebotarev with Siegel-zero control for M_∘(Z) (Smith, Prop. 6.5, with Heilbronn)
items.statement: Let L(Q) := ℚ(√−1, √π_j(z) (j ∈ S′), √π_j(Q) (j ∈ [k_gap] − S′)) for z ∈ Z_pre ∖ Z_pre,bad, and let d(M_box, m) := [L(Q) M_∘(Z_i) : L(Q)]. For i > k_gap: |X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z))| = |X_i(a, Q × {z})| / d(M_box, m) · (1 + O(e^{−2k_gap})).
items.locator: §8.3, proof that Theorem 8.13 implies Theorem 8.10, p. 92 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Cited as [Smith, Prop. 6.5]. It uses (8.3) and Heilbronn's theorem against possible Siegel zeros. Lemmas 6.8 and 6.10 show that d(M_box, m) does not depend on i; the source writes M_∘(Z̃_i) for M_∘(Z_i). The error term must be uniform in a field of degree up to 2^{O(2^m M_box^{2m})}. That is the effective Chebotarev input again; no stage plans it. Route: a source of AnalyticNumberTheory (AN.2 exceptional zeros and uniform prime number theorems, AN.4 effective Chebotarev and Dedekind zeta functions, AN.5 mean values of multiplicative functions).

items.name: Heilbronn's theorem on real zeros of Dedekind zeta functions
items.statement: If K/ℚ is a finite Galois extension and ζ_K(s) has a simple real zero β (such as an exceptional zero), then ζ_k(β) = 0 for some quadratic subfield k ⊆ K. So a Siegel zero of a 2-extension comes from a quadratic subfield, and it is excluded by the excellent-box condition.
items.locator: §8.3, proof that Theorem 8.13 implies Theorem 8.10, p. 92; also §8.4, (8.44), p. 104 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Cited as [Heilbronn 1973] ('a well-known result of Heilbronn'), with no statement. The form given is the standard one; the precise hypothesis used (normal extension, simple zero) is not stated in the source. No stage plans it. Route: a source of AnalyticNumberTheory (AN.2 exceptional zeros and uniform prime number theorems, AN.4 effective Chebotarev and Dedekind zeta functions, AN.5 mean values of multiplicative functions).

items.name: Chebyshev's inequality (for (8.22))
items.statement: For a real random variable Y with finite variance and c > 0, P(|Y − E[Y]| ≥ c) ≤ Var(Y)/c². Applied to Λ(x) on the uniform measure, with (8.20) and (8.21), it gives (8.22) outside a set of density O(e^{−k_gap/2}).
items.locator: §8.3, proof that Theorem 8.13 implies Theorem 8.10, p. 92 (arXiv v1)
items.note: Checked at Mathlib 082e2d3: ProbabilityTheory.meas_ge_le_variance_div_sq [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (hc : 0 < c) : μ {ω | c ≤ |X ω − μ[X]|} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (variance X μ / c²).

items.name: Theorem 8.13 implies Theorem 8.10, step 3: conclusion, (8.23)
items.statement: The sum over x with π_{S′}(x) ∉ Z_pre,bad is at most the two terms of (8.23). The first is (d(M_box, m)^{r−k_gap}/R) · |Σ_{i∈[t]} Σ_{x ∈ X(a, Q, {Art_k}) ∩ Z̃_i} ι(F(Art_{m,x}))|. Theorem 8.13 bounds it by A d^{r−k_gap} / (R (log log log log N)^{100c/(m6^m)}) · Σ_i |X(a, Q) ∩ Z̃_i|, and Σ_i |X(a, Q) ∩ Z̃_i| ≤ Σ Λ(x) + R · #{x : π_{S′}(x) ∈ Z_pre,bad}. The second is bounded by Σ_x |1 − d(M_box, m)^{r−k_gap} Λ(x) / R|, split by whether x satisfies (8.22).
items.locator: §8.3, proof that Theorem 8.13 implies Theorem 8.10, (8.23), pp. 92–93 (arXiv v1)
items.note: For the x failing (8.22) the source uses the trivial bound Λ(x) ≤ R. That bound is not enough, since d^{r−k_gap} e^{−k_gap/2} → ∞. Cauchy–Schwarz with (8.20)–(8.21) closes the step. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Raw cocycles ψ_i(x, v) attached to kernel vectors
items.statement: For every non-zero v ∈ V_{a,2} and every x ∈ X(a, Q), fix a raw cocycle (ψ_i(x, v))_{0≤i≤t(x,v)} for N(x) with ψ₁(x, v) = Σ_{1≤j≤r, π_j(v)=1} χ_{π_j(x)} and t(x, v) maximal among such raw cocycles. Also set n₁ := n₂.
items.note: Raw cocycles and the module N are defined in §2.1. In §8.4, N denotes that module, not the height. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: An additive system 𝔄 on (Z̃, S) with properties (a)–(d), (8.24)–(8.28)
items.statement: There is an additive system 𝔄 = (C_T, C_T^acc, F_T, A_T)_{T⊆S} on (Z̃, S) with properties (a)–(d). (a) C_∅^acc = X(a, Q, {Art_k}_{2≤k<m}) ∩ Z̃. (b) 𝔄 is (2^{(n_max+10)(n_max+2m+10)}, S)-acceptable. (c) Let F′(x) := F(Art_{m,x}). For all x̄ ∈ C(𝔄), (ΣF′)(x̄) = φ(Frob(pr₁(π_{i_Cheb}(x̄)))) + φ(Frob(pr₂(π_{i_Cheb}(x̄)))), where φ = φ_{π_{S′−{i_char}}(x̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(x̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(x̄))} in Case I and φ = φ_{π_{S′}(x̄); −1} in Cases II–IV. (d) Take |T| < m, 1 ≤ j ≤ n_{|T|+1} and x̄ ∈ C_T^acc, and put 𝒲 := {j₁, j₂} if j₁ ≤ d_m and 𝒲 := {j₂} otherwise. In Case I: (8.24) Σ_{x∈x̄(∅)} ψ_{|T|}(x, w_j) = 0 for j ∉ 𝒲, if T ⊆ S′ − {i_char} or j ≤ n_m; (8.25) Σ_{x∈x̄(∅)} ψ_{|T|}(x, w_{j₂}) = φ_{π_{T−{i_char}}(x̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(x̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(x̄))} if i_char ∈ T; (8.26) the same sum is 0 if i_char ∉ T; (8.27) Σ_{x∈x̄(∅)} ψ_{|T|}(x, w_{j₁}) = 0 if i_Cheb ∉ T and j₁ ∈ 𝒲; (8.28) Σ_{x∈x̄(∅)} ψ_{|T|+1}(x, w_j)(σ_{π_i(x̄)}) = 0 for all i ∈ S − T, if T ≠ ∅. Cases II–IV have analogous vanishing conditions with j₂ (Case II), w_{j₂} + R (Case III), and w_{j₁}, w_{j₂} + R and w_{j₁} + w_{j₂} + R (Case IV).
items.note: The source states (a)–(d) as goals and proves them in the next four items. σ_p is an inertia generator at p (§2). (ΣF′) and C(𝔄) are as in §6.2. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Construction of F_T = (F_{T,1}, F_{T,2}, F_{T,3})
items.statement: Case I; the other cases are similar. Induct on |T|, with F_T := 0 if T = ∅ or |T| ≥ m. For 0 < |T| < m, 1 ≤ j ≤ n_{|T|+1} (with T ⊆ S′ − {i_char} if j > n_m) and x̄ ∈ C_T, let ψ(x̄, j) := Σ_{x∈x̄(∅)} ψ_{|T|}(x, w_j). Add φ_{π_{T−{i_char}}(x̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(x̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(x̄))} when j = j₂ and i_char ∈ T, and set ψ(x̄, j₁) := 0 when i_Cheb ∈ T and j₁ ∈ 𝒲. By Proposition 2.9, dψ(x̄, j) = 0, and ψ(x̄, j) is an unramified quadratic character of ℚ(√x) in which Up(π_j(x̄)) splits for j ∉ T. By (8.7) there are an injection f : [n₂] → [r] − S − {1} with π_{f(i)}(w_j) = 1 ⟺ i = j, and some i₀ ∈ [r] − S − {1} with π_{i₀}(w_j) = 0 for all j ∈ [n₂]. For any x₀ ∈ x̄(∅), put F_{T,1}(x̄) := (ψ(x̄, j)(Frob(Up_{ℚ(√x₀)/ℚ}(π_i(x₀)))))_{j ≤ n_{|T|+1}, i ∈ T}; F_{T,2}(x̄) := ((ψ(x̄, j)(σ_{π_{i₀}(x₀)}))_j, (ψ(x̄, j)(σ_{π_{f(i)}(x₀)}))_{j, i∈[n₂]}); F_{T,3}(x̄) := (Σ_{x∈x̄(∅)} ψ_{|T|+1}(x, w_j)(σ_{π_i(x₀)}))_{j, i∈S−T}. For T ⊄ S′ − {i_char}, j runs only up to n_m in F_{T,1} and F_{T,2}. Each part is independent of x₀ and satisfies (6.1), so F_T defines an additive system with |A_T| ≤ 2^{(n_max+10)(n_max+2m+10)}.
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Verification of property (d)
items.statement: If x̄ ∈ C_T^acc then ψ(x̄, j) = 0 for every 1 ≤ j ≤ n_{|T|+1}, which is (8.24)–(8.27); (8.28) is F_{T,3}(x̄) = 0. For |T| = 1 this follows from the choice of variable indices. For |T| > 1: F_{T′,3} vanishes on all lower cubes, so ψ(x̄, j) is unramified. F_{T,1}(x̄) = 0 then puts it in V_{a,2}. F_{T,2}(x̄) = 0 kills its R-component (via i₀) and its w_k-components (via f).
items.note: Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Verification of properties (b) and (c) in Case I, (8.30)–(8.34)
items.statement: In Case I, 𝔄 is (2^{(n_max+10)(n_max+2m+10)}, S)-acceptable. For non-degenerate x̄ ∈ C(𝔄), pick z̄_i ∈ x̄(S − {i}) ∩ C_{S−{i}}^acc for each i; let x₀ be the unique point of x̄(∅) outside every z̄_i(∅). Then Art_{i,x₀} = Art_i for 2 ≤ i < m, by Theorem 5.10 applied to minimal triples on some T ⊆ S − {i_Cheb, i_char} with |T| = i, using that each b ∈ A_i ⊆ V_{a,2} is constant on T. Also (ΣF′)(x̄) is the sum in (c): Theorems 5.10 and 5.11 on both faces x̄(S − {i_Cheb}) and x̄(S − {i_char}) give (8.30), (8.31), and part (ii) of Theorem 5.10 gives (8.32)–(8.34).
items.note: Uses Theorems 5.10 (minimal triples) and 5.11 (governing triples) from §5. The text 'Equation (8.30, (8.31) and (8.34)' drops a parenthesis. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Verification of properties (b) and (c) in Case II, (8.35)–(8.38)
items.statement: In Case II, Art_{i,x₀} = Art_i for 2 ≤ i < m, by minimal triples on T ⊆ S with |T| = i and i_Cheb ∉ T. Here c_{j₃,j₄} = c_{j₄,j₃} for j₃, j₄ ≤ n_m, c_{j₃,j₄} = 0 when j₃ or j₄ lies in (d_m, n_m], and c_{n_m+1,j₂} = 1. Theorem 5.10 gives Σ_{x∈x̄(∅)} Art_{m,x}(v_l, w_k) = 0 for all l ≠ j₂ and k ≠ j₂ if j₂ ≤ d_m, and for all l and all k ≠ j₂ if j₂ > d_m. Theorem 5.2 gives (8.35) Σ_x Art_{m,x}(R, w_k) = 0 for k ≠ j₂ and (8.36) Σ_x Art_{m,x}(R, w_{j₂}) = φ_{π_{S′}(x̄); −1}(Frob(pr₁(π_{i_Cheb}(x̄)))) + φ_{π_{S′}(x̄); −1}(Frob(pr₂(π_{i_Cheb}(x̄)))). If j₂ ≤ d_m, Theorem 5.6 (m ≥ 3) gives (8.37) Σ_x Art_{m,x}(w_{j₂}, w_{j₂}) = 0 and (8.38) Σ_x (Art_{m,x}(v_l, w_{j₂}) + Art_{m,x}(w_{j₂}, v_l)) = 0 for l ≤ d_m. Hence (c).
items.note: Uses Theorems 5.2 (reflection principle at ∞), 5.6 (self-pairing, s ≥ 2) and 5.10. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Verification of properties (b) and (c) in Case III, (8.39)–(8.43)
items.statement: In Case III, c is symmetric on [d_m]², vanishes outside [d_m]² and on row n_m + 1, and c_{j₂,j₂} = 1. Property (b) follows from Theorem 5.10 applied to the minimal triples for w_k (k ≠ j₂) and for w_{j₂} + R on T ⊆ S − {i_Cheb}. Property (c): Theorem 5.7 gives (8.39) Σ_{x∈x̄(∅)} Art_{m,x}(w_{j₂}, w_{j₂}) = φ_{π_{S′}(x̄); −1}(Frob(pr₁(π_{i_Cheb}(x̄)))) + φ_{π_{S′}(x̄); −1}(Frob(pr₂(π_{i_Cheb}(x̄)))). Theorem 5.6 gives (8.40) Σ_x Art_{m,x}(v_l, v_l) = 0 for l ≤ d_m, l ≠ j₂. Similarly (8.41): Σ_x Art_{m,x}(v_l + w_{j₂}, v_l + w_{j₂}) is the same φ-sum. So (8.42) Σ_x (Art_{m,x}(v_l, w_{j₂}) + Art_{m,x}(w_{j₂}, v_l)) = 0, and (8.43) holds for k, l ≠ j₂ by Theorem 5.10.
items.note: Uses the identity Art(v, w) + Art(w, v) = Art(v, v) + Art(w, w) + Art(v + w, v + w) over 𝔽₂. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Verification of properties (b) and (c) in Case IV
items.statement: In Case IV, c is symmetric on [d_m]², vanishes outside [d_m]², on row n_m + 1 and on the diagonal, and c_{j₁,j₂} = 1. Property (b) is as in Case III. Property (c): Theorem 5.10 for χ(w_{j₂} + v_{j₁} + R) gives Σ_x Art_{m,x}(w_{j₂} + v_{j₁}, w_{j₂} + v_{j₁}) = 0. Theorems 5.6 and 5.7 give Σ_x Art_{m,x}(w_k + v_l, w_k + v_l) = 0 when j₂ ∉ {k, l} and = φ_{π_{S′}(x̄); −1}(Frob(pr₁(π_{i_Cheb}(x̄)))) + φ_{π_{S′}(x̄); −1}(Frob(pr₂(π_{i_Cheb}(x̄)))) otherwise. They also give Σ_x Art_{m,x}(w_k, w_k) = 0 for k ≠ j₂, and the same φ-sum for k = j₂. The polarisation identity then gives (c).
items.note: Checked that the polarisation identity gives the φ-sum exactly for {l, k} = {j₁, j₂}, and 0 for the other pairs. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Top-level Chebotarev equidistribution, (8.44)
items.statement: Gal(M_∘(Z) M(Z) / M_∘(Z)) is central in Gal(M_∘(Z) M(Z) / ℚ) and has order 2^{(M_box−1)^{|S′|}} (Lemmas 6.7 and 6.10). For σ in it, let X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z), σ) := {p ∈ X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z)) : Frob(p) = σ}. Then for i > k_gap, |X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z), σ)| = |X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z))| / 2^{(M_box−1)^{|S′|}} · (1 + O(e^{−k_gap})).
items.note: Proof: [Smith, Prop. 6.5] for L(Q) M_∘(Z) M(Z)/ℚ, with Heilbronn against Siegel zeros. 'Very similar to the proof of [Smith, Prop. 8.5]'. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Q_post, Z̃(Q_post), even distribution over Chebotarev classes, and evenly distributed candidates
items.statement: For Q_post ∈ ∏_{i ∈ [r]−[k_gap], i ≠ i_Cheb} X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z)), Z̃(Q_post) := {x ∈ Z̃ : π_{[r]−[k_gap]−{i_Cheb}}(x) = Q_post}. Q_post is unevenly distributed over the Chebotarev classes if for some σ ∈ Gal(M_∘(Z) M(Z) / M_∘(Z)), ||X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_post, M_∘(Z), σ)| − |X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_post, M_∘(Z))| / 2^{(M_box−1)^{|S′|}}| ≥ |X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_post, M_∘(Z))| / (e^{0.5 k_gap} · 2^{(M_box−1)^{|S′|}}); otherwise it is evenly distributed. An element Q_{j,post} ∈ ∏_{i ∈ [j]−[k_gap], i ≠ i_Cheb} X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z)) is an evenly distributed candidate if two conditions hold. First, when j − 1 > k_gap, π_{[j−1]−[k_gap]}(Q_{j,post}) is an evenly distributed candidate. Second, when j ≠ i_Cheb, |Σ_{p ∈ X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_{j−1,post}, M_∘(Z), σ)} (p / π_j(Q_{j,post}))| ≤ |X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_{j−1,post}, M_∘(Z), σ)| / |X_{k_gap+1}(a, Q, M_∘(Z))|^{1/100} for all σ.
items.note: Uneven Q_post contribute at most |Z| · |X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q, M_∘(Z))| · #{uneven Q_post} (8.45). Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Few uneven Q_post (repeated large sieve)
items.statement: For N₀ large, every evenly distributed candidate Q_post = Q_{r,post} is evenly distributed over the Chebotarev classes, by (8.44). Repeated use of the large sieve ([Smith, Prop. 6.6]) shows that at most ∏_{i ∈ [r]−[k_gap], i ≠ i_Cheb} |X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z))| / |X_{k_gap+1}(a, Q, M_∘(Z))|^{1/100} of the Q_post are not candidates. Hence (8.45) ≤ |Z| · ∏_{i ∈ [r]−[k_gap]} |X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z))| / |X_{k_gap+1}(a, Q, M_∘(Z))|^{1/100} ≤ |X(a, Q) ∩ Z̃| / |X_{k_gap+1}(a, Q, M_∘(Z))|^{1/1000}, where the last step uses Proposition 7.6. So it suffices to prove (8.46) for evenly distributed Q_post.
items.note: This is the same bilinear Legendre-symbol large-sieve input as (7.11), now with Frobenius-class-restricted inner sums; see the SV.2 item. Route: the proposed Part II of ArithmeticStatistics (Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields).

items.name: Final step: Proposition 6.6 on Z × [M_box] and the Chebotarev partition, (8.46)–(8.49)
items.statement: X(a, Q) ∩ Z̃(Q_post) = Z × X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_post, M_∘(Z)). Apply Proposition 6.6 to Z × [M_box], indexed by S, with a = 2^{(n_max+10)(n_max+2m+10)} and ε = (log log log log N)^{−100c/(m 6^m)}. Here ε < a^{−1} and log M_box ≥ A_Comb · 6^{m+1} · log ε^{−1} by the choice of c; let g₀ ∈ Add(Z × [M_box], S) be the function it provides. Primes p₁, …, p_{M_box} give g_{p₁,…,p_{M_box}} ∈ Add(Z × [M_box], S), sending (z̄, (i, j)) to φ(Frob(p_i)) + φ(Frob(p_j)), where φ is φ_{π_{S′−{i_char}}(z̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(z̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(z̄))} in Case I and φ_{z̄; −1} in Cases II–IV. Lemmas 6.9 and 6.10 and even distribution give (8.47): X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_post, M_∘(Z)) = L ∪ ⋃_{i=1}^{t} A_i, with ordered sets A_i of size M_box satisfying g_{p_{i,1},…,p_{i,M_box}} = g₀ and |L| ≤ |X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_post, M_∘(Z))| / e^{0.25 k_gap}. So (8.48) holds on Z × L. By properties (b) and (c), each restriction 𝔄_i of 𝔄 to Z × A_i is (a, S)-acceptable with ΣF′ = g₀ on C(𝔄_i), and Proposition 6.6 gives (8.49): |Σ_{x ∈ X(a, Q, {Art_k}) ∩ Z̃(Q_post) ∩ (Z × A_i)} ι(F(Art_{m,x}))| ≤ ε |Z × A_i|. This proves (8.46) and Theorem 8.13.
