routes.title: Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions, Part II: Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields
routes.brief:
Starts where Arithmetic statistics, counting fields and Selmer distributions (ArithmeticStatistics) stops. ST.3 plans selected class-group distribution theorems and, through PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21, governing fields and 2^k-ranks; nothing in the atlas plans Smith's method for the distribution of 2^∞-class groups. This Part II builds it and proves Stevenhagen's conjecture, following Koymans–Pagano, 'On Stevenhagen's conjecture' (arXiv 2201.13424v1; to appear in Acta Mathematica).

Final theorem, as the paper states it. Let 𝒟 be the set of squarefree integers d > 0 such that every prime p | d satisfies p ≡ 1, 2 mod 4, 𝒟⁻ the set of squarefree d for which x² − dy² = −1 is soluble in integers, and 𝒟(X), 𝒟⁻(X) the elements with d < X. Theorem 1.1: lim_{X→∞} |𝒟⁻(X)|/|𝒟(X)| = 1 − α, α = ∏_{j odd}(1 − 2^{−j}) ≈ 0.41942. (The paper notes that the same method gives the distribution of 2Cl(ℚ(√d))[2^∞] on 𝒟 and an effective error term, without proving them.)

Layers. (1) Algebraic foundations (§2): raw cocycles for multiquadratic extensions, expansion maps and their existence criteria (§§2.1–2.2), and the higher Artin pairings Art_{k,ℚ(√d)} on the 2-power torsion of the narrow class group (§2.3). (2) Higher Rédei reciprocity (§3, Theorem 3.2), whose first case is Rédei's reciprocity law. (3) Reflection principles (§§4–5): profitable triples, the reflection principles for the place ∞ and for the self-pairing (the trivial spin symbol, via Massey symbols and Hilbert reciprocity), and the standard reflection principles on product spaces one dimension smaller than Smith's. (4) Combinatorics (§6): additive systems, the Ramsey lemma for product sets in dense subsets, and the Galois groups of the governing fields. (5) Equidistribution of the first Artin pairing (§7): prime-divisor statistics on 𝒟, preboxes and Legendre symbols, boxes, with the effective Chebotarev theorem and Heath-Brown's large sieve. (6) The endgame (§8): boxes, genericity, the second-moment computation and the Markov-chain limit P_Sym for symmetric matrices over 𝔽₂. Tests: the first case of Theorem 3.2 against Rédei's reciprocity law; the 4-rank distribution on 𝒟 proved by Fouvry–Klüners.

Import, never re-plan: ArithmeticStatistics ST.0 (families), ST.3 (class-group distributions, governing fields, 2^k-ranks) and ST.5 (random-matrix models); ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.1 (quadratic reciprocity, Hilbert symbols) and CA.4 (Pell equations); AnalyticNumberTheory AN.2, AN.4 and AN.5 (exceptional zeros, effective Chebotarev, Selberg–Delange); SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.2 (large sieve; Heath-Brown's quadratic large sieve routed there); ProbabilisticAndMetricNumberTheory PM.1; InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.4 (embedding problems for 2-groups); ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.* (Galois cohomology); the Tau Ceti roadmaps ClassFieldTheory, Chebotarev, GlobalNumberFields, Multiquadratic (genus theory), ProfiniteCohomology, ProfiniteProPGroups and QuadraticFormInvariants. Prerequisite papers: Smith, '2^∞-Selmer groups, 2^∞-class groups, and Goldfeld's conjecture' (arXiv 1702.02325) and 'Governing fields and statistics for 4-Selmer groups and 8-class groups' (arXiv 1607.07860); Koymans–Pagano, 'Higher genus theory' (IMRN) and 'Higher Rédei reciprocity and integral points on conics' (arXiv 2005.14157); Fouvry–Klüners, 'On the negative Pell equation' (Ann. of Math. 2010); Friedlander–Iwaniec–Mazur–Rubin, 'The spin of prime ideals' (Invent. Math. 2013); Heath-Brown's quadratic large sieve (Acta Arith. 1995).
routes.reason: ArithmeticStatistics owns class-group distributions, and ST.3 already carries governing fields and 2^k-ranks, but no stage plans the method this proof rests on. A search of every stage for Rédei, governing fields, reflection principles, additive systems, raw cocycles, expansion maps and Artin pairings finds nothing relevant. Smith's method is a coherent body of new layers in ArithmeticStatistics' direction (algebraic foundations, reciprocity, reflection principles, combinatorics, equidistribution and the endgame), about two hundred items, so it is a Part II rather than a source of ST.3, which the Part II imports.

CA.4 plans Pell equations, 'classified through units with positivity conventions'. The negative Pell equation belongs there: the set 𝒟⁻, rational solubility through Hasse–Minkowski, Dirichlet's theorem that primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 are in 𝒟⁻, and the reformulations through the narrow class group ((√d) narrowly trivial; the 2-parts of the narrow and ordinary class groups agree) and the Galois-module structure of the units.

ST.0 plans arithmetic families with local conditions, and 𝒟 is one. ST.3 plans class-group distribution theorems, and the prior bounds towards Stevenhagen's conjecture (Fouvry–Klüners, CKMP, the authors' KP3) and the sets D_{2,n} belong there. ST.5 plans random-matrix distributions: MacWilliams' count of symmetric matrices over 𝔽₂, the limit P_Sym and the KP3 rank identity.

AN.2 plans prime number theorems with possible exceptional zeros labelled; the paper needs the prime number theorem for quadratic characters uniform in the conductor, Landau's repulsion of exceptional zeros and the effective lower bound for an exceptional zero. AN.4 plans Chebotarev and Dedekind zeta functions; the paper needs the effective Chebotarev theorem with exceptional-zero control (Smith, Prop. 6.5) and Heilbronn's theorem on real zeros. AN.5 plans mean values of multiplicative functions; the paper needs the asymptotic for |𝒟(X)| and Sathe–Selberg bounds for 𝒟 with a prescribed number of prime factors.

SV.2 plans the multiplicative large sieve and bilinear sums. The bilinear Legendre-symbol estimate the paper uses (Smith, Prop. 6.6) comes from Heath-Brown's large sieve for quadratic characters, a sharper member of that family that SV.2 does not yet name.
PM.1 plans Turán–Kubilius and Erdős–Kac. Theorem 7.2(a), that few d ∈ 𝒟(N) have ω(d) far from ½ log log N, is their restriction to 𝒟.

sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 2.18. Let a ∈ 𝒟 be greater than 1. Then the extension L(φ_{a;a}(𝔊))/ℚ is a ℤ/4ℤ-extension of ℚ ramifying exactly at those places where ℚ(√a)/ℚ ramifies. Furthermore, the ramification index of such places equals 4.
